News.title: Andy Burnham vows no general election before 2029 and insists ‘people don’t want it’ despite questions over mandate
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has vowed there will be no general election before 2029 despite burning questions about his mandate.

The new PM insisted that “people don’t want” another vote despite him taking the top job unopposed in what critics described as a “coup”.

In his first major interview as PM, Burnham categorically ruled out an early general election when speaking to the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg.



Burnham took over No10 from Keir Starmer a little over a month after returning to Westminister as an MP – and has now vowed to unleash the “biggest change in decades” on the UK.



But despite this, he insists he will stick by Labour’s manifesto and says he is protected by the mandate Labour won in 2024.

He said: “I’m going to rule it out… I don’t think people want it.

“Opinion polls might say some people do, some people don’t.



“We’re in a parliamentary democracy… People voted for a manifesto and I will honour that manifesto.”

Opposition figures – including Reform leader Nigel Farage – have urged the new PM to call an election, which he legally does not have to do until August 2029.

Elsewhere in the interview, Burnham said: “I have faced the public in Makerfield – I went out on those doorsteps.

“I’ve got the support of colleagues in parliament [and] there’s no early general election.



He added: “But the thing is I just think what I most need to do is get Britain focused on getting the country back where it should be, getting it working.”

This comes as Burnham said he will put the UK’s interests first in his dealings with Donald Trump – even if it means disagreeing with the US president.

The pair spoke over the phone on Monday, within an hour of Burnham arriving in Downing Street.

After the call, Trump stated in a post on Truth Social that Burnham “has got a big job ahead of him, but he will be able to do it” and pledged that the US “will be there to help”.

Downing Street described the 20-minute conversation as “extremely warm”.



But speaking with the BBC, Burnham said: “I can’t at any point say that I won’t take a different opinion from him [Donald Trump], that I will need to voice a different idea that is right for Britain.”

He added he would publicly disagree with the president if he deemed necessary.

Burnham added: “You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That’s what you’re required to do if you’re to do this job properly.”

Ex-PM Sir Keir Starmer’s relationship with Washington became increasingly fractious over the Iran conflict.

Burnham said he was “very aware” of Chancellor John Healey’s position and resignation as Starmer’s defence secretary following disagreements over the issue.



He said: “The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded and that’s the thing that’s right in front of us and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year.”

Elsewhere, new Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he shared “very warm conversation” with his US counterpart Pete Hegseth.

The pair are thought to have brainstormed ideas for an international conference which allies of the UK and US would attend, but have not yet firmed up the details of a summit.

A source close to Streeting last week said: “The Defence Secretary had a very warm conversation with Secretary Hegseth.

“They discussed the situation in the Strait of Hormuz and how allies can work together.



“They also discussed defence investment and the UK’s commitment to meeting our Nato commitments.”

News.title: Moment disqualified driver rammed by 3 cop cars before window is smashed with baton after driving wrong way on A-road
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a disqualified driver is rammed by three police cars before they smash his window with a baton.

In the video, the cops have to act quickly after Wayne Sykes starts driving the wrong way down an A-road.



He is rounding the roundabout when his car suddenly mounts a grass verge and drives into oncoming traffic exiting the A46 in Nottinghamshire.

The officers then hit the back of the Vauxhall Insignia causing it to spin round.



When Sykes, 42, tries to reverse away but two more police cars box him in.

One officer then smashes his car window with a baton before Sykes is arrested.

The cops were already searching for the wanted man when they started following him near East Bridgford on June 11.

He appeared at Nottingham Crown Court on June 12 and pleaded guilty to dangerous driving, driving without insurance and driving whilst disqualified.



He was then jailed for 32 months on July 17 and handed an extended driving ban.

Sergeant Craig Luckett, of the Roads Policing Unit, said: “Whenever we begin a pursuit on the roads, public safety is always our number one priority.

“So, when this individual went to enter a busy dual carriageway in the wrong direction we had no choice but to take immediate action to bring the pursuit to a safe resolution, it doesn’t bear thinking about the carnage which could have ensued had my officers not taken direct action.

“Thanks to the quick thinking, professionalism and courage of all involved this man was swiftly detained and the public protected from harm.”

A spokesperson for the force said: “A dangerous and disqualified driver was rammed by a police car after he tried to drive the wrong way along the A46.



“Officers were searching for the wanted man Wayne Sykes when they began following him near East Bridgford on Thursday 11 June.

“Sykes, a disqualified driver who failed to appear in court earlier in the week for driving related offences, then failed to stop as he drove towards the village of Newton.

“As he rounded the roundabout at the junction of Bridgford Street, Skyes forced the pursuing officers into immediate action by mounting a grass verge and drove the wrong way towards oncoming traffic exiting the A46.



“Fearing for public safety, the pursuing officers immediately made tactical contact with the rear side of Sykes’ Vauxhall Insignia, sending it spinning around.

“As Sykes then tried to reverse away, two other police vehicles completed a containment manoeuvre to box the vehicle in.”

News.title: Iran’s new supreme leader ‘more driven than ever’ to create nuclear bomb after Trump’s strikes, US intelligence fears
News.content:
IRAN’S new Ayatollah is even more determined to develop a nuclear bomb than his late father, Washington fears.

Fresh US intelligence suggests the killing of the former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in February has led to the intensification of Tehran’s nuclear ambitions.



The Iranian program could bolster President Donald Trump’s case for actioning further strikes in the region.

For years, Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei’s 2003 religious ban on weapons of mass destruction tempered global concern regarding Iran’s nuclear programme.



Now, following the recent US-strikes in the area, officials believe Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei takes a more favourable approach to nuclear armament.

While Mojtaba has never publicly called for use of nuclear bombs, intelligence assessments reportedly show he has fewer ideological qualms about weaponization and may back a more advanced arsenal, according to The New York Times.

For quite some time, Tehran quietly expanded its nuclear infrastructure and preserved the option to build a weapon if it choses under the late Ayatollah’s regime.

And while they may have had the capabilities, the development of a nuclear bomb seemed uncertain.



If confirmed, evidence of Mojtaba’s nuclear ambitions could reinforce the rationale for future US military action.

For now, Iran has not restarted enrichment or resumed weapons work since last year’s US airstrikes, which inflicted major damage.

Instead, Tehran appears focused on salvaging what remains – including the heavily fortified underground complex known as Pickaxe Mountain.



Officials say Iran has moved some centrifuges, used to enrich uranium, into the deep underground facility.

The centre is believed to lie beyond the reach of America’s most powerful bunker-busters.

Tehran has poured extra ground forces around the site, amid fears the US could attempt a sudden raid rather than rely on airstrikes alone.

In June, the US hammered Iran’s Fordow nuke plant with stealth bombers during an overnight mission.

The strike was executed for the purpose of inflicting major damage to Iran’s nuclear programme.



B-2 stealth bombers dropped massive bunker-busters on Fordo and Natanz, while Tomahawk missiles hit Isfahan.

Officials revealed that about 75 precision-guided weapons were unleashed in total.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said: “Our B-2s went in and out and back without the world knowing at all.”

Intelligence on Mojtaba Khamenei’s intentions comes with heavy caveats, with much of it predicating the current fighting.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mojtaba is thought to favour sophisticated warheads small enough to sit atop long-range missiles.



Ali Khamenei’s fatwa banning nuclear weapons never stopped Iran mastering the technology to build one, and hardliners long argued Tehran should be able to assemble a bomb at speed if it had to.

News.title: Fury as benefit cheats handed £4.3million of your money every week while swapping UK for sun loungers abroad
News.content:
BENEFIT fraudsters are getting £4.3million in taxpayer-funded handouts a week while swapping Britain for sun loungers abroad.

Sun on Sunday analysis shows hard-working families are unknowingly bankrolling scroungers pretending they are still living in Britain.



The fraud means claimants stay on fully funded British benefits despite living in foreign destinations, including sun-soaked holiday resorts.

The Department for Work and Pensions’ estimated figures reveal £226million was lost in the year to March because of abroad fraud.



Of the total fraud, £103million is from bogus Universal Credit claims, £67million from dodgy expats on Pension Credit, £29million of Housing Benefit claims, and £27million wrongly received for Personal Independence Payments.

Around 2,000 are also legally claiming PIP despite living abroad full-time under treaty deals with European Economic Area nations.



Benefit claimants are legally required to inform the DWP if they intend to leave the UK for an extended period.

Brits can stay on full benefits like PIP for up to 13 weeks at a time while out of the country.

However, being away any longer means claimants have an obligation to inform the DWP, with their payments paused until their return.

New PM Andy Burnham was last night urged to crack down on the fraud.



Former Tory leader Sir Iain Duncan Smith said: “This could be cut down if the DWP brought back face-to-face meetings. People on benefits like Universal Credit should be looking for work.”

A DWP spokesman said: “We’re determined to crack down on fraud. Our latest figures show us fraud and error has fallen by a quarter since its 2022 peak. We will leave no stone unturned.”

News.title: Beast who plotted to murder Holly Willoughby deemed ‘too dangerous’ to be released from prison to attend mum’s funeral
News.content:
THE stalker who plotted to murder Holly Willoughby has been deemed too dangerous to attend his mum’s funeral.

Gavin Plumb, 39, is unlikely to have his request to be released from prison for a few hours in order to say goodbye to his mum Carol, 64, granted.



Plumb is currently two years into his 15 years sentence for his plot to kidnap and kill the TV star – and is said to be devastated following his mum’s death from cancer earlier this year.

He was hoping to have a few hours away from high-security Long Lartin prison in Worcestershire for the service, the Daily Star reports.



One source said: “Plumb is a broken man. His mum used to visit and call quite often.

“He has asked for permission to attend her funeral. It is unlikely to be given because he is regarded as a real security threat.”

They added that should circumstances change, he could attend handcuffed and accompanied by prison guards, but still won’t be allowed at any family gathering at a private house.

Plumb will need his request approved by the governor and cleared by the prison service.



The source also noted the high chance of a large media presence should the former Essex security guard attend the service.

Typically, prisoners are allowed to go to the funerals of close family members and friends.

Earlier this month, prison officers found a stash of photos of Holly under a mattress in Plumb’s jail cell.

A source said: “Plumb is still obsessed with Holly. The pictures were taken from magazines. He should not have been allowed access to images of her.”

They added that Plumb has also struck up a grim friendship in the high-security jail with fellow lag Suffolk Strangler Steve Wright, who is serving life for murdering six women.



The source said: “Plumb is still completely obsessed and completely remorseless.

“He was asked about his crimes once and he replied, ‘Who wouldn’t want to kidnap Holly and rape her?’ He was really smug about it.”

Plumb was jailed in July 2024 for soliciting Holly’s murder, kidnap, and the commission of rape, had his cell searched when his disturbing behaviour raised suspicions.



His plan was thwarted by an undercover US officer online thousands of miles away in Minnesota.

The officer posed as another kidnap enthusiast while Plumb outlined how they would attack Holly and her husband, TV producer Dan Baldwin.

The US officer printed a fake plane ticket to convince Plumb he was travelling to the UK and got his address — then alerted the FBI, which contacted Scotland Yard.

Essex Police, — fearing an imminent threat to Holly, arrested Plumb at his home in Harlow on the day they were warned about him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They found a kidnap kit including handcuffs, 400 heavy-duty cable ties and chloroform plus more than 10,000 photos of Holly inside Plumb’s flat.



For the plot against Holly, 45, he got a minimum of 15 years and 85 days at Chelmsford crown court in 2024.

News.title: Man, 25, ‘fighting for life’ after being stabbed in head with screwdriver & undergoing op to remove ‘half his skull’
News.content:
HORRIFIC 'ATTACK' Man, 25, ‘fighting for life’ after being stabbed in head with screwdriver & undergoing op to remove ‘half his skull’

A MAN is “fighting for his life” after being stabbed in the head with a screwdriver.

Jamie Chappell, 25, was rushed to hospital following the horror incident on Thursday in Purton, Wiltshire, where he underwent a five-hour operation to remove “half his skull”.



James Denys, 36, has been charged with grievous bodily harm in what police call a “serious assault”.

A spokesperson for the Chappell family told Swindon Advertiser: “Jamie is one of the kindest, most gentle souls you could ever meet.



“He left for work on the morning of Thursday 23rd July like any other day, never imagining that within hours he would be fighting for his life.

“Today Jamie remains critically ill. Every hour is a battle and our family continues to live with the uncertainty, fear and heartbreak that no family should ever have to endure.”



Emergency services rushed to the Widham Gardens building site where Chappell was stabbed in the head on July 23.

He was taken to Southmead Hospital where staff tried to save his life in what his family called an “unimaginably difficult time”.

The attack was originally being treated as a suspected murder attempt.

Denys, of Ravensdale, East Wichel, appeared in court and was charged with assault causing grievous bodily harm.



He has been remanded in custody and will appear at Swindon Magistrates Court on Saturday.

A second suspect, also 36, was arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender but has since been released on bail.

Detective Chief Inspector Deb Hatch described the event as a “serious incident” and extended her thoughts to the victim’s family.

She has urged any witnesses or concerned individuals to speak to the police and help in its investigation.

Information can be provided by calling 101 or anonymously through Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: MPs blast nanny state officials telling Brits not to eat raw meat at their summer BBQs
News.content:
MPs have blasted nanny state officials after they issued guidelines telling Brits not to eat raw meat at their summer BBQs.

The Government has shared advice online telling people not to be “a tool” and ‘“don’t let your food sunbathe”.



Recommendations from the Food Standards Agency [FSA] issued earlier this month include taking the “jeopardy out of your jerk chicken”.

Alex Burghart, Shadow Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, said Brits can manage their own BBQs perfectly well this summer.



He added: “Families have been flipping burgers on their patios and porches for generations.

“Labour cannot fill a pothole or stop the boats, yet somehow find the time, and the taxpayers’ money, to cook up coleslaw guidance. It’s Labour that deserves a grilling after this nonsense.”



The FSA guidance tells people not to take the “it looks done” gamble, adding: “The outside can look done while the inside remains raw.

“Take the jeopardy out of your jerk chicken by always cooking meat all the way through.”

They also tell people to “take the peril out of your poultry” by keeping raw meat away from cooked food.

And warn against the “sunny side risk”, adding: “Don’t let your food sunbathe as bacteria can multiply quickly when it gets hotter.”



It is part of a campaign called “Stop. Think. Serve” to encourage people to be careful with their everyday kitchen habits.

Rebecca Sudworth, Director of Policy at the Food Standards Agency, said: “We know that food poisoning cases rise during the summer months, and BBQs and picnics can create the conditions where bacteria thrive if food isn’t handled carefully.”

News.title: Manhunt for ‘Islamist’ after van rams into Berlin Pride crowd & driver stabs revellers leaving 1 dead & 16 injured
News.content:
POLICE have launched an urgent manhunt for an “Islamist” suspect after a van rammed into a crowd at a Pride parade in Berlin.

At least one person has died and 16 injured after the driver ploughed into revellers before knifing people at random.



Police have named the suspect as “armed and dangerous” Abdul B., a 21-year-old man with a “slim build” and black hair.

Cops in the German capital said: “One or more people are believed to have subsequently fled the vehicle.





“Furthermore, several people are reported to have been injured with stabbing weapons.”

Witnesses said the white van drove into crowds in Berlin’s Tiergarten park at high speed at about 10pm local time on Saturday night.

The suspect then crashed into a tree and abandoned the vehicle, before using a bladed weapon to attack people in the park near the end of the parade route.

Witnesses told emergency services that people with stab wounds were lying on the ground.



Cops have now launched a major manhunt for the driver, who is said to have fled on foot.

He has been identified as a member of the city’s “Islamist scene” and is known to cops but he has not yet been arrested, a spokesman for Berlin police said on Sunday.



Crowds had filled the streets for Berlin’s annual Christopher Street Day (CSD) Pride event.

Berlin police said: “Shortly before 10pm, the driver of a white vehicle is said to have struck several people.

“There are numerous injured, including several with life-threatening injuries.”

Eight people have suffered serious injuries, three of whom are fighting for their lives.



A helicopter landing pad was set up in front of the Reichstag, the seat of Germany’s Parliament.



The Pride event was cancelled, with the word “evacuation” displayed on a huge screen at the Brandenburg Gate.

Hundreds of thousands of people had flocked to Berlin to join one of Europe’s largest LGBTQ+ celebrations.

Berlin cops said: “We believe that a vehicle entered the Tiergarten park and hit several people and injured them.”

Police cordoned off the area as they searched for the suspected attacker.

Choppers have been deployed to search for “one or more suspects”.



Berlin Mayor Kai Wegner called the incident “an attack on our free and open society”.

He wrote: “After a peaceful and colorful CSD, the assembly for a tolerant and peaceful Berlin was attacked in the most brutal way.

“Berlin is the city of freedom – and our freedom has been attacked in the most horrific way today.

“My thoughts are with the victims, their families and friends. I thank the emergency services who were immediately on site and did everything in their power.

“And I trust the police and security authorities, who will investigate at full speed.”



German Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed he would “push to make sure this heinous act is fully investigated and punished”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Berlin’s Queer Liaison Officer Alfonso Pantisano told Tagesspiegel: “This is a day of great mourning for the queer community.

“They must not allow themselves to be intimidated, especially now.”

News.title: Berlin Pride crash: Police name Abdul B, 21, as suspect after van drives into crowd killing 1
News.content:
Police in Berlin say a major manhunt is underway after a white minivan ploughed into a crowd of people in the Tiergarten park around 10pm on Saturday night

Berlin Pride crash: Police name Abdul B, 21, as suspect after van drives into crowd killing 1

One person has died and 16 more have been injured after a v ehicle drove into the crowd during a Pride event in Berlin, with the suspect fleeing the scene.

At around 10pm on Saturday night, a white minivan drove at speed into a group of people in the city centre's Tiergarten park during the annual Pride event, also known as Christopher Street Day,

Witnesses said they saw a car driving "very quickly" into the crowd and heard screams as people ran. Police spokesman Florian Nath told reporters that witnesses also reported people lying on the ground with stab wounds.

Berlin Pride was cancelled with attendees told to “evacuate" immediately.

Police have named the suspect as 21-year-old Abdul B, who is "associated with the Islamist scene," and a major manhunt is underway for him.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed to "make sure this horrific act is fully investigated and punished".

News.title: Andy Burnham vows to stand up to Donald Trump 'if it's right for Britain'
News.content:
Andy Burnham vows to stand up to Donald Trump 'if it's right for Britain'

In an interview with the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, the Prime Minister said he is prepared to disagree with Donald Trump publicly - and said he would not be calling a snap general election

View 2 Images Andy Burnham has said he will stand up to Donald Trump when needed (Image: BBC)

Andy Burnham has said he is prepared to clash with Donald Trump if it is in Britain's national interest.

‌



The Prime Minister, who has also reiterated that he will not call a snap general election, said he would publicly disagree with the US President if necessary. His predecessor, Keir Starmer, had a difficult relationship with Trump, who repeatedly criticised him over his refusal to allow the US to launch aggressive strikes on Iran from British bases.

‌



In an interview with the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, Mr Burnham said: "I can't at any point say that I won't take a different opinion from him [Donald Trump], that I will need to voice a different idea that is right for Britain." And he continued: "You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly."

‌



The two leaders spoke for the first time on Monday in conversation Downing Street described as "extremely warm". Trump later posted on social media that Mr Burnham "has got a big job ahead of him, but he will be able to do it" - and said the US "will be there to help".

Inside No10 North as Andy Burnham sets up his new power base READ MORE :

View 2 Images Donald Trump was a thorn in Keir Starmer's side at times (Image: Andrew Harnik, Getty Images)

In a wide-ranging interview, to be broadcast this morning, the Prime Minister also ruled out calling a snap election. He told Ms Kuenssberg: "I'm going to rule it out... I don't think people want it."

‌



He went on: "I just think what I most need to do is get Britain focused on getting the country back where it should be, getting it working."

The PM also declined to give a timetable for getting defence spending to 3% of the UK's GDP. Mr Burnham said he was very aware of Chancellor John Healey's position, having resigned as Defence Secretary from Mr Starmer's government in disagreement on the issue.

Mr Burnham said: "The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded and that's the thing that's right in front of us and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year."

‌



The new Prime Minister took office on Monday, and has made a string of announcements on the cost of living and supporting pubs and live music venues. These include announcing VAT was being scrapped on household electricity bills, and the return of a £2 bus fare cap outside London.

And pubs will benefit from a 20% business rate cut, Downing Street said - saving the average boozer more than £1,000 a year.

In a pledge to go further, the former Greater Manchester Mayor claimed he was used to being told things can’t be done, and that the era of Government’s giving up trying to solve the issues impacting people was over.

‌



Writing for the Sunday Mirror, Mr Burnham claimed this week had shown how politicians could make lives a “little bit easier”, but that his job won’t be done until people aren’t just living, but “living well".

He said: "Life doesn’t always go to plan. But whether someone gets the chance to get back on their feet says something about who we are. It says something about the country we’re trying to build.

“I want Britain to be a country where nobody is written off. Where everyone is treated with respect no matter who they are or what they’ve been through. And where the government doesn’t avoid a problem because it’s difficult, but rolls up its sleeves and gets to work.

Article continues below

“I want people to stop worrying and start feeling hopeful about what’s coming next. I want them to start to believe in Britain again. But I can't ask people to dream about the future when they’re struggling to make life work.

"Of course, there will still be those who say it can’t be done. But we proved them wrong in Manchester. And we’re going to prove them wrong again on a bigger scale. We are going to get Britain believing again - and bring back hope."

News.title: Harry and Meghan's strict test before any Balmoral reunion as royals 'let guard down'
News.content:
Harry and Meghan's strict test before any Balmoral reunion as royals 'let guard down'

EXCLUSIVE: In the coming weeks, the royals are expected to head to Balmoral for their annual summer holiday - but two royals noticeably absent from visiting recently are Prince Harry and Meghan

View 4 Images Prince Harry and Meghan have not been recent visitors to Balmoral (Image: Getty Images)

Its stunning surroundings of rolling green hills and beautiful moors have seen it dubbed the ‘most beautiful place on earth’.

‌



And with the summer holidays now in full swing, the Royal Family is expected to be gearing up to head to Balmoral over the next few weeks in their time-honoured tradition.

‌



Like his mother before him, the King spends part of August and September on the 50,000-acre Scottish Highlands estate, welcoming various relatives for a short stay while he is in residence. But two royals who have not enjoyed a stay in Aberdeenshire for many years are Prince Harry and wife Meghan.

‌



Oprah Winfrey defends infamous question in Harry and Meghan tell-all chat READ MORE :

Why Prince William and Kate are rewriting history and giving George the childhood his dad never had READ MORE :

View 4 Images Prince Harry and Meghan with their children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet (Image: @meghan/Instagram)

Since dramatically quitting their royal roles over six years ago and as their feud with their royal relatives deepened, neither they nor their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, have spent any time at the Scottish retreat.

However, in a glimmer of hope of potential royal reconciliation, last month, the King was reunited with his grandchildren after the Duke and Duchess of Sussex visited him at his country home of Highgrove.

‌



It was the first time in four years that Charles had seen his grandchildren in person and has been interpreted by many as a sign of the thawing of the relationship between the King and his youngest son.

So with relations appearing to head in the right direction, could a Balmoral trip for Harry, Meghan and their children be in the offing for a family reunion? Royal expert Jennie Bond is not so sure.

View 4 Images Prince Harry as a youngster at Balmoral with his father and older brother (Image: Getty)

‌



The former BBC royal correspondent told the Mirror: “I think it’s still a question of baby steps as far as the reconciliation between the King and the Sussexes goes.

“Everyone is still waiting to see whether the privacy of the recent reunion at Highgrove will be honoured. So far, so good – no leaked details, no rumours of any photos being made public. And it needs to remain that way.

“But I certainly can’t see Harry and Meghan being invited to Balmoral when William and his family are there. Other family members would clearly have to be asked if they wanted to be there at the same time.

‌



“The castle is almost a sacred place for the royal family. It is where the late Queen was happiest and where she died. It is the place where the family feels truly off-duty and relaxed. They can put their guard down, and they would have to feel that was still the case if Harry and Meghan were there.”

View 4 Images King Charles taking up residence in Balmoral in the summer of 2024 (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

Sources close to Harry have previously said he is keen to introduce his young children to his homeland to allow them to learn and experience their heritage.

‌



In photos on Instagram by Meghan, it shows on their recent family visit to the UK, they also visited Althorp, the Spencer family estate, where the prince's late mother, Princess Diana is buried.

For Harry, spending summers at Balmoral was a yearly tradition, where he would join his extended family for long walks, games, horse rides, fishing trips and picnics.

And Jennie added: “Harry himself has written about how special Balmoral is. In his book, Spare, he recalled how happy he was: ‘To me, Balmoral was always simply paradise. A cross between Disney World and some sacred Druid grove’.

‌



“So I’m absolutely sure he wants to show his children what it’s like one day – and it is an entirely different world to the one they know in California.”

And even though the royal expert says a trip to the Scottish Highlands for the Sussexes this year might not be forthcoming, she believes there is potential for this to change in the future.

Article continues below

Jennie explained: “I think it’s unlikely that we will see Harry and his family at Balmoral this year. But if the baby steps keep on coming, Harry might get his wish to show his children the wonders of this magical Scottish castle.”

News.title: Prince William's 'dear' friendship with Tom Cruise sparked by two shared passions
News.content:
Prince William's 'dear' friendship with Tom Cruise sparked by two shared passions

The Prince and Princess of Wales have been snapped with Hollywood actor Tom Cruise on a number of occasions, and William and Tom are said to have developed 'quite a friendship' over a shared love

View 3 Images The Prince of Wales with award-winning actor Tom Cruise

With one acting royalty and the other actual royalty, it's no surprise that Tom Cruise has struck up "quite a friendship" with Prince William. The Prince and Princess of Wales have been snapped with the A-list actor on multiple occasions, but one royal expert believed their relationship goes beyond what cameras have captured in recent years.

‌



In 2022, Cruise mixed with the royal couple at the premiere of his film Top Gun: Maverick as they made their way down the red carpet. Further images show the actor grasping Kate's hand, while also sharing a joke with the future King and Queen.

‌



Duchess of Kent leaves £1.4 million fortune to children and charities READ MORE :

View 3 Images The Prince and Princess of Wales with Tom Cruise at the Top Gun: Maverick premiere

‌



In February 2024, Tom and William were spotted laughing together once more, and posing for photographs at London's Air Ambulance Charity Gala Dinner. And according to the Daily Mail's Richard Eden, the duo have "developed quite a friendship over the years" thanks to their mutual passion for aviation.

Tom - who was seen at the World Cup final last week - once said of his bond with the heir to throne: "We have a lot in common. We both love England and we're both aviators, we both love flying."

William and Tom's joint appearance at the London Air Ambulance Charity Gala came just weeks after the King's shock cancer diagnosis back in February 2024.

‌



Buckingham Palace announced that Charles had an undisclosed form of cancer - and just weeks after this news became public, Kate also revealed that she too was undergoing cancer treatment.

View 3 Images Prince William with Tom Cruise have developed an unlikely friendship over the years (Image: Getty Images)

Addressing the assembled guests at the event, the Prince of Wales said: "I'd like to take this opportunity to say thank you, also, for the kind messages of support for Catherine and for my father, especially in recent days. It means a great deal to us all.

‌



"It's fair to say the past few weeks have had a rather medical focus. So I thought I'd come to an air ambulance function to get away from it all!".

William then took aim at Tom with a light-hearted jibe, referencing the Hollywood star's legendary high-octane film stunts. He said: "Here in London, the current aircraft have served magnificently. But our capital city needs a new fleet."

He continued: "And we are up against time. The clue really is in the Appeal's name. By September, we need the two new red birds - decked with the latest kit such as night vision - in our skies. I should also take this opportunity to give a mention to my - our - fellow pilot, Tom Cruise. Tom, huge thanks for supporting us tonight."

‌



Meanwhile, just last year, Tom also lent his support to another of William's passion projects - the Earthshot Prize - and he sent a surprise video message that was played during the awards ceremony in Rio de Janeiro, where he dubbed the prince a "dear friend".

Tom's connections with the Royal Family stretch back to the early 1990s. Photographs from that era capture him meeting William's now late mother Princess Diana, and subsequently attending her funeral in 1997.

Article continues below

In 2017, he was also pictured in conversation with Prince Philip, who passed away in 2021, at the 75th anniversary of the Outward Bound Trust at Buckingham Palace.

News.title: HMRC issues alert for one group - it's 'free, easy and essential'
News.content:
HMRC issues alert for one group - it's 'free, easy and essential'

The tax authority says it could avoid a lot of problems later

View 2 Images Consumer experts have long advised first-time workers to check their tax code (Image: Dougal Waters via Getty Images)

Thousands of people stepping into the workforce have been urged to take one simple step that could help them avoid tax problems from day one.

‌



HMRC has issued an "essential" alert encouraging those leaving university and entering the workplace to download its free app. It says it is vital help when it comes to managing everything from their National Insurance number to checking they are paying the right amount of tax. In a social media post aimed at students planning life after university, the tax authority said: "Planning for life after uni?

‌



"Start right with the HMRC app. From finding your National Insurance number to checking your employment history, it's free, easy, and essential for your next step."

‌



View 2 Images Features include claiming tax refunds and making Self-Assessment payments (Image: O2O Creative via Getty Images)

For many graduates, the weeks before starting work are the first time they will need to deal directly with the tax system, making it important to ensure employers have the correct details to avoid emergency tax codes or payroll delays.

The app allows users to instantly view their National Insurance number - a detail many young workers discover they need when completing employment paperwork. It also lets employees check their tax code, monitor their income, see how much tax has been deducted and review their employment history over the previous five years.

‌



The service can also help graduates estimate their take-home pay after Income Tax and National Insurance deductions before receiving their first payslip.

As careers develop, the app can also be used to track Child Benefit, check State Pension forecasts, view gaps in National Insurance contributions and manage Self Assessment if someone later becomes self-employed or has additional income.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Article continues below

Other features include claiming tax refunds, making Self-Assessment payments, updating personal details such as a change of address and tracking correspondence sent to HMRC. The app also enables users to store their National Insurance number in their digital wallet, making it easier to access when changing jobs.

After downloading the app, users sign in using their existing HMRC online account or create one if they do not already have one. They can then access it using a six-digit PIN, fingerprint or facial recognition. The reminder comes as thousands of university leavers prepare to enter the jobs market over the summer, with many starting graduate schemes, apprenticeships and permanent roles in the coming weeks.

Consumer experts have long advised first-time workers to check their tax code shortly after receiving their first payslip, as incorrect tax codes can leave employees paying too much tax or facing an unexpected bill later. Anyone who believes they have overpaid tax can also use the HMRC app to check whether they are due a refund and, in many cases, claim it directly through the service. More details here.

News.title: Everyone who qualifies for £332.10 free NHS dental treatment as 212,143 fined
News.content:
Everyone who qualifies for £332.10 free NHS dental treatment as 212,143 fined

New figures show people are risking a fine of up to £100 by incorrectly claiming they are entitled to free dental care

View 3 Images Many people have to pay for their treatment (Image: Getty)

People are being warned to check their eligibility for free dental treatment after a sharp rise in the number of fines issued for incorrect claims. Figures from the NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) through a Freedom of Information request showed more than 200,000 penalty charge notices were issued in relation to dental treatment in 2025.

‌



This was up more than 40 per cent from two years previously. Free or partially free treatment is available for people in receipt of certain benefits but some say the rules are confusing, causing many to incorrectly believe they are entitled to help.

‌



Dr Andrej Bozic, an oral surgeon at private clinic Dentum, says people should know their entitlement before they visit the dentist - or risk a fine of up to £100. He said: “If you are entitled to free NHS dental treatment you will be asked to show proof of eligibility and sign a document. It’s so important that you are clear on what you are and aren’t entitled to because incorrect claims, even if they are made by mistake, can result in fines of £100.”

‌



View 3 Images Dr Andrej Bozic (Image: Dentum)

The FOI data shows 148,405 penalty charge notices were issued in 2023. The following year this rose to 189,757 and by 2025 it stood at 212,143. Last month money expert Martin Lewis said many people were incorrectly claiming after being moved from Tax Credits to Universal Credit and assuming the same NHS benefits still apply.

Dr Bozic said: “It’s extremely concerning to see more than 200,000 fines last year for people incorrectly claiming for free treatment they are not entitled to. There is clearly an element of some people not understanding the complex eligibility criteria.”

‌



If you’re not entitled to free NHS dental treatment the costs are grouped into three bands. The first, covering examination, assessment and simple procedures such as scaling costs £29.70.

The second band, costing £76.60, covers treatments such as root canals or fillings. And the third covers more complex treatment such as orthodontic treatment and fixing missing teeth. This costs £332.10.

View 3 Images Seeing a dentist can be expensive but some people qualify for free care (Image: Getty Images/Westend61)

‌



But accessing NHS dental care is not always easy and patients in some areas of the country face a shortage of places - referred to as so-called "dental deserts". This shortage leads many to pay for private dental care or, in some cases, travel abroad for treatment such as to the Dentum private dental clinic based in Croatia where around 1,500 UK patients travel each year for both complex and cosmetic care.

Who qualifies for free dental care

According to the NHS you can get free NHS dental appointments and treatment if:

you're aged under 18, or under 19 and in full-time education

you're pregnant or have had a baby in the last 12 months

you've had a stillbirth in the past 12 months

you're getting treatment in an NHS hospital from a hospital dentist (but you may still need to pay for dentures or bridges)

you receive War Pension Scheme payments, or Armed Forces Compensation Scheme payments and the treatment is for your accepted disability

Article continues below

You can also get free NHS dental treatment if you or your partner receive certain benefits including:

Income-related Employment and Support Allowance

Pension Credit Guarantee Credit

Pension Credit Guarantee Credit with Savings Credit

Universal Credit – but only if your income is below a certain amount

If you or your partner receive benefits that mean you can get free dental treatment from the NHS, your dependents aged under 20 can also get free dental treatment.

News.title: Three red drinks that could help lower blood pressure
News.content:
Three red drinks that could help lower blood pressure

Having high blood pressure can put you at risk of serious health complications

View 3 Images Studies have shown that these drinks could have an impact on your blood pressure (Image: Getty)

Three red juices could help lower your blood pressure, according to research. These delicious drinks could therefore reduce your risk of serious complications such as heart attacks and strokes.

‌



High blood pressure is a significant concern across the UK, with approximately one in three adults believed to be affected by the condition. Also known as hypertension, it means the heart must work harder to pump blood around the body. Over time, this places additional strain on vital organs such as the heart and can result in lasting damage.

‌



It is also associated with a number of serious health conditions including heart disease, stroke and even dementia. Fortunately, there are lifestyle changes you can make to bring your blood pressure down, such as quitting smoking, increasing physical activity, and reducing alcohol consumption. Diet is another crucial factor, with excessive salt intake widely recognised as one of the biggest offenders.

‌



While certain foods and drinks can push blood pressure up, others can bring it down. Among the latter, beetroot juice, tomato juice, and pomegranate juice could all make a notable difference.

View 3 Images Having high blood pressure can increase your risk of heart attack and stroke (Image: Getty)

Beetroot juice

An unlikely choice of drink, beetroot juice is packed with nitrates - natural compounds that could help reduce blood pressure. This is because the body converts nitrates into nitric oxide, which widens blood vessels.

‌



A scientific review, published in Frontiers in Nutrition in 2022, examined seven studies exploring the effects of beetroot juice on blood pressure. It found that the drink lowered systolic blood pressure in individuals with hypertension.

Tomato juice

Another less familiar beverage, tomato juice could be key to better blood pressure. A 2019 study, published in Food Science and Nutrition, examined the impact of unsalted tomato juice on participants.

The participants consumed approximately 200 millilitres of the drink daily for one year on average. Consequently, researchers observed a reduction in systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure in 94 individuals with untreated high blood pressure or prehypertension.

‌



View 3 Images One study on tomato juice found it could decrease both systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure (Image: Getty)

Pomegranate juic e

Research has also connected pomegranate juice to enhanced blood pressure. A meta-analysis, published in Pharmacological Research in 2017, examined eight randomised placebo-controlled trials involving 574 individuals.

Some participants drank the juice regularly for two weeks, while others continued for 18 months. The analysis determined that pomegranate juice decreased both systolic and diastolic blood pressure, with the reduction in systolic pressure occurring irrespective of consumption duration.

‌



To reduce your blood pressure, the NHS recommends you:

Have a healthy, balanced diet

Exercise regularly – aim to do at least 150 minutes of exercise a week

Lose weight if you're overweight

Do not eat too much salt – avoid salty food or adding salt to your meals

Do not drink too much alcohol – avoid drinking more than 14 alcohol units a week on a regular basis.

Do not drink too much caffeine – drinks high in caffeine include coffee, tea and cola

Do not smoke

Article continues below

If you are concerned about your blood pressure you should speak to your GP.

News.title: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump 'if right for Britain'
News.content:
Burnham said: "My strength is remaining close to people, close to the public, that will not change as prime minister."

Asked if he would call out Trump if it was the right thing, he said, "of course", going on to say: "You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly."

Burnham also said he had had "concern" about the president starting the conflict with Iran, and he "wouldn't hold back from saying what I think is right".

The prime minister would not commit to a date when the government would spend 3% of GDP on defence. His Chancellor John Healey resigned from the previous government saying that unless a commitment was made to spend that amount by 2030, the country would not be safe.

But Burnham said: "I appointed my new chancellor very aware of what he had said about the critical importance of defence spending and the position that he had taken about that.

"The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded and that's the thing that's right in front of us and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year."

News.title: Andy Burnham rules out early election in exclusive BBC interview
News.content:
In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, Andy Burnham explicitly dismissed the idea of an early general election, saying "I'm going to rule it out... I don't think people want it."

Explaining his decision, the new prime minister suggested the majority of the electorate "voted for a manifesto" in the last election, and vowed he would "honour that manifesto" with the support of parliamentary colleagues.

Burnham went on to say, "I just think what I most need to do is get Britain focused on getting the country back where it should be, getting it working."

Andy Burnham: The Laura Kuenssberg Interview will be available across BBC News on Sunday and the interview will be shown in full on Panorama on BBC One on Monday at 20:00 BST.

News.title: Police investigate donations by Tice company to Reform UK
News.content:
Police are investigating payments to Reform UK by a company controlled by the party's deputy leader, Richard Tice, BBC News has learned.

Britain Means Business gave the party two donations of Â£250,000 in the run-up to the 2024 general election, when Tice was party chairman.

Tice has said the money was given to his firm by Fiona Cottrell, a significant donor to Reform UK and mother of a convicted fraudster with close links to Nigel Farage.

Tice said: "This is the first I have heard of it - if true why are the Met Police briefing the BBC before contacting interested parties? Is the Met leadership now engaged in the widespread politically motivated smear campaign against Reform and its leaders?"

Earlier this month, the Times newspaper, external revealed that two donations given directly by Fiona Cottrell to Reform UK in May 2024 were being investigated by the Metropolitan Police.

That investigation relates to legislation governing elections, which bans concealing or disguising donations derived from an "impermissible" donor, or the use of "false" information about a donation including the amount or the identity of the donor.

The BBC has asked Fiona Cottrell for comment.

News.title: What Love Island tells us about the changing face of dating
News.content:
On the fourth series of Love Island UK in 2018, Megan Barton-Hanson pulled fellow Islander, Wes Nelson, for a chat.

Just moments earlier, she had ended her relationship with Eyal Booker after admitting the pair had little more than physical chemistry. Now, sitting opposite Wes, who had been coupled up with Laura Anderson since the start of the competition, she decided not to wait for him to make the first move.

"I think it's pretty obvious that I do really fancy you," she told him. "And I just felt like, if I didn't say something, I'd regret it massively."

By the end of the episode, viewers had a new nickname for her: "Muggy Megan". Critics accused her of moving too quickly between relationships and breaking "girl code". Others admired her honesty.

At the time, Barton-Hanson argued that she had been treated differently to her male counterparts. "People definitely do give girls a harder time than menâ¦ It's sexist."

But eight years later, scenes like Barton-Hanson's no longer feel quite so out of the ordinary. Until this series, the opening coupling had always seen the men choose first. This year, the shows rules were changed, with the women making the first choice.

News.title: Residents allowed to return after Cairngorms wildfire evacuation
News.content:
Residents of the village of Nethy Bridge, near the wildfire that has been burning in the Cairngorms, have been told they can return to their homes after being evacuated on Friday night.

The fire was declared a major incident due to a change in weather, but that has now been stood down by Police Scotland.

First Minister John Swinney said the government and emergency services will continue to treat the blaze with the utmost seriousness until the last flames are out.

Locals have criticised the handling of the wildfire, which has been burning for 10 days, saying the move to declare it a major incident came too late and the government had been slow in scaling up their response.

In a statement on Saturday night, Police Scotland said "after an extensive multi-agency response to a large fire within Cairngorms National Park, residents of Nethy Bridge are being advised that they can now return to their properties".

Police Scotland's deputy assistant chief officer, Kenny Barbour, said the decision to stand down the major incident followed a detailed assessment by emergency responders.

He added in a statement: "The extensive work carried out over recent days, including the creation of effective fire breaks, has significantly reduced the risk to nearby communities, allowing evacuated residents to safely return home."

Supt Judy Hill added that the "ongoing multi agency response remains a high priority, with significant partnership resources and volunteers working tirelessly and in challenging circumstances, to support our efforts to extinguish the fires".

Firefighters will continue to maintain a significant operational presence until the incident is safely concluded, with 75 remaining on the ground on Saturday, police said.

At a meeting of the Scottish government's resilience room on Saturday evening, the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said there had been "good progress" in strengthening fire breaks to protect residential areas and said the number of fire hot spots was reducing.

First Minister John Swinney welcomed the lifting of the evacuation notice but stressed that "the Scottish Government, the emergency services and all relevant authorities will continue to treat this wildfire, as has been the case since its onset, with the utmost seriousness and necessary resources until the last flames are out."

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty in tears after missing out on gold again
News.content:
After tears in Paris, tears again in Glasgow.

It leaves even the great Adam Ramsay-Peaty wondering how much of this is worth it.

"I work a lot harder than what it says on the scoreboard," the Englishman said after taking 100m breaststroke bronze at the Commonwealth Games, his eyes and cheeks red with emotion.

"It hurts too much. I have got to approach training differently now because it hurts too much."

Ramsay-Peaty has done it all in this sport.

Three Olympic gold medals. Eight world titles. The 14 fastest times in history.

But after taking a break from swimming amid a wave of mental health issues in 2023, he is still searching for that winning feeling again on the big stage.

He was pipped to Olympic gold in Paris two years ago. In Glasgow, despite coming into the final as the fastest qualifier, he had to settle for bronze.

He was beaten by Australia's Sam Williamson but also Jersey's history-maker Filip Nowacki, the 18-year-old he has taken under his wing.

Ramsay-Peaty was third at halfway and could not close the gap. His time - 59.65 seconds - was more than four-tenths slower than his semi-final swim and three seconds off his personal best from seven years ago.

"It took a lot of courage to get back into the sport, so we should be happy with everything we get, but then that contradicts the athlete inside me and what I work for," he said.

"I just think I deserve more. I know sport isn't about what you deserve or even what you work for - it's who gets it on the day.

"I just know I'm a better athlete than that. It's very disappointing."

Ramsay-Peaty has spoken about the difficult decisions that come with being an elite athlete. The time away from his son, whom he held in his arms after the Paris silver. The events at home he has to miss.

"They are not even sacrifices; they are choices," he said.

"It's like getting knocked out in the group stages in the World Cup for a very good team. You know you're better and it hurts because you know you have to wait for a very long time for the next championships.

"This is probably - realistically - my last Commonwealth Games and I thought I'd trained for better. I could do better. I've been faster this season. That's where the frustration is."

News.title: I thought the Lockerbie bombing was a closed case until I started asking questions
News.content:
I was only a year old when the UK's deadliest terror attack shocked the world.

In December 1988, Pan Am flight 103 exploded over the Scottish town of Lockerbie, killing all 259 people on board as well as 11 on the ground.

I was a teenager by the time Libyan intelligence officer Abdelbaset al-Megrahi was convicted of the bombing in 2001 and, when he later died, I thought that was largely the end of the story.

It wasn't.

The case still rumbles on and, later this year, a man suspected of making the bomb which blew up the plane, Abu Agila Masud, goes on trial in Washington DC.

As part of a Radio 4 Intrigue podcast series, I had an opportunity to delve into this complex case with fresh eyes.

The deeper I dug, the more complicated Lockerbie became and there have been times that I don't know what to believe.

News.title: Pizza, pasta, potatoes, protein - how Italian children became so overweight
News.content:
Daily life is not easy for Salvatore. At 17, he weighs 170kg (26st 10lb) and struggles to walk.

He can't tie his own shoelaces and his Vespa scooter strains to bear his weight - in one week, its wheels broke seven times.

"He eats constantly," says his mother Anna.

Salvatore is among a growing number of Italian children and teenagers living with obesity. The problem is particularly acute in the south: in parts of the Campania region, more than 40% of eight and nine-year-olds are overweight. The town of Ponticelli, on the outskirts of Naples, has earned the unenviable reputation as one of the world's child obesity capitals.

It is a striking development in a country long regarded as the spiritual home of the Mediterranean diet. Yet today, Italian children are among the most overweight in Europe, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

Salvatore is waiting for life-changing surgery at the Betania Hospital in Ponticelli, where Dr Sonja Chiappetta has spent 15 years treating patients with severe obesity.

Until recently, she says, most of her patients were in their fifties. "Now I see those same patients when they're teenagers, as young as 16. They are getting younger, and it's frightening."

The surgery she carries out removes up to 90% of the stomach - meaning people are unable to eat large quantities of food. Demand has risen sharply in this part of Italy.

But Salvatore has been told he cannot get the operation. His weight is so excessive it makes the surgery too dangerous.

Instead, Dr Chiappetta has prescribed him a GLP-1 weight-loss injection to reduce his appetite and help him lose enough weight for the operation.

News.title: Another UK heatwave looms after cooler end to weekend
News.content:
Sunday will be a cooler day for all of the UK as it begins cloudy with a little bit of rain for southern and eastern areas.

As temperatures fall widely by a couple of degrees, a few locations will finally mark the end to their third heatwave of the year, including Usk in Monmouthshire and Exeter in Devon.

Both places are forecast to see temperatures drop beneath the heatwave threshold for the first time in 21 consecutive days.

A breezier and fresher day for all, temperatures will largely be in the mid-20s Celsius for the south-east of the UK and in the mid-teens Celsius further north.

For many, the relief from the heat will be short-lived as high pressure is set to build close to the south of the UK next week.

This will stall rain-bearing weather fronts and any wet weather will become confined to northern and western areas - especially north-west Scotland.

In southern parts of the UK, temperatures look set to climb once again.

Tapping into the heat over the near continent, the UK is likely to enter another heatwave, with temperatures in England and Wales likely to peak around 25-32C for much of next week.

News.title: What a week's work experience taught these Year 10s about their futures
News.content:
When Kelsey first arrived at secondary school, she said she wanted to be almost anywhere else but there.

She struggled with friendships, clashed with teachers and often tried to avoid coming into school.

But after a week's work experience placement at Whipsnade Zoo, in Bedfordshire, her outlook could not be more different.

She said it made her a "completely different person" - more confident, with a "good group of friends" and a greater sense of purpose about where her education could lead her.

Children across the UK are strongly encouraged to do work experience while at school. In England, the government published new legal guidance in June for schools to deliver two weeks of "in-person and immersive" work experience in future, one between Year 7 and Year 9, and one between Years 10 and 11.

But not all work experience placements are equal, and finding the right one can be tricky.

Organisations like the Sutton Trust and the Social Mobility Foundation said some students could be limited by the availability of placements in their area, or a lack of family connections with local employers.

BBC News spoke to three Year 10 pupils, one year ahead of their final GCSE exams, about how they decided what areas of work they were interested in, their experiences of trying to find the right placement, and what it taught them about their future education and ultimate career goals.

News.title: Man charged with possession of explosive substance after bomb found in car
News.content:
A Dublin museum employee has been charged in connection with an investigation into the discovery of a bomb in a car in the Republic of Ireland.

Simon O'Donovan, 44, with an address at Sperrin Road in Dublin 12, was charged with being in possession of an explosive substance at St Lawrence Rd in Chapelizod, Dublin 10 on 22 July.

He appeared before the Special Criminal Court on Saturday evening, where the court heard he was employed by the Collins Barracks National Museum of Ireland.

A vehicle was stopped on the N2 near Carrickmacross near the Irish border on Wednesday. On Friday, a 25-year-old woman was charged in relation to the same incident.

News.title: Tourists describe their escape from France wildfires
News.content:
Families have relived how their tranquil holidays in France turned into a race to escape raging wildfires.

Tourists told the BBC of emergency alerts in the middle of the night, desperate drives just metres from six-storey high flames and the sight of people flocking to beaches with their suitcases.

Huge forest fires in south-west France and central Spain have displaced more than 220,000 people, with the French military drafted in to help and the Spanish government declaring a national emergency.

Winds and continued heat are still helping to fan the flames with some tourists reporting smelling acrid smoke like a "bonfire" far outside the affected areas.

Flights to Bordeaux and Madrid, the closest cities to the blaze-hit regions, are currently not affected. Earlier on Saturday, a French foreign minister described the fires as a "tragedy" but urged tourists not to cancel their travel plans.

Among those caught up in the crisis is Zac Morrison, who arrived in Cap Ferret - a popular peninsula blanketed with pine trees 40 miles (65km) south-west of Bordeaux - on Thursday.

The 21-year-old from London, who is on holiday with 10 members of his family, woke up to two text alerts at 04:00 and 06:00 local time ordering him to evacuate "by all means necessary".

News.title: Twenty firefighters taken to hospital after explosion in Essex
News.content:
Twenty firefighters were taken to hospital after a blaze ripped through an industrial unit and spread to a fertiliser store, triggering a major explosion.

The fire service declared a major incident on Friday, as more than 100 firefighters tackled the flames at Highlands Farm, near the village of Rettendon, Essex.

Three fire engines and two fire service cars were destroyed in the blaze.

Speaking at a media conference on Saturday, Rick Hylton, Essex's chief fire officer, praised the "remarkable professionalism, courage and commitment" of the fire crews.

News.title: Six men arrested over fatal stabbing in south London
News.content:
Six men have been arrested on suspicion of murder after a 22-year-old man was fatally stabbed in Clapham, south-west London, the Metropolitan Police has said.

Police were called at 04:37 BST following reports of a man attending hospital with a stab wound. He later died in hospital, the force said.

The incident is believed to have taken place around Tremadoc Road and Clapham High Street.

Police said four of the suspects also attended hospital with stab wounds and are continuing to receive treatment, although their injuries are not believed to be life-threatening or life-changing.

Alongside the four men in hospital â three aged 22 and one 24 â officers also arrested two further men, aged 27 and 23, at the hospital on suspicion of murder. They remain in police custody.

The Met said it understood the fatally injured man was stabbed at about 04:20. It added that officers were carrying out inquiries in and around Tremadoc Road and Clapham High Street to establish the full circumstances around the incident.

Det Ch Insp Sarah Lee, who is leading the investigation, said those in the area would continue to notice an increased police presence throughout Saturday.

The family of the man who died have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

Supt Mark Gallacher, a policing lead for the area, described the incident as "tragic".

"We understand that this will cause concern among the local community and specialist detectives are doing everything possible to determine what has happened," he added.

The Met urged witnesses or people with information about the incident to contact police on 101, quoting reference 1474/25July.

Information can also be provided anonymously to independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Joshua knocked down twice as dramatic win sets up Fury fight
News.content:
Anthony Joshua suffered two knockdowns - the first happening after just 20 seconds - before recovering to dramatically stop Kristian Prenga in the second round of his comeback fight in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The British heavyweight was fighting for the first time since surviving the December car crash in Nigeria that claimed the lives of his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele.

He was sensationally rocked by a huge uppercut from underdog Prenga in the opening round, and then hit the canvas again later in the round.

At that point he looked on the verge of one of the biggest shock defeats in heavyweight history, with the long-awaited Tyson Fury fight hanging by a thread.

But Joshua produced one of the greatest escapes of his career, and now that fight is on.

He unleashed his right hand in the second round, with the final shot sending Albanian Prenga crashing down and forcing the referee to halt the contest.

"It's more than punch power. That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina, that was the families. It hurts to even talk about it. It has been tough," Joshua, 36, said.

He choked up and stepped away from the microphone, before adding: "It's my brothers. I don't want to talk about it."

There had been speculation fellow Briton Fury might make a appearance despite insisting he would not attend.

But the master of mind games stayed true to his word, with Fury nowhere to be seen barely 24 hours on from his own warm-up win over Mariusz Wach in Thailand.

"I respect everything he has done and everything that he has achieved, but as a fighting person, we're here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat," Joshua said about the prospect of fighting Fury.

Contracts have been signed, but the venue and date for a fight more than a decade in the making are still unknown.

This chaotic night, however, belonged to Joshua in a victory forged through adversity during the most difficult months of his life.

News.title: It's the cocktail taking young drinkers by storm - but the packaging is 'unrecyclable'
News.content:
Cleaning up after pre-drinks, AÃ©dÃ©n Rooney puts his empty BuzzBallz in the recycling.

"It's plastic and metal, so I'd just assume it's recyclable," he said.

The company behind the bright, pre-mixed cocktails that have taken Gen Z by storm said they were recyclable on its website, but experts say this is not true.

BuzzBallz cannot be recycled as the PET plastic ball cannot be separated from the aluminium lid, global environmental action body WRAP said.

"It's greenwashing. I'm shocked," AÃ©dÃ©n said.

BuzzBallz blamed a website error for claiming they were recyclable via Terracycle, a US-only scheme, but did not comment on its now-deleted FAQ that said they were recyclable where UK councils allow.

News.title: Berlin police name suspect with ties to ‘Islamic circles’ after attack on LGBTQ+ event
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. German authorities on Sunday issued a wanted notice for a fugitive suspect in the van ramming near Berlin’s Pride festival that left one person dead and injured at least 17 others.

Police and prosecutors asked for help in finding the 21-year-old, whom they identified as Abdul B.

They said he is believed to have injured several people with a moving vehicle, and that one or more people apparently then left that vehicle.

Several people were also apparently stabbed, they added.

open image in gallery The 21-year old suspect identified by police as Abdul B. in a public call for his arrest, after a vehicle rammed down the crowd near Berlin's Pride CSD celebrations on Saturday evening, killing one person and wounding several, in this undated handout photo released by Polizei Berlin on July 26, 2026. Polizei Berlin/Handout via REUTERS ( Reuters )

Sunday’s notice warned the public to avoid “direct contact” with the suspect, saying that he may be armed and dangerous.

Police had said earlier that they had identified a suspect who has ties to Islamic groups in the German capital.

“The suspect is known to police. He is known to us as a member of Islamic circles here in Berlin, and our search for this person is proceeding at full speed,” police spokesperson Florian Nath said.

Mr Nath added that “we still have no information whatsoever regarding his specific motives, the exact sequence of events, or his role in the crime itself.”

open image in gallery Emergency personnel and police gather in Berlin, early Sunday, 26 July 2026 ( AP )

A van slammed into people gathered for Berlin’s famed LGBTQ+ event on Saturday night, killing one person, injuring at least 17 others and prompting police to call off the celebrations and a concert in the German capital hours after they had begun.

Police said some of the victims had life-threatening injuries.

In a post on X, police called on everyone to leave the site of the event immediately as ambulances and firefighters attended to the victims.

“We are conducting an intensive search for possible suspects,” Mr Nath said on a short video released on the Berlin police account on X.

Police spokesperson Alexander Klute told The Associated Press later that “at this point, we don’t know anything about possible motives, the identity of the perpetrator or the perpetrators, or anything of that nature”.

open image in gallery A Berlin firefighter rests near the scene where one person was killed and 16 injured after a car is believed to have hit the crowd on the outskirts of the Christopher Street Day (CSD) parade in Berlin, on 26 July 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

According to police, a white van had driven into the Tiergarten park around 10pm, which is next to the route that the pride march had passed along earlier, and hit several people before colliding with a tree.

Police could not say how many officers had been deployed to the scene but that it was “definitely a lot of police”.

Overall, more than 2,200 police officers have been on duty in Berlin since Saturday morning to protect the pride parade and other LGBTQ+ events in the city.

Police were conducting witness interrogations at the park during the night and were investigating accounts that in addition to the crash some victims appeared to have suffered stab wounds – but that it was too early to draw any conclusion from those accounts.

Berlin mayor Kai Wegner expressed shock, saying that “following a peaceful and vibrant pride parade, the rally for a tolerant and peaceful Berlin was attacked in the most brutal manner”.

“This is an attack on our free and cosmopolitan society,” Mr Wegner said. “I have confidence in the police and security authorities, who will be working around the clock to investigate.”

Meanwhile, authorities called on possible witnesses to come forward and share with police any video or photos they might have taken at the scene of the attack.

The city also activated a crisis hotline for people missing friends or family members.Hundreds of thousands of people had come to Berlin on Saturday to celebrate at Berlin’s pride parade, known in Germany as Christopher Street Day. It’s one of Europe’s largest LGBTQ+ celebrations.

open image in gallery A police vehicle after the annual Berlin's Christopher Street Day Pride parade was called off, after a car crashed into the crowd at Tiergarten park, leaving several people injured, in Berlin, Germany, 26 July 2026 ( Reuters )

The pride event in front of the city’s Brandenburg Gate, near Tiergarten, was called off around 10.15pm and a band’s performance on stage was interrupted.

People were urged to go home and to avoid taking the route through the park.Before the incident, people had celebrated peacefully, marching through the city for hours, dancing to loud music, and cheering the around 80 floats that participated in the parade.

Julian Miethig, who had attended the LGBTQ+ party at the Brandenburg Gate earlier, said he had just wanted to go to an afterparty when he heard from a friend that “something bad happened there and there are a lot of fire trucks, a lot of emergency vehicles, ambulances.”

He said he went to Tiergarten and was shocked that something like this could have happened at Berlin’s pride celebrations.“It’s a dark day for the community,” he said.

(With additional input from Reuters)

News.content:
