Alcohol has many negative effects on our health, some of which may surprise you.

These include short-term impacts such as waking up with a pounding head or anxiety, to long-term effects including cancer.

If you are thinking about taking some time off alcohol, you’ll find many quick wins and long-term gains for your health.

We’ve made a timeline – based on scientific research – that shows what you might feel in the first days, weeks, months and years after taking a break from alcohol.

Some benefits start immediately, so every day without alcohol is a win for your health.

After one day

open image in gallery Some health benefits of giving up alcohol start very quickly, meaning your body and mind will reap the benefits ( Getty )

Alcohol takes around 24 hours to completely leave your body, so you may start noticing improvements after just one day.

Alcohol makes you need to urinate more often, causing dehydration. But your body can absorb a glass of water almost immediately, so once alcohol is out of your system alcohol dehydration is reduced, improving digestion, brain function and energy levels.

Alcohol also reduces the liver’s ability to regulate blood sugar. Once alcohol leaves the system, blood sugar begins to normalise.

If you are a daily drinker you may feel a bit worse to start with while your body adjusts to not having alcohol in its system all the time. You may initially notice disrupted sleep, mood changes, sweating or tremors. Most symptoms usually resolve in about a week without alcohol.

After one week

Even though alcohol can make you feel sleepy at first, it disrupts your sleep cycle. By the end of an alcohol-free week, you may notice you are more energetic in the mornings as a result of getting better quality sleep.

As the body’s filter, the liver does much of the heavy lifting in processing alcohol and can be easily damaged even with moderate drinking.

The liver is important for cleaning blood, processing nutrients and producing bile that helps with digestion.

But it can also regenerate quickly. If you have only mild damage in the liver, seven days may be enough to reduce liver fat and heal mild scarring and tissue damage.

Even small amounts of alcohol can impair brain functioning. So quitting can help improve brain health within a few days in light to moderate drinkers and within a month even for very heavy dependent drinkers.

open image in gallery Your mood will improve by about a month after you have stopped drinking ( Alamy/PA )

After one month

Alcohol can make managing mood harder and worsen symptoms of anxiety and depression. After a few weeks, most people start to feel better. Even very heavy drinkers report better mood after one to two months.

As your sleep and mood improve you may also notice more energy and greater wellbeing.

After a month of abstinence regular drinkers also report feeling more confident about making changes to how they drink.

You may lose weight and body fat. Alcohol contains a lot of kilojules and can trigger hunger reward systems, making us overeat or choose less healthy foods when drinking.

Even your skin will thank you. Alcohol can make you look older through dehydration and inflammation, which can be reversed when you quit.

About the authors Nicole Lee is an Adjunct Professor at the National Drug Research Institute, Curtin University, Australia. Katinka van de Ven is an Alcohol and other drug specialist, UNSW, Sydney, Australia. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

Alcohol irritates the gut and disrupts normal stomach functioning, causing bloating, indigestion, heartburn and diarrhoea. These symptoms usually start to resolve within four weeks.

One month of abstinence, insulin resistance – which can lead to high blood sugar – significantly reduces by 25 per cent. Blood pressure also reduces (by 6 per cent) and cancer-related growth factors declines, lowering your risk of cancer.

After six months

The liver starts to repair within weeks. For moderate drinkers, damage to your liver could be fully reversed by six months.

At this point, even heavy drinkers may notice they’re better at fighting infections and feel healthier overall.

After one year or more

Alcohol contributes to or causes a large number of chronic diseases, including heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes, and seven different types of cancer, as well as mental health issues. All of these risks can be reduced by quitting or cutting back on alcohol.

Alcohol increases blood pressure. High blood pressure (hypertension) is the top risk factor for death in the world. A small 2mmHg increase in blood pressure above the normal range (120mmHG) increases death from stroke by 10 per cent and from coronary artery disease by 7 per cent.

Cutting back on alcohol to less than two drinks a day can reduce blood pressure significantly, reducing risk of stroke and heart disease. Reducing blood pressure also reduces risk of kidney disease, eye problems and even erectile dysfunction.

With sustained abstinence, your risk of getting any type of cancer drops. One study looked at cancer risk for more than 4 million adults over three to seven years and found the risk of alcohol-related cancer dropped by 4 per cent, even for light drinkers who quit. Reducing from heavy to moderate drinking reduced alcohol-related cancer risk by 9 per cent.

Making a change

Any reduction in drinking will have some noticeable and immediate benefits to your brain and general health. The less you drink and the longer you go between drinks, the healthier you will be.

Whether you aim to cut back or quit entirely, there are some simple things you can do to help you stick with it:

Set clear goals plus the smaller steps you need to take to get there

Pay attention to the benefits you notice from quitting

Monitor your progress with a Drink Tracker

Get support from others, for example Hello Sunday Morning’s anonymous Daybreak app, SMART Recovery, CounsellingOnline or Sober in the Country.

If you are still wondering about whether to make changes or not you can check your drinking risk here.

If you have tried to cut back and found it difficult you may need professional help. Call the National Alcohol and other Drug Hotline on 1800 250 015 and they will put you in touch with services in your area that can help. You can also talk to your GP.

We would like to thank Dr Hannah MacRae for assistance in identifying the research used in this article.

News.content:
This is the moment Berlin Pride was evacuated after a vehicle drove into the crowd, killing one person and injuring at least 17 others on Saturday evening (25 July).

Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered peacefully in the German capital for the annual Christopher Street Day celebrations, one of Europe's largest LGBTQ events, before the attack brought it to an abrupt end.

A suspect in the Berlin attack was identified in the early hours of Sunday morning as a member of the city’s “Islamist scene”, according to police. Police and prosecutors asked for help in finding the 21-year-old, whom they identified as Abdul B.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton hit with penalty in blow to Hungarian GP hopes
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s hopes of significantly denting Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead were dealt a blow after he was given a three-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Hamilton looked to be the man to beat heading into qualifying at the Hungaroring and was on course for a record 10th pole position here before a messy final few minutes cost him.

Ferrari were well placed to end Mercedes’s run of having taken pole position for every grand prix this season. Instead, defending champion Lando Norris snuck in and took a superb pole for McLaren with a lap of 1min 17.207sec.

A poor final lap from Hamilton was compounded by a grid penalty for impeding the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, meaning the seven-time world champion will start fifth for the race at one of his most favoured circuits. The only consolation was that Antonelli was also given a three-place grid penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. The Italian will start seventh while Charles Leclerc, Hamilton’s team-mate, will be alongside Norris on the front row.

Heading into the final runs in Q3, Hamilton was 0.101sec ahead of Norris, but did not improve his time. Yet Norris, who was fastest in Q1 and Q2, and was the last of the top three across the line in Q3, had no problem, beating Hamilton’s time by 0.012sec.

Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team for sending him out first, a decision he said “shocked” him.

“I don’t know why we went first, that was a bit of a shock to me and I definitely wouldn’t have chosen to go first,” Hamilton said. “I had a clean out-lap and when I started my lap and already in turn one I had a snap [of oversteer], I was already a tenth down. The last lap was the worst lap of all... we clearly had the car to be on pole.”

Worse was on the way for Hamilton. The stewards later confirmed the three-place grid penalty to add to the disappointment of missing out on pole.

Replays showed a frustrated Piastri gesturing to Hamilton for blocking him at turn one, ruining the Australian’s final flying lap. Hamilton said he was unaware that Piastri was there, which was proved by video evidence that showed how much he impeded the McLaren. It would have been an easy decision for the stewards to make.

News.title: ‘Always in bloom, a visit really makes one’s day’: Your favourite garden centres
News.content:
Bryan, 86, from the South East, has been a customer of Henry Street Garden Centre in Arborfield, Berkshire for decades: “My wife and I often used to browse and purchase plants and garden furniture.”

But his favourite memory was watching his wife’s “delight at their incredible Christmas displays of decorations. Lights, live reindeer even and the wonderful family atmosphere all around you,” he describes. “It’s still a magical place for me where I can get close to her memory.”

For Mary, 79, from the South East, “a garden centre is special if the plants are in season and healthy and there is great choice of both plants and compost”. She nominates family-run Grovewell Garden Centres at Swingfield near Folkestone, which has three other branches based in Kent.

Not only are their plants “always beautifully displayed”, she explains, they have “an amazing choice of garden supplies, cards and gifts, as well as a nice little coffee shop”. Her favourite memory, however, was at Christmas time a few years ago. “They have a couple of beautiful, nodding and interacting reindeer with a sofa in front of them. We were admiring them and an older guy on the staff asked if we wanted a photo taken, which was so sweet of him.”

“He took my husband’s phone and got a really happy little snap of us and the reindeer, which our girls thought was hilarious,” she says. “Service with a smile.”

Community spirit

News.title: Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe
News.content:
Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

Kick-off is at 12.30pm.

News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

News.title: The best plays and musicals in London (and beyond) to book in 2026
News.content:
War Horse, back at the National Theatre almost two decades after its premiere, has lost none of its power, while Kenneth Branagh is casting a spell in Stratford-upon-Avon as Prospero in The Tempest. Further ahead, the year promises some thrilling new theatrical prospects, including a stage adaptation of the Oscar-winning film The Lives of Others, starring Keira Knightley.

Sports.title: England boss Thomas Tuchel takes in World Cup disappointment with London bike ride
Sports.content:
ENGLAND coach Thomas Tuchel gets a grip on his World Cup ­disappointment — by taking a ride on an electric hire bike.

The 52-year-old Three Lions boss looked in need of a pick-me-up as he went on a coffee run in ­Notting Hill, West London.



He bought himself a drink and handed another to a homeless woman.

A week earlier, he guided England to a 6-4 win over France to seal third place, our best World Cup finish since 1966.



But it came after an agonising 2-1 semi-final defeat to Argentina.

England had been leading until the 85th minute.

Tuchel came in for heavy criticism due to the substitutions he made while trying to protect England’s 1-0 lead.

The German coach then said England lacked the ‘DNA’ to control possession.



Midfielder Jude ­Bellingham, meanwhile, chilled at Disneyland, California, with his ­girlfriend Ashlyn Castro.

And his teammate Declan Rice was at Disney in Florida with his nephew.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reunites with ex-boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in Norway before praising Man Utd’s academy stars
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK praised Manchester United’s academy gems for playing with swagger in the club’s 5-0 preseason win over Rosenborg.

Carrick again started with a strong side in Trondheim, but brought on two youngsters at the break in full backs Harry Amass and Jaydan Kamason.



Kamason produced two brilliantly worked assists, while Amass scored and played a fake one-two with Joshua Zirkzee to set up the Dutchman’s stunner.

Eight more youngsters arrived on the hour mark, with Jacob Devaney, on at centre-back, instantly finding the net before Ethan Williams completed the riot.



While it is still early days in pre-season, the most of the younger players have covered themselves in glory against Wrexham in Helsinki, and a limited Rosenborg side in Trondheim.

Carrick told MUTV in Norway: “That’s the best way to be as a footballer, when you’re in that zone and you’re confident, that’s my job to try and get the players in that frame of mind.

“The younger players, when you see them expressing themselves and being themselves and keep pushing themselves to be better.

“Some of the play in the second half was really, really good and I was delighted to see that from them.

“They’ve all got potential in different ways, and you want them to fulfil it and keep pushing themselves, and they certainly did that.”

Carrick met up with his former boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer before the match on Friday.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The pair were both considered to take over from Ruben Amorim when the Portuguese was sacked in January.

Carrick did most of the coaching during Solskjaer’s three years in charge and that played a major part in the Geordie getting the nod over the Norwegian.

The pair have remained close friends and keep in touch, and Solskjaer’s family home in Kristiansund is a three hour drive from Trondheim.

Carrick worked under Solskjaer during United’s preseason friendly in Oslo against Kristiansund BK in July 2019.



Following the defeat to Wrexham in Finland and the more structured football in Norway, United head to Sweden next.

The Red Devils are back in action on Saturday when they face Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

Sports.title: New PM Andy Burnham actively considering letting football fans drink in stands again
Sports.content:
ANDY Burnham’s Government is actively considering letting football fans drink in the stands again.

Officials are considering whether to review restrictions which stop people consuming alcohol in view of the pitch.



The ban was introduced in 1985 to stop football hooligans fighting.

Other sports like rugby were not affected.



A government spokesperson said: “We are considering the case being made by some clubs and supporter groups for reviewing the current restrictions on alcohol consumption at football matches.

“The safety of football fans remains our priority, and any future consideration of changes would need to be evidence-led and informed by the views of policing and safety authorities, as well as clubs, supporters and other partners across the football sector.”

It comes just weeks after the new Prime Minister said it was “wrong” that spectators could not enjoy a pint during matches.

Everton fan Mr Burnham made the comments while watching a rugby league match at the club’s Hill Dickinson Stadium.



In a social media clip while holding a pint, he said: “How come these lads can do that in my seat here when we can’t do that at an Everton home game?

“There’s something wrong there, we need to take a look at that.”

This week the new Prime Minister announced that pubs, social clubs and live music venues will be given a 20 per cent cut to business rates from April.

Landlords welcomed the change but called on the Labour leader to go further by slashing VAT on boozers too.

The new Prime Minister insisted he was ready to protect “working-class culture” – in a win for The Sun’s Save Our Sups campaign.



More than 30,000 venues will save an estimated £1,100 each in the next financial year from the business rates cut.

Sports.title: ‘Sky’s the limit’ – Ayden Heaven talks up England hopes and could benefit from Man Utd mentor Harry Maguire’s misfortune
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED star Ayden Heaven insists “the sky is the limit” this season as he targets a dream England call-up.

And the Old Trafford teenager could be ready to carry the torch, just as mentor Harry Maguire’s proud Three Lions career likely enters its final chapter.



The 19-year-old centre half is targeting a major breakout year under Michael Carrick after waiting in the wings last term.

While Maguire has not retired from England duty, missing out on the 2026 World Cup squad at 33 suggests a natural transition is underway for the Three Lions—one Heaven has his eyes on.



When asked about pushing to be part of England’s Under-21s Euros title defence next summer, Heaven skipped a step to aim straight for the top.

He said: “I could push further than that. Maybe try and get into England, the main men’s team. The sky‘s the limit.

“I’ve just got to keep working hard every day. Harry has helped a lot, he has 20 years of experience.

“He’s always telling me to be vocal so I’m always ready when I get the opportunity to play.”

At this stage of his career, Heaven has only reached England Under-20 level.

He started 11 Premier League games last season, often when one of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt or Harry Maguire were unavailable through injury or suspensions.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Heaven said: “I’m young and I’ve got to be patient, especially in my position. You don’t see a lot of 19-year-olds playing week in, week out.

“I know it’s nothing personal and I’ve just got to be patient. I’m waiting for my opportunity.”

It’s almost certain Heaven will not be called up by Thomas Tuchel in the next September international break, but this season should be a banner with more games back in the schedule.

The teen is pushing to start alongside Maguire in United’s opening day clash against Hull City on August 22, having been the starting duo so far in pre-season.



With Lisandro Martinez forced off injured during the World Cup final and Matthijs de Ligt recovering from back surgery, the door has opened for the young centre-back.

Heaven’s main rival for a spot is Frenchman Leny Yoro, who is just a year older.

But with United’s World Cup stars still on break, Yoro has been deployed at right-back in their opening two pre-season friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg.

Heaven said: “We’re both young. We work hard every day in training together and we are close friends off the pitch.”

The Londoner earned high praise after filling the void left during crucial wins against Chelsea, Brentford, and Liverpool as United racked up three wins on the bounce to help secure Champions League football.



He added: “To hear the manager’s praise as an extra boost that he’s given up. He played a big part for this club when he played.”

Heaven, under contract until 2029, was former boss Ruben Amorim’s second signing, snapped up from Arsenal’s academy by Ineos for £1.25m.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Amorim liked Heaven’s game, but managed his minutes carefully, singling him out for applause after United’s 4-1 win over Wolves in December.

That came one match after he was substituted for Yoro at half-time after a challenging opening 45 minutes against West Ham.

Sports.title: Arsenal signing Christos Tzolis was tipped for the top from young age and almost poached by Barcelona at 12
Sports.content:
CHRISTOS TZOLIS has been tipped for the top by those in Greece since he was seven years old.

And the winger has finally reached the summit after Arsenal coughed up £34million to sign him on a five-year deal from Club Brugge.



The hefty fee has raised a few eyebrows given that Tzolis failed to make the grade during three nightmare years at Norwich.

But those at the 24-year-old’s first club, Greek side PAOK, are not surprised and can still remember when Barcelona tried to poach him at the age of 12.



Academy technical director at PAOK, Vasilis Mittas, told SunSport: “Christos joined us at the age of seven, with qualities that set him apart.

“From the very beginning, it was clear that he was an exceptionally talented footballer.



“Everyone who worked with Christos at the academy believed he had the potential to reach the very highest level and play for one of Europe’s biggest clubs.

“One memory that stands out goes back to our Under-12s team. As a reward for winning an international tournament, the club’s owner gave us the opportunity to play a friendly match against Barcelona at their training ground.

“We won 2-1, with Christos scoring one goal and providing an assist, playing a decisive role in the victory and producing the standout performance of the match.

“His display was so impressive that Barcelona expressed an interest in him immediately after the game.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Tzolis did not sign for Barca and nor did he let the hype go to his head, even after scoring 100 goals in a single season for one of PAOK’s youth sides.

Mittas remembers the winger as being “humble and grounded”, with those traits still part of his character today.

The Greek star had a month’s holiday this summer, but spent most of it training when he learned that Arsenal were interested in him.

Mittas said: “He never caused any problems off the pitch.



“He was the type of player who would do everything possible on the pitch to help his team succeed.

“Throughout his development at the academy, he played across all three attacking positions, but what truly distinguished him was his personality.

“He possessed an incredibly strong mentality and an unwavering desire to win.”

Tzolis’ mental strength proved vital when he left PAOK in 2021 as a 19-year-old and joined Norwich for £9m.

The winger failed to take off with the Canaries and spent two of his three seasons out on loan.



Tzolis bounced back, though, and rebuilt his career with 43 goals and 45 assists in 108 games over two seasons at Brugge.

Mittas added: “He has always been a fighter, someone who never gives up.

“Christos was still very young [at Norwich] and had to adapt to a completely new environment, a different culture, a new language and the unique demands of English football.



“What impressed me most was the way he responded. He never allowed that difficult period to define him.

“Everyone at PAOK believed he would come back stronger, and that’s exactly what he did.

“Looking back now, those challenges made him mentally tougher and played a significant role in shaping the player he has become today.”

Now 24 and coming into his prime, Mittas believes that everyone is starting to see the player PAOK knew Tzolis could be.

He has been signed by Arsenal to play off the left flank and replace Leandro Trossard, but can operate as a No10.



Tzolis models his game on Spain legend David Villa and his eye for goal has always been a big weapon.

Mittas said: “He has the instinct of a natural goalscorer.

“In every match, he finds a way to create or exploit one or two clear goal-scoring opportunities. He combines pace, explosiveness and excellent transitional play.

“I believe Christos is a perfect fit for Arsenal’s style of play, just as he is ideally suited to the demands of the Premier League.

“He is a player with significant room for further development, and I have no doubt that working every day under a coach like Mikel Arteta will help him reach an even higher level.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Ultimately, everything comes back to his character, work ethic and ambition. He always sets himself the highest standards and works relentlessly to achieve them.

“He is now entering what are traditionally considered the most productive years of a footballer’s career – and I firmly believe that his best football is still ahead of him.”

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes almost doubles annual income as Man Utd captain, 31, rakes in millions off pitch
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES scored a whopping £9.2MILLION in image rights payments.

The Manchester United skipper banked the huge sum in off-pitch earnings as he looks to agree a new deal at Old Trafford.



Fernandes, 31, is entering the final 12 months of his contract but club figures have told him they do not want him to leave under any circumstances.

United already have an option to extend the deal by a further 12 months — but they are hoping to increase it further.



Last season he became the first United player to win the Football Writers’ Player of the Year since Wayne Rooney 16 years ago.

Latest accounts filed by the Portuguese playmaker’s image rights firm show he tucked away £9.2m in off-pitch earnings.

And paperwork covering the 2024-25 season shows he has piled up £9.5m in BF8 Sports Ltd — the firm he set up in 2020 to use for off-field pay.

That figure shot up by £1.1m compared with the previous year — almost £100,000 a month.

After paying bills, Fernandes is left with £9,180,001.

And that is on top of his wages for playing.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Fernandes is reportedly on £12.5m a year at United, with bonuses, image rights and lucrative sponsorship deals with brands including Nike, DHL and EA Sports earning him more millions.

He is also reported to have a number of properties in both England and Portugal.

Fernandes is expected to join Man Utd’s pre-season campaign after completing his holiday following the World Cup where he represented Portugal.

Sports.title: Major update on Jack Grealish’s future as Enzo Maresca breaks silence on £100m England star frozen out under Guardiola
Sports.content:
IT was three years ago when Jack Grealish and Enzo Maresca were last together at Manchester City.

They were reunited at the Etihad Campus this week — but it looks highly unlikely it will last more than a few weeks.



Back in summer 2023 — when the Italian left his role as Pep Guardiola’s assistant to take charge of Leicester — Grealish, 30, looked to have the world at his feet.

He had just played a starring role in City’s historic Treble and was finally justifying his record-breaking £100million price-tag.



Yet, since then he has started only 17 Premier League games for the club and spent last season on loan at Everton.

Maresca, 46, revealed at his first press conference as the new boss on Friday the pair have stayed in regular contact. Like most people, the Italian clearly has a soft spot for Grealish.

Yet, when asked where it has all gone wrong for the former Aston Villa captain, Maresca said: “When you don’t work day by day with the players, it’s difficult to judge. I don’t know what he has done. It’s complicated.”

Grealish is still working on an individual programme as he battles back from the foot injury he suffered with the Toffees in January.

So he was unable to join in the sessions with the new boss at the City Football Academy but posted pictures on social media.

He wrote: “Nice to see everyone. I’m nearly there — hopefully not long now til I’m back training.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

No doubt it would have been nice to see Maresca, too. Although maybe he was hoping for a bit more encouragement from the new manager.

Instead the Italian said: “In any club I join, it’s my duty to coach the players at the club and Jack is here at the moment. I have a good relationship with him and since I left we’ve been keeping in touch.

“He has a big heart and is a very good guy but we’ll see what happens.”

It was hardly a ringing endorsement from an incoming manager — and the Three Lions favourite could be forgiven for seeing the writing on the wall.



So in a week when he was overtaken as City’s record transfer by another England man in £116m Elliot Anderson, Grealish finds himself at a crossroads.

Grealish was loved by both fans and staff during his loan spell down the M62 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium after he made such an encouraging start.

His season was ended by injury but he spent the final few months of the campaign working on his rehab on Merseyside — rather than returning to his parent club.

But, unsurprisingly given the way it all ended, the Toffees did not take up the £50m option to buy him permanently this summer.

Everton have not ruled out taking him back but another loan makes no sense for either him or City as he has just one year left on his contract.



David Moyes will want to see sure signs he is fully recovered before committing some of his transfer budget to signing a player who turns 31 in September.

His good pal and former Villa team-mate Gabby Agbonlahor believes Grealish’s days at City are over — and predicts he could even move abroad.

He said: “It will be interesting to see what happens with Jack, if he’s given a chance by Maresca. He would have been part of that City squad when Maresca was there as assistant.



“But will the manager think, ‘No’, and will Jack think, ‘Do you know what? Maybe I want to move on’?I don’t see him staying. Don’t rule out him going back to Everton.

“David Moyes loved him but it wouldn’t surprise me to see him play somewhere else in Europe.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

First, Grealish needs to get himself fit and Maresca must decide whether to give him one last chance at City, five years after he made his record-breaking move.

But time is running out for the Midlander — and plenty of people at the Etihad will feel he has had enough last chances.

Sports.title: Moment starstruck David Beckham hugs his basketball idol Michael Jordan on sun-soaked Ibiza holiday with their wives
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL legend David Beckham embraces his basketball idol Michael Jordan on holiday.

The sporting giants had lunch in sunny Ibiza along with their wives.



David, 51, wrapped an arm around fashion designer Victoria, 52, while Michael, 63, cosied up to Cuban model Yvette Prieto, 48.

At one point, former Manchester United and England star David, who is about 6ft tall, smiled as he looked up to 6ft 6in Michael.



When he left United for Real Madrid in 2003, David opted for the No 23 jersey – the same Michael wore for the Chicago Bulls.

He previously revealed he was starstruck after meeting Michael for the first time at a restaurant.

He recalled: “Even though he was sat at a table with Madonna and a couple of others, I was looking straight at him.”

“Victoria just nudged my leg and said, ‘Stop embarrassing me’.”



When Madge sent over champers, David and Vic went over to say hello.



He said: “Michael stood up and I shook his hand and his whole hand covered the whole of my arm.”

Sports.title: Man Utd can solve two problems after approval to sign star Bryan Mbeumo hates playing
Sports.content:
Man Utd can solve two problems after approval to sign star Bryan Mbeumo hates playing

Manchester United continue to bolster their squad during the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Antonee Robinson is on United's radar (Image: Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Manchester United continue to be linked with Fulham star Antonee Robinson in a move that could provide two benefits to the Red Devils. Not only is the American defender is one of the most experienced left-backs in the Premier League, he's also the one Bryan Mbeumo hates coming up against the most.

‌



Robinson has drawn widespread admiration across the top flight, but it is the verdict of the United striker that is likely to carry the most weight. Mbeumo named Robinson as the toughest defender he has ever faced while appearing on the Obi One podcast last year.

‌



He said: "I used to play against him when he was at Wigan and (he) changed completely. When he arrived he was really athletic, quick, but with his feet he was like, not so good, you know?

‌



"But throughout the years he improved a lot, and I think now he can do everything. He can attack, he can defend, he's strong, he's good with his feet now, and yeah, I think really, really hard to play against him."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

Coming from a forward who tormented Premier League defences for years before his switch to United, that endorsement is far and above a huge compliment.

‌



Michael Carrick is understood to be monitoring Robinson closely as he looks to provide competition at left-back. Luke Shaw remains the only recognised senior option in that position following Tyrell Malacia's departure.

After Malacia's contract expired, Harry Amass became backup to Shaw. However, the teenager is considered too raw to shoulder the burden alone after just seven first-team appearances.

Robinson has become one of the Premier League's most consistent and dynamic full-backs, making 26 goal contributions across 215 appearances. He has also earned 58 caps for the United States national team, netting five times.

‌



View 2 Images Antonee Robinson has given Bryan Mbeumo plenty of bother in the past (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images)

His age has been flagged as a potential obstacle, with The Guardian reporting that Robinson falls outside United's preferred target profile. However, the quality of his performances continues to attract suitors regardless.

United can kill two birds with one stone in signing Robinson. He can provide cover - and competition - at left-back and allow Mbeumo to enjoy playing alongside him rather than coming up against him.

Article continues below

Robinson is believed to be available for approximately £25million - a fee that could represent outstanding value for any club willing to invest in a proven performer. For United in particular, securing Robinson alongside the returning Shaw would not only provide Carrick with dependable cover but also hand youngster Amass the breathing room to develop at a sensible pace.

Sports.title: Liverpool star was banished from pre-season after boss called him out on camera
Sports.content:
Liverpool star was banished from pre-season after boss called him out on camera

Liverpool's pre-season was disrupted after one of their players broke the rules

View 3 Images Mamadou Sakho joined Liverpool in 2013 (Image: VI-Images, VI-Images via Getty Images)

Liverpool's current pre-season tour of the USA is underway. However, one of the club's previous trips Stateside was marred by a falling out between former manager Jurgen Klopp and ex-defender Mamadou Sakho, which was partly caught on camera.

‌



Sakho, 36, officially retired from football earlier this year after being without a club since May 2025. The French defender was brought to Liverpool by ex-manager Brendan Rodgers in September 2013 in a bid to toughen up the club's backline, arriving from Paris Saint-Germain for £18 million.

‌



After taking over in October 2015, the following summer marked Klopp's first pre-season with the Reds. The German was clearly unafraid to make his presence felt among those in the squad who treated strict rules as merely guidance, as Sakho was sent home prematurely from the club's American tour.

‌



The grievance came to light after Sakho was handed a GoPro camera as the Liverpool squad visited Alcatraz prison in San Francisco. As Klopp was being interviewed by club staff, Sakho snuck up and laughed in the background and the German let slip that Sakho had violated a club rule on lateness.

“We could have left Mama Sakho here because he is filming me while I give the interview here,” Klopp said. Sakho interjected: “I have just one question. How long do you think you can live here?”

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Jurgen Klopp favourite has told Andoni Iraola all about Liverpool target Maghnes Akliouche READ MORE :

"Actually, I don't have to think about it. You should think about it," Klopp said back. "Because only one of us came late last night, for departure in Liverpool. It was not me."

Speaking after Sakho was sent home from the USA, Klopp explained: “I thought maybe it made sense for him to fly home to Liverpool and after eight or 10 days, when we come back, we can talk about it. It's not that serious.

“He nearly missed the departure of the plane, he missed a session and was late for a meal. We have some rules and we have to respect them. If somebody doesn't respect it or somebody gives me the feeling he is not respecting it, then I have to react, that's all.

‌



View 3 Images Mamadou Sakho and Jurgen Klopp's relationship was tested at Liverpool (Image: 2015 Liverpool FC)

“It is private how he reacted. But we had no argument. You cannot argue when only one person is speaking. That's all. I think missed a session is missed a session. Even injured players have sessions.”

Speaking in France later, Sakho admitted his penchant for tardiness to Canal Football Club, saying: “It is true that I turned up late. There was a rule that I should have observed. I do not at all see myself as above the rules, I respect everyone.

‌



“I paid my fine, I was sanctioned, I apologised to my team-mates and my manager. Aside from that… I do not want to go into the controversies.”

Sakho's debut campaign nearly delivered the Reds their first Premier League title in almost 25 years. Yet he featured in just 18 Premier League games as Liverpool's backline leaked 50 goals, ultimately costing them the championship and, while he impressed in Klopp's early days, his career never fully got off the ground at the Reds.

View 3 Images Sakho had a difficult end to his Liverpool career (Image: Colin Lane)

‌



The centre-back's actions in the USA proved to be the breaking point for Klopp, whose patience had worn thin. Sakho was demoted to the Under-23s and never featured for the senior side again.

January 2017 came around and Sakho departed Liverpool, sealing a loan switch to Crystal Palace. Sakho performed so impressively in south London that the Eagles even signed him permanently in the summer of 2017, shelling out £25m.

He departed in the summer of 2022. Sakho later featured for Montpellier and finally for Torpedo Kutaisi in the Georgian first division before calling time on his colourful career.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish's dream summer move set to be blocked following transfer announcement
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish's dream summer move set to be blocked following transfer announcement

Jack Grealish spent last season on loan to Everton from Manchester City

View 3 Images Jack Grealish is now facing a tough summer (Image: Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Jack Grealish's dream Aston Villa homecoming could be off the cards following the signing of Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea. The left winger agreed a season-long loan in Birmingham with an obligation to buy clause set for next summer.

‌



Garnacho arrived at Villa Park following the Blues' acquisition of Morgan Rogers for a record £117million fee. While these transfers represent positive reinforcements for both clubs, it could also spell disaster for Grealish.

‌



The England international joined City for £100m in 2021, signing a six-year deal. During his time at the Etihad, Grealish has secured three Premier League titles and the Champions League.

‌



However, his time on the pitch diminished rapidly and he sought a loan move after being left out of Pep Guardiola's plans. Grealish joined Everton for the 2025/26 campaign and regained his old form with six assists in 22 games.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Jack Grealish offered Man City lifeline by Enzo Maresca after Pep Guardiola snub READ MORE :

Enzo Maresca insists Man City won't repeat what Man Utd did after Sir Alex Ferguson READ MORE :

But a stress fracture in his foot killed his momentum and left him sidelined. The 30-year-old now has a decision to make: whether he tries to find a way under Enzo Maresca or move on to pastures new.

‌



A return to Villa could've been the dream for the boyhood fan, who joined the club aged six and became one of their modern heroes. Grealish appeared 213 times in claret and blue, making 75 goal contributions and leading them back to the Premier League as captain in 2019.

View 3 Images Alejandro Garnacho's arrival in Birmingham throws a wrench into the plans (Image: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

The money from his transfer to City helped stabilise Villa and Grealish shared his die-hard love with one clear message. He said: "I'll always be a Villa fan. I love this club with all my heart and I hope you understand my reasons for seeking a new challenge. The club are in great hands, the manager, the lads, the new signings coming in. It's an exciting time to be a Villa fan. I'll see you all again soon. Until next time. UTV."

‌



A return for the winger looks like a no-brainer for both parties, with former teammate Robert Snodgrass telling OLBG that the club simply have to think 'why not.' He said: "Listen, it is certainly possible that there might be a few openings available at Villa, as they may be looking to bolster their ranks. You just never know what a club like that might be planning.

View 3 Images Now Grealish will need to fight for his dream transfer (Image: Laurence Griffiths/Getty Images)

"When you look at the overall situation, I think Jack would absolutely love a return to that environment. It's well-documented that he is a die-hard Villa fan who is incredibly passionate about that club, so if the chance arose, you really have to think why not?"

Article continues below

Now, this transfer has become more difficult following Garnacho's arrival in Birmingham. The 22-year-old will provide cover in Grealish's natural position while also having age and speed on his side.

The left winger is eight years Garnacho's senior and has struggled with injury in recent seasons.

Sports.title: Matheus Cunha made thoughts clear after taking Marcus Rashford's shirt number at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Matheus Cunha made thoughts clear after taking Marcus Rashford's shirt number at Man Utd

Matheus Cunha made a telling comment about Marcus Rashford after taking the forward's Manchester United shirt number

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford will return to Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Matheus Cunha expressed how much of an honour it was to take Marcus Rashford’s No.10 shirt after he signed for Manchester United. Cunha was signed last summer from Wolves for a fee of £62.5million.

‌



The Brazilian forward was handed the jersey number when it was freed up following Rashford’s own move to Barcelona on a season-long loan with an option to buy. Many believed the Englishman would never return to his boyhood club, given the acrimonious nature of his departure following a falling out with then-head coach Ruben Amorim.

‌



But Barcelona opted not to activate their £26m purchase option this summer and, with Michael Carrick now in charge instead of Amorim, Rashford is set to return to United. The 28-year-old will re-join the side’s pre-season training following his post-World Cup summer break.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It is reported that Rashford’s representatives have had encouraging discussions with United about his pre-season return to Carrington. However, the forward will face an uncomfortable, awkward situation whereby he will no longer have his old iconic jersey, having lost his shirt number while away from Old Trafford.

Cunha, 27, will still occupy the number despite Rashford’s return. Prior to notching 10 goals and four assists in 35 appearances in his first season at Old Trafford last term, the Brazil international mentioned how he was relishing the chance to follow in the footsteps of former United players who wore the No.10 shirt, including Rashford.

‌



Marcus Rashford will have to confront awkward Man Utd reality when he returns to Old Trafford READ MORE :

Man Utd hatch transfer plan as Man City star Rodri gives green light to summer move READ MORE :

He admitted it was a "privilege" to wear it and hoped it would inspire him to match the exploits of his illustrious predecessors at United. Cunha said: "I can mention many players that used this shirt. It's so easy for me. Of course, I think the one that I always think about when I see this number in this shirt for me was Wayne Rooney. He was someone that I grew up to watch him play and I have watched many games now.

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha took the No.10 jersey in Rashford's absence (Image: Getty )

"Then I swapped shirts with Marcus after a game. I have his shirt in my home. But, of course, we know many players used this shirt – Ruud van Nistelrooy and Zlatan Ibrahimovic. It's the dream not only to use the shirt, but with all the history they have around the number, it's something beautiful that I have the privilege to do it.

Article continues below

"With every single number, it will be a pleasure to wear the shirt. But, yeah, with this one it’s something different. Then, of course, the responsibility comes."

Previous wearers of the No.10 shirt at United include Denis Law, Teddy Sheringham, Wayne Rooney, Ruud van Nistelrooy and Zlatan Ibrahimovic.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford 'would do a lot of good at Liverpool' after Man Utd transfer clause expires
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford 'would do a lot of good at Liverpool' after Man Utd transfer clause expires

A shock move to Liverpool for Marcus Rashford has been touted this summer

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford could still depart Old Trafford this summer (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford has been told he would flourish at Liverpool as the Manchester United star's future remains up in the air. That is the opinion of Chelsea legend Claude Makelele, who says he believed Barcelona would keep the England star following his successful loan last season.

‌



The La Liga champions opted to sign Newcastle star Anthony Gordon instead after refusing to pay the £26million option in Rashford's contract. The 28-year-old was expected to seek a permanent move away from Old Trafford this summer, with a clause in his deal allowing for his exit should a £40m bid come in, according to The Athletic.

‌



The clause was available to every club apart from United's biggest rivals, Manchester City and Liverpool. However, it has since expired, meaning any club now has the opportunity to sign Rashford by opening fresh negotiations for the forward.

‌



Rashford is set to join United's pre-season tour following his break after representing England at the World Cup. But a third successive move away from his boyhood club to none other than their greatest adversary has been suggested by Makelele.

Speaking to ComeOn, the Frenchman said: "I would have expected Barcelona to keep Marcus Rashford, honestly. It's strange. He had an exceptional season, and I think he loved playing in that team because they play football.

Man Utd hatch transfer plan as Man City star Rodri gives green light to summer move READ MORE :

Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race READ MORE :

"It's not the Premier League, it's not box-to-box. It let him rediscover his game, and he needed that after everything he went through at Manchester United. Sometimes a move is exactly what saves you: it gives you back the taste for football, for this sport we love, and it clearly did him good.

‌



"If staying at Barcelona isn't possible and he decides to come back to the Premier League, he would do a lot of good at Liverpool." Makelele's stance was backed by ex-Liverpool striker Fernando Morientes. The Spaniard suggested that playing for Andoni Iraola's side will only provide more motivation for Rashford to succeed.

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford is set to return to Manchester United this summer (Image: Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

He said to Reviant: "Marcus Rashford to Liverpool? I wouldn't be surprised. It might be a good place for him to show his quality. He showed it last year, I was going to say sparingly, not sparingly exactly, but in specific moments he showed he's a great player.

‌



"The thing is, with this type of player you have to give him minutes, give him games, because if you play him one game and rest him the next two, in the end these are players who never really settle.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola remains on the chase for a winger at Anfield (Image: Jacek Boczarski/Anadolu via Getty Images)

"For Liverpool, this type of player has an edge to it, since he's also played for Manchester [United] before. I don't know if that would give him even more motivation to prove how good a player he is.

‌



"But these are players I like, because they're natural athletes, they're very quick, and in the end the big clubs need this kind of profile: fast, athletic players with a good shot on them.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"The other side of it is whether he ends up delivering or not, and whether he has the backing of the stands too. He had his spot alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha. But now he’ll have to show it again at another club and Liverpool would be a good option yes."

Article continues below

Rashford primarily plays on the left of the attack, and Liverpool have already secured a reinforcement in that position with the signing of Victor Munoz. However, the club remain light on the opposite flank following the exit of Mohamed Salah.

Sports.title: Man Utd dream squad for 2026/27 as Aurelien Tchouameni signs and Marcus Rashford call made
Sports.content:
Man Utd dream squad for 2026/27 as Aurelien Tchouameni signs and Marcus Rashford call made

Manchester United could assemble the ideal squad for Michael Carrick this summer

View 5 Images Michael Carrick will be hoping to celebrate some more Man Utd signings soon (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

After dropping upwards of £80m to reinforce their central midfield options, Manchester United have established a sturdy base for a pivotal upcoming campaign. Even so, few expect their summer recruitment drive to wrap up just yet.

‌



Summer tune-ups have offered Michael Carrick valuable insight into what various members of his squad can deliver on the pitch. Meanwhile, a selection of international stars are set to report back at a later date following their post-World Cup breaks.

‌



With the start of the new Premier League season under four weeks off, United are gearing up for an opening-weekend trip to face top-flight newcomers Hull City.

‌



Prior to that opening fixture, the Red Devils are likely to secure further arrivals, though they may also sanction first-team departures to help balance the books. Below, we break down how the remainder of the transfer window could play out.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Final piece of midfield puzzle

United have been drawing up a shortlist of midfielders to fill the remaining slot alongside Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. Much will hinge on whether the asking price is agreeable, however, as the club will not be pushed into overpaying.

‌



Marcus Rashford will have to confront awkward Man Utd reality when he returns to Old Trafford READ MORE :

Mateus Fernandes shows Man Utd what they're missing with screamer on Spurs debut READ MORE :

Real Madrid and French midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni, 26, seems to be the missing piece of the puzzle for Carrick, although it largely depends on Real Madrid's willingness to do business. However, a tough round of negotiations this summer would be small change to pay for a player of such quality, and one who could provide steel to United's engine room.

View 5 Images Manchester United are keen on Aurelien Tchouameni (Image: Getty Images)

The Sun have reported that Los Blancos are willing to part with the Frenchman this summer, with United said to have ‘recently enquired’. Madrid are also believed to be interested in Manchester City's Rodri, therefore paving the way for Tchouameni to leave the Bernabeu and become United's next midfield star.

‌



Rashford decision reached

The burning question remains what lies ahead for Marcus Rashford. The England international is still a United player after Barcelona allowed a purchase option to lapse, though a departure remains a possibility.

Several wide forwards have already been linked with the club. Crysencio Summerville now appears destined to move abroad, while concrete noise surrounding other targets has been relatively sparse of late.

View 5 Images Marcus Rashford could yet play a part for Man Utd next season (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The easiest decision for United is to simply keep Rashford. The 28-year-old was in fine form for the Catalan giants last season and has a solid working relationship with Carrick. The England star's United fallout was said to stem from a rocky relationship with former boss Ruben Amorim.

With Amorim long gone, the path is clear for Rashford to reignite his United career. He would represent a ready-made option for United as an attacking force, with alternatives going for sky-high prices this summer.

Full-back reinforcement

With United in need of support in wide areas and in defence, there is one option that seems ideal for the Red Devils: Djed Spence. The Tottenham Hotspur full-back is coming off the back of a stunning World Cup for the Three Lions.

‌



View 5 Images Djed Spence became England's unsung hero (Image: Getty Images)

The 25-year-old slotted in both at left-back and right-back during this summer's tournament, proving his flexibility. Inter Milan are believed to be in the running to sign the defender, with a price tag of around £25m being touted.

While it's a gamble, given that Spence only became a Premier League regular over the last two seasons, his versatility could be key to Carrick's squad rotation.

‌



£50m raised for signings

While question marks hang over Rashford's future, there is greater clarity on potential departures elsewhere. Joshua Zirkzee is amongst those who could generate a reasonable fee should a suitable buyer emerge, though perhaps falling short of the £35m United paid Bologna.

Two of United's reserve goalkeepers also appear set to depart. Altay Bayindir is expected to head back to Turkey, while Radek Vitek has already made clear his desire for regular first-team football, meaning a move away from Old Trafford beckons.

View 5 Images Joshua Zirkzee is one player who could leave Manchester United this summer. (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Decisions are yet to be made on others, including Toby Collyer. Nevertheless, a string of sales could generate as much as £50m.

That money could enable Carrick to bring in an additional striker to the squad. Ideally, this would be someone content with a squad role, with Benjamin Sesko continuing to spearhead the attack this season.

Full squad list

Goalkeepers: Lammens, Darlow, Heaton

‌



Defenders: Dalot, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez, Shaw, Spence, Dorgu

Midfielders: Mainoo, Mount, Fernandes, Tchouameni, Santos, Tielemans

Forwards: Sesko, Rashford, Mbeumo, Cunha, Amad

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Yan Diomande informs Andoni Iraola of decision as Reds boss given £51million answer
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Yan Diomande informs Andoni Iraola of decision as Reds boss given £51million answer

Andoni Iraola's pre-season preparations at Liverpool has been dominated by transfer sagas

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is still searching for a marquee winger at Liverpool (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola's options to replace Mohamed Salah at Liverpool are beginning to thin. The Egyptian superstar departed Anfield at the end of the 25/26 season and his place on the right-wing has yet to welcome a successor.

‌



The £34million signing of Spain forward Victor Munoz last month has been the only new addition to Liverpool's attacking line-up. Speculation of moves for Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola has been strife, but further incomings have been lacking.

‌



There is just over a month until the summer transfer window closes and even less until the 26/27 season commences. Iraola could speed up his side's chase for forward reinforcements after he was told of Diomande's latest decision. Meanwhile, the Reds could fork out over £50m to solve one key issue.

‌



Diomande makes decision

View 3 Images Yan Diomande's future has become clearer (Image: Getty Images)

The transfer saga of Yan Diomande has dominated much of the summer and it could heading towards its conclusion. Real Madrid have entered the race for the RB Leipzig star and are reportedly confident of agreeing a deal for his services.

The Spanish giants have had a bid rejected of £85million for his services, but positive talks with the 19-year-old's camp has Jose Mourinho's side in the driving seat. Diomande has long been linked to Liverpool, who tabled an identical package to Madrid, which was swiftly rejected.

‌

Sports.title: Impressive Liverpool beat Sunderland in Iraola's first game in charge
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola won his first match in charge of Liverpool as his new side produced an impressive display to beat Sunderland 4-2 in their opening game of their summer tour of the US.

Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot at Anfield in June, will have been delighted with some of the football Liverpool produced in the Nashville heat, especially a fine team move that led to the opening goal for young midfielder Kieran Morrison after 13 minutes.

The Basque, like his opposite number Regis Le Bris, rung the changes after the first half, with Liverpool improving after the break to turn around a 2-1 deficit thanks to a characteristic Dominik Szoboszlai piledriver, followed by further strikes from fellow substitutes Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas.

However, there was one negative for Iraola, who saw stand-in captain and long-serving defender Joe Gomez forced off early on with what looked a muscle issue in an area of the team where Liverpool really could do without any injuries heading into the new campaign.

The key moments from Nashville SC Stadium

8: INJURY! A big worry already for Liverpool with captain Gomez down with an injury and this does not look good for the centre-back.

13: GOAL! The first goal of the Iraola era is scored by Morrison after a wonderful team move involving some impressive build-up from the likes of McConnell, Ngumoha and Elliott, who fed the midfielder in space on the right of the box and he then found the bottom corner with a low shot.

28: GOAL! Sunderland are level as McConnell loses possession deep inside the Black Cats' half allowing Le Fee to break upfield and as the Reds defence backed off, the playmaker fired an unstoppable effort past a helpless Mamardashvili from 25 yards.

49: GOAL! Sunderland have turned this one around to now lead after Frimpong lost possession in a bad area, with the ball then slipped through for Tuterov, with the half-time sub finishing confidently.

56: GOAL! It is now raining goals as Szoboszlai hits an absolute worldie to bring Liverpool level after an excellent break down the left involving Koumas and Kerkez and after Sunderland only half clear the danger, the Hungary midfielder lashes home an unstoppable volley from the left edge of the box.

72: GOAL! And now Liverpool are back in front as Ramsey feeds Chiesa in space in the box and from a tight angle and faced with the onrushing Moore to beat, the sub finds the back of the net from a tight angle.

85: GOAL! Liverpool score another excellent goal to surely wrap this game up as Sunderland initially give the ball away and Szoboszlai finds Koumas in the box and the sub does well to find the net with a confident finish.

'A lot of things to correct, but a good starting point'

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola:

"I think it was different halves. Especially, they were a lot stronger in the first half. We kind of balanced both teams, and you could feel the difference. A lot of things to correct, obviously, it's the first day.

"You could feel the heavy legs, the players have been training. So, we lacked some freshness. But it will give us a good starting point to improve things.

"Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe [Gomez]. We were happy because we were kind of going through all the training without losing any player. Unluckily for us, straight away we've lost Joe."

Lots of positives for Iraola to take

Sky Sports' Rich Morgan:

Lots of positives for Iraola to take from his first match in charge of Liverpool, starting obviously with the win, although this being preseason in many ways it was the performance of his players and how well they gelled at times that will have most pleased the new Reds boss.

Liverpool scored some eye-catching goals, the team got better as the game wore on, despite the heat in Nashville, and all 22 players used with be better for this first competitive runout of preseason.

Iraola sweating on nature of Gomez's latest injury

Sky Sports' Rich Morgan:

Iraola may have won his first match in charge of Liverpool, but there was some worrying injury news as Joe Gomez was forced off early on.

Image: Joe Gomez was substituted early on with an injury

The long-serving defender appeared to suffer a muscle issue and was replaced in the centre of defence by youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe just 10 minutes into the club's first preseason game of their summer tour of the US.

Gomez, 29, has a long history of injuries at Anfield, although Iraola will hope it is nothing too serious with Ibrahima Konate having left on a free transfer at the end of last season, while both Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet missed the game in Nashville also with injury.

Leoni, signed last year from Parma, will not be back to full fitness for at least a few months after suffering an ACL on his Reds debut last September, while Jacquet, who joined the club from Rennes this summer, missed the game with a minor knock having only just recovered from a shoulder issue.

Sports.title: Sheeraz escapes with narrow points win as he sets his sights on Canelo
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz escaped with a narrow points win, while Josh Kelly overcame a horror gash to his nose on the Anthony Joshua vs Kristian Prenga undercard in Saudi Arabia on Saturday.

Londoner Sheeraz, who sealed his first world title with a second-round stoppage win against Alem Begic to claim the vacant WBO super-middleweight crown in Egypt, defeated Germany's Simon Zachenhuber.

After a 12-round fight that ended with boos around the arena the judges returned scores of 114-114, 115-113 and 116-112, in favour of Sheeraz, who posed with Jacob Bank in the ring following his win.

"I am a champion in the division. I'm sure people are champing at the bit after [my] performance," said Sheeraz, who said he would be sat ringside on October 31 to watch Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez challenge for Christian Mbilli's WBC belt.

"I got the win, that's all that matters. I could make a million excuses. I'll be better in the next fight.

"I need a step up now, someone who will mentally present a challenge. I was switching off at times, I was too comfortable when I didn't have a threat in front of me."

Image: A bloodied Josh Kelly wins his IBF World Super Welterweight title contest against Caoimhin Agyarko

Josh Kelly overcame a horror gash to his nose as he secured a unanimous points win against Irishman Caoimhin Agyarko in an IBF Light-Middleweight title fight in Saudi Arabia.

Nicknamed 'Pretty Boy', Kelly was left bloodied as the pair clashed heads in the 11th round with the Brit's face left a mess.

But he did enough to get the win with scorecards of 115-112, 115-112, 114-113.

"I told Caoimhin, don't take it as a loss, take it as a learning. If he wants it bad enough, he will bounce back," said Kelly.

Agyarko said: "I thought I won it, but if it's not good enough for the judges, I accept that. I'm heartbroken, I wanted to make history. Josh Kelly is a class act, but I think he underestimated me a bit, there.

"Listen, it will come. I will be the first Black Irish world champion, there's no doubt about that."

After the bout, Kelly said he wants to face unified 154-pound champion Jaron 'Boots' Ennis.

Promoter Eddie Hearn, who represents both Kelly and Ennis, said a clash between the two in the States is now a real option.

"He's had a defence of the title and before that mandatory comes again, really you want to be looking at those big money fights and trying to roll the dice," Hearn said.

"I think that comes with 'Boots' Ennis. If I'm Josh Kelly I'm looking at the big payday out in America against 'Boots' Ennis. It's a three-belt unification fight. [WBC champion] Sebastian Fundora, all those guys."

Leopards head coach Adrian Lam praised the way his side came through, despite having to make changes during the match because of injuries.

"I thought we were resilient today and hung in there and played really well," said Lam, who confirmed Frankie Halton suffered a suspected torn pectoral muscle which could rule him out for the rest of the season.

"The first half was awesome and we left some tries out there as well, but I though we were physical and we were up for it."

Warrington boss Sam Burgess felt his team deserved more.

"It is one of those games. I thought the scoreline probably didn't reflect the game or how tight the game was," Burgess said on Sky Sports.

York were back in it again when Scott Galeano forced his way over in the corner for an unconverted try, but Lolohea put Wrench in and Flanagan added the two points to give Huddersfield breathing space.

They increased their lead to 24-10 when Flanagan converted a sniping Zac Woolford score, but Jordan Thompson and Inman both crossed in quick succession, with Bennison taking the home side to within two points as a dramatic fightback came up just short.

Catalans hold on for derby win away to Toulouse

Tommy Makinson scored two tries as Catalans Dragons ended a four-match losing run with a scrappy 18-16 win away to Toulouse.

On a rain-soaked evening at Stade Ernest-Wallon, John Cartwright's side turned the tables on their French rivals following a 60-18 drubbing on Magic Weekend.

Makinson collected a high kick a Toby Sexton and used the soggy conditions to skid over the line in the 14th minute after Toulouse took an early lead through Jake Shorrocks' penalty.

Sports.title: Joshua devotes win to late friends as 'lovely treat' of Fury fight looms
Sports.content:
An emotional Anthony Joshua remembered his late friends as he staved off a seismic shock against Kristian Prenga to rubberstamp a fight with Tyson Fury that he says will be a "lovely treat" for fans.

Joshua knocked out Albanian heavyweight Prenga in the second round in Jeddah on Saturday night, after twice being floored himself in the first, including just 20 seconds into the contest.

The British star displayed tremendous character to battle back from the brink of defeat, a trait he has had to show in abundance since the deaths of team members Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele in a car crash in December in which he was a passenger.

Image: Joshua was sensationally knocked down by Albanian Prenga inside 20 seconds of their clash in Saudi Arabia

Speaking after overcoming Prenga, Joshua told DAZN: "It's more than punch power. That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina, that was the families. It hurts to even talk about it.

"It has been tough. It's my brothers. I don't want to talk about it."

Joshua: I respect everything Fury has done

Joshua was able to discuss Fury, with the British boxers now set to end over a decade of circling each other by locking horns in November, with America seemingly the most likely destination.

Fury beat Polish veteran Mariusz Wach in his own tune-up fight in Thailand on Friday.

AJ added of his countryman, who did not head to Saudi Arabia for a face-off with his rival: "I am going to rip his heart out. I am the meanest and most vicious champion there has ever been!

Image: Joshua celebrates after his second-round KO of Prenga in Jeddah on Saturday night

"All jokes aside, I respect everything he has done and achieved but we are here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat.

"I've learnt I can't be stopped. I won't be stopped and I won't be denied. We're here and we're coming. Trust me."

'No one can imagine what Joshua has been through'

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn confirmed that contracts have been signed for the blockbuster showdown before going on to praise his fighter's "astonishing" return to the ring after the "grief and pain" he had to deal with following the car crash shortly before Christmas.

Hearn said of Joshua on DAZN: "To be honest with you, tonight is all about the strength AJ has showed to even be here tonight - and the strength in that fight.

"No one can imagine what he has been through in the last seven months. During the first round, I was thinking, 'we came back too soon'.

Image: Joshua was floored twice in the opening round but bounced back to win and stay in course for a clash with Fury

"I feel boxing once saved him and I feel like he needed boxing to help him get through this. That camp allowed him to focus while he was facing so much grief and pain.

"He is a strong man and he likes to deal with his problems on his own - I'm not saying that is the right way but that is his way to do it. To even be in the ring tonight was astonishing.

"When you go down a couple ​of times in the first round and you're looking like ​your career might be over, he had to go to the depths one more time to get ‌up and fight on."
