Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's astonishing letter congratulating Argentina on finishing second at the World Cup is LEAKED as FIFA president hails Lionel Messi and Co's 'professionalism' despite thuggish post-match antics
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's astonishing letter congratulating Argentina on finishing second at the World Cup is LEAKED as FIFA president hails Lionel Messi and Co's 'professionalism' despite thuggish post-match antics

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has shamelessly praised Argentina’s ‘professionalism’ in a tone-deaf letter to the nation's FA - despite launching an investigation into their behaviour after losing the World Cup final against Spain.

While congratulatory letters are customary after the World Cup, with all three medal-winning nations receiving one from Infantino, his choice of words is questionable.

In the letter - first leaked by the Argentine media and since verified by Daily Mail Sport - sent to the President of the Argentine FA, Claudio Tapia, Infantino thanked Argentina for their impact on a successful World Cup and applauded their professionalism.

‘Dear Mr. President, Yesterday, Sunday, July 19, 2026, at the magnificent New York New Jersey Stadium, Argentina won the silver medal of the FIFA World Cup 2026, after an exciting final against Spain,’ Infantino said.

‘I would like to reiterate my most sincere congratulations for this important new result for Argentine soccer.

‘The FIFA World Cup 2026 will remain in memory as an unforgettable celebration of football, marked by spectacular matches, the irruption of new promises, the presence of the great figures of the sport and the extraordinary atmosphere lived in stadiums full of fans.

Gianni Infantino handed Lionel Messi his silver medal alongside President Trump

Infantino watched the World Cup semi-final with Argentine FA chief Claudio Tapia

The Argentina squad turned their back as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy

Join the discussion Should teams showing poor sportsmanship still be praised for professionalism by football’s top officials?

‘The magnificent performance of the Albiceleste also contributed decisively to making this edition an exceptional event that captivated millions of football enthusiasts around the world.

‘Please send my sincere congratulations to all who have contributed to this magnificent result: to the players, to coach Lionel Scaloni, as well as to the coaching and medical staff and, of course, to the many fans who have accompanied and encouraged the team throughout the competition.

‘These victories are always the fruit of constant work, professionalism and attention to detail, but also of passion, commitment and love for this wonderful sport. All this augurs a very promising future and, without a doubt, will pave the way for new and great successes for Argentine football.

‘I wish you, dear Mr. President, all the best for the next competitions and I hope to see you again very soon. With all my friendship, Gianni Infantino.’

Argentina, who lost in extra-time in the final, frustrated opponents throughout the tournament with their anti-football style of play.

The 2022 winners failed to register a single shot on target in the final and following the defeat, they turned their backs as Luis de la Fuente’s side lifted the trophy.

Leonardo Paredes attacked Eric Garcia in a post-match fracas that also appeared to involve Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and assistant coach Roberto Ayala - an incident FIFA are investigating.

The final itself was packed with controversy. Lionel Messi attempted to con referee Slavko Vincic into sending Marc Cucurella off after the Spain defender covered his mouth while speaking to the official. Argentina had attempted a similar tactic on Jude Bellingham during their semi-final against England.

In that semi-final victory, Argentina were also guilty of frequent simulation and gamesmanship in a provocative display.

They also drew complaints from British dignitaries after celebrating with a banner reading ‘Las Malvinas son Argentinas’, which translates as ‘The Falklands are Argentine’.

Sports.title: 'Hurt' Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after surprise Commonwealth Games bronze: Star reveals family feud has taken its toll and admits he 'doesn't know what went wrong'
Sports.content:
'Hurt' Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after surprise Commonwealth Games bronze: Star reveals family feud has taken its toll and admits he 'doesn't know what went wrong'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

First came an apology. 'Sorry guys,' said Adam Ramsay-Peaty, as his voice began to tremble. He wiped away a tear from his face and stared at the Tollcross floor to find his words.

The bronze medal around his neck felt like a heavy weight. 'It's hard because I know how hard I've worked. I know the s**t I've been through, which is no fault of my own. It does take a toll.'

After standing upon the podium, the 31-year-old walked around the pool and stopped for selfies with his adoring fans. An Englishman has not received a reception like this in Glasgow for a long time.

He stopped to hug his pregnant wife, Holly – the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay – before kissing her pregnant stomach. They are expecting a daughter in December and, as the swimmer confessed, family life has changed his priorities.

'She's always super proud of me,' he said. 'As a father, it doesn't matter if you come home with the gold, as long as you come home with the teddy, which I did. That's what matters.

'As you can tell, the emotion is always something that I'm going to carry. I'm never going to be afraid to show weakness because it's so important for making stronger people, making stronger men, stronger fathers, stronger husbands.

'I think 'S**t, how have I worked so hard at this age?' - then you get a result like that. I'm better than that. Maybe it's because I've had two years out, but it does hurt. There's a lot going on in my head right now.'

Adam Ramsay-Peaty was brought to tears as he reflected 'I'm never going to be afraid to show weakness' after securing bronze at the Commonwealth games

Adam Ramsay-Peaty stopped to hug his pregnant wife, Holly - the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay - before kissing her pregnant stomach

The pair wed on December 27 last year at Bath Abbey

Ramsay-Peaty was chasing from the start. He was not the leader of the pack. Perhaps he will fare better over 50 metres but here, over two lengths, he finished almost three seconds off his world record.

Australian Sam Williamson won gold and 18-year-old Filip Nowacki, of Jersey, claimed a brilliant silver that bodes well for the future of British swimming.

'I'm not crying because it's a bronze instead of a gold,' said Peaty, choking up throughout. 'I'm crying because I know that swim could have been better. I don't really know what went wrong in these last two weeks but something isn't hitting right, whether it's pace or focus.

'I feel like I couldn't have put more in, so you ask, 'What's the point of all the 5.30ams. What's the point of all the metres every day? What's the point of feeling exhausted all the time? What's the point of saying, 'No' to all the family events because of training?' It's because you want excellence and that isn't excellence for me.

'I enjoy a scrap but I lost that scrap in the last 25 metres. That's sport. Most of the time I've won the scrap. For some reason, the Commonwealths is that humble reminder.'

The wedding stories, the family feud and the social media abuse have taken their toll. The pool should be his place of escape but he swam with the world on his shoulders.

'People who comment and read headlines have got to look themselves in the mirror. Ignoring that comes at a cost. That hasn't played a part in that result here but it has to stop. Do better. I don't want young Filip to go through that.'

Join the discussion Has obsession with gold medals made us forget the human cost athletes pay for success?

Ramsay-Peaty was overcome with emotion in the mixed zone reflecting on his bronze medal

Throughout his decorated career, Ramsay-Peaty has been so far ahead of the field that he has had to look in the mirror to find competition. He has broken 14 world records, asserting a similar dominance to Sweden's serial pole vault champion Armand Duplantis. Untouchables. Now people will ask if time is finally catching up with Britain's greatest swimmer.

Nowacki is still waiting for his A Level results but the schoolboy from Millfield has already beaten his idol's teenage records. In 2012, Jason Kenny beat Chris Hoy to become the top dog of cycling. Lamine Yamal overcame Lionel Messi in last week's World Cup final. Swimming insiders believe it is a matter of time until Nowacki pulls a similar stunt.

'For me, he's got a very bright future ahead of him,' said Ramsay-Peaty, whose gold earrings caught the light of the cameras. 'He's my favourite for the 200m. He's definitely got the speed and he's about 25kgs less! He's got many many miles ahead of him, whereas my miles are probably coming to an end. I guess two years isn't that long to try and find that in me.'

Side by side, they look like David and Goliath. Nowacki is five inches shorter and does not have the same popping biceps. Ramsay-Peaty changed the game with his powerful upper body stroke but Nowacki's strength is in his kick. He keeps his hips high and moves more gracefully than his senior, who forces his way through the water.

Nowacki will discover his maths, economics and physics exam results during next month's European Championships. Then he plans to enrol at Loughborough University, where he can master his craft in time for the LA 2028 Olympics. Major medals are in his sights, although Ramsay-Peaty is not ready to stand aside just yet.

'To be racing one of the best in the world – arguably the greatest breaststroker of all time – is very special to me,' said Nowacki, who won the world junior championships last year in a time of 2:07.32, which would have medalled in every senior Olympics, bar one

Ramsay-Peaty knows a promising swimmer when he sees one. He has already signed up Nowacki to his own agency and will continue to mentor his prodigy.

'If I compare myself to 2014, 12 years ago, it's very exciting where Filip and his career can go,' he said. 'It's sport, it's beautiful, but f**k me, it can hurt.'

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua pays tribute to his two best friends killed in a car crash as he returns to the ring for clash with Kristian Prenga
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua paid tribute to two close friends killed in a car crash in December as he returned to the ring for the first time since the tragedy.

Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele died while the car they were travelling in struck a truck on a road near Lagos in December. The pair were on holiday with Joshua after he beat Jake Paul in Miami.

The heavyweight boxer, who was also in the vehicle, was taken to hospital before being discharged and flying home to the UK - where he attended the funerals of his strength and conditioning coach Ghami and Ayodele, one of his trainers.

Returning to the ring after seven months of inactivity, Joshua beat Albanian Kristian Prenga by knockout in the second round - despite being knocked down twice himself in the first.

Fighting in honour of Ghami and Ayodele, Joshua paid tribute to his friends by having their names printed on his military camouflage trunks.

He also walked to the ring wearing a military-style jacket to match his camo shorts. The jacket featured a medal bar displaying the IBF, IBO, WBA, and WBO titles - which he previously held - alongside pennants bearing Ghami and Ayodele's names.

Meanwhile, ‘Latz x Sina, My Brother's Keeper, MBK’ was printed on the canvas in his corner.

Anthony Joshua wears jacket featuring medal bar with 'Sina' and 'Latz' pennants

Joshua's friends were honoured by having their names printed on the canvas

Asked about how he has been coping after beating Prenga, Joshua said: 'It's been tough,' before becoming emotional. 'That's my brothers. I don't want to talk about that.'

Speaking on DAZN, Matchroom Boxing chief Eddie Hearn added: 'Nobody can imagine what he's been through in that last seven months. In that first round, I thought we'd come back too soon.

'Boxing got him through. To even be in the ring tonight is astonishing. You don't know what he's been through. He had to go to the depths one more time to get up, like he has done the last seven months.'

In February, Joshua memorialised Ghami and Ayodele by having their names tattooed on his arm.

Oleksandr Usyk was ringside for the clash in Jeddah to support Joshua, whom he beat twice in world title fights. Usyk has been working closely with Joshua, supporting his training camp.

Victory for Joshua means he is on track to finally fight Tyson Fury in a long-awaited British heavyweight showdown.

Sports.title: Defensive signings are a MUST after Joe Gomez injury, young star who took his chance and forgotten man Federico Chiesa gives Andoni Iraola food for thought: THINGS WE LEARNED as Liverpool beat Sunderland
Sports.content:
Defensive signings are a MUST after Joe Gomez injury, young star who took his chance and forgotten man Federico Chiesa gives Andoni Iraola food for thought: THINGS WE LEARNED as Liverpool beat Sunderland

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Andoni Iraola era got off to a flying start in Nashville with a 4-2 thumping of Sunderland – though the injury to defender Joe Gomez may leave the new Liverpool manager pondering at what cost this win came.

Goals from teenager Kieran Morrison, stand-in captain Dominik Szoboszlai, returning loanee Lewis Koumas and Federico Chiesa helped Iraola to a win and pleasing performance over their fellow Premier League opposition.

But the win was somewhat overshadowed by the first-half injury of Gomez and the fact fellow defender Jeremy Jacquet sat the match out due to a fitness concern of his own. It makes the need for a new defender starkly obvious.

Reds expert Lewis Steele was in the city of cowboy hats, hot chicken wings and honky-tonk bars and brings you his key Tennessee takeaways...

Defensive reinforcements are a necessity

It was the sight that no Reds fan, or the transfer committee, wanted to see.

Just seven minutes into the Iraola era, he had his first injury casualty to deal with. Welcome to Liverpool, some may joke, given the well-documented problems with fitness across the board for the team last season.

Joe Gomez went down off the ball, holding what appeared to be a muscular problem. He had a grimace on his face and a look of resignation. The defender missed the majority of 2024-25 and was in and out of fitness last term as his career continues to be plagued by such issues.

The severity of the blow is unclear at this stage and his exit from the pitch may have been merely precautionary – but that does not matter given central defence is a problem area that Iraola noted unprompted in his press conference in Chicago earlier this week.

Joe Gomez was forced off injured just nine minutes into Liverpool's win over Sunderland

Jeremy Jacquet, the new boy signed from Rennes who is hoping to play a significant role this term, is not fit and sat out of this friendly. It is understood Liverpool are going carefully with the young Frenchman after he missed half of last season at Rennes, so want to ease him in slowly.

Jacquet’s last game was February 7 and, even if he was to be as good as everyone at the club hopes and expects him to be, he is still only 21 and needs to settle into the physical demands of English football.

Virgil van Dijk is not on this pre-season tour and has been given an extended break, given he played more minutes than any player in Europe last term. The Dutchman is now 35 and is heading into the final year of his contract.

The only other senior centre back is Giovanni Leoni, the teenage Italian who signed from Parma this time last year but only made one appearance in which he ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament and missed the remainder of the season. His recovery is going well but he is still out.

When he is back, his fitness will need to be managed carefully.

It is also worth recalling that Ibrahima Konate, who played 36 of 38 Premier League games last year, left for Real Madrid on a free transfer.

All of these ingredients add up to one conclusion: Liverpool simply must sign a new defender this summer. Failure to do so leaves them incredibly light in that area and it could cost them dearly.

Morrison takes his chance

Defence is not the only area of the pitch where Iraola’s men are light going into the new campaign, which means there will be chances for youngsters to step up.

It has been one of the key themes of pre-season given plenty of senior stars are absent from this trip, including Van Dijk, Alisson, Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister and new signing Victor Munoz, who won the World Cup with Spain. Which kids can step up?

Here in Nashville, it was Morrison who did just that. A goal in the first half was the highlight after Harvey Elliott – back after a forgettable year at Aston Villa – threaded a nice pass to Morrison, who cut in off the right flank and curled a shot into the bottom corner with his left foot.

Kieran Morrison scored Liverpool's opener in a 4-2 win against Sunderland

The 19-year-old, who can play across the forward line, had several other moments of quality and could have notched an assist or two if luck was more on his side.

Northern Ireland are trying to tie down the Manchester-born teenager, who has one senior cap for the national team (he needs to play three times to ensure England cannot poach him at a later date) – and this performance showed why.

He joined Liverpool as an Under-14, having spent eight years at Manchester United as a kid. With several gaps in the forward line – not to mention a Mohamed Salah-sized hole on the right – could Morrison step up?

We won’t get carried away based on one pre-season outing but he was the man of the match here in Tennessee and Iraola must have been impressed. Manchester United’s loss, it would appear, is Liverpool’s gain.

Which other kids stood out?

While the lack of defensive depth is a glaring issue and a worry for many, two who might be rubbing their hands are teenage duo Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who both played the majority of this match.

Ndiaye, 18, was signed from Senegalese side Amitie FC in January having caught the eye at the Under-17 World Cup. He is a physical unit, seems calm in possession and is left-footed, which always helps. He has made the first-team bench several times.

Next to him was Austrian youngster Ndukwe, also 18. Signed from Austria Wien in January, Ndukwe officially joined up with his new team this summer. The 6ft 6in defender is another identified by global talent-spotter Matt Newberry in an intriguing recruitment drive.

21-year-old James McConnell impressed in midfield for Liverpool

Both played well and may be needed this season.

Further up the field, James McConnell was impressive in midfield, Calum Scanlon caught the eye on the left flank with several energetic runs and Josh Abe, who only turned 16 earlier this month, had some nice touches.

Lewis Koumas took his goal with composure after a fine move starring also Dominik Szoboszlai, who was wearing the captain’s armband.

Chiesa shows Iraola what he can do

There are several notable shortcomings to Federico Chiesa’s game that have been well documented by fans. But one thing he has that could be desirable to Iraola is versatility.

He can play on the right wing, left or, as he did here, as a No 9. The Italian scored Liverpool’s third with a well-taken finish from a tight angle then he played a lovely round-the-corner ball in the lead-up to Koumas’s goal.

Chiesa has had a weird career at Liverpool. His first season was a write-off, pretty much, due to injury. The next campaign had some bright moments and big goals but, overall, he never earned the trust of Arne Slot.

Many expected he would leave this summer but is he worth keeping around due to his versatility? It is food for thought for Iraola.

Anthony Joshua fights back tears as he dedicates dramatic victory over Kristian Prenga to two best friends killed in car crash as he recovers from TWO knockdowns to win on return

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anthony Joshua knows better than anyone how quickly heavyweight boxing can tear up the script. And for a moment on Saturday night in Jeddah, it looked as though another shock was unfolding as the British heavyweight was dropped twice and wrestled to the canvas in a chaotic opening round.

But Joshua dug deep, weathered the storm and, after finding another gear in the second, produced a devastating combination that flattened Albanian heavyweight Kristian Prenga, leaving the 35-year-old sprawled on his back and bringing a dramatic end to a fight that had threatened to derail his comeback before it had even begun.

Although, when AJ's hand was raised, the victory itself almost felt secondary.

For the first time since returning to the ring, the grief that he had worked so hard to suppress finally appeared.

The former two-time heavyweight world champion appeared, perhaps for the first time in public, to let the emotions he had buried since Latif 'Latz' Ayodele and Sina Ghami's tragic deaths in a car crash in Nigeria last December finally surface.

Joshua admitted before the fight that he had spent months suppressing the pain of losing the two men - Latz, his strength coach, and Sina, his personal trainer - insisting he did not want to make their deaths about himself while their families mourned.

Yet, after completing the hardest comeback of his career, both physically and mentally, the emotion could no longer be contained. Joshua broke down during his post-fight interview when crediting his friends for getting him through the first round before quietly saying: 'I don't want to talk about it anymore.'

Anthony Joshua gave an emotional interview after beating Kristian Prenga in Jeddah

When AJ's hand was raised, the victory itself almost felt secondary

Joshua was overcome with emotion after the fight, going from a euphoric high to an emotional low within minutes

For months after the crash, Joshua lived with constant pain. Simply getting out of bed became a struggle. He spent two months gently pedalling on a stationary bike before learning how to balance on a stability ball as he rebuilt his body from the ground up.

While the mental toll must have been every bit as demanding, if not more.

That said, Joshua and Eddie Hearn never liked calling this his 'comeback fight'. Seven months out of the ring is hardly unusual for a heavyweight. He had never truly been away from boxing.

But in every way that mattered, this was a comeback.

Because making it back into the ring after losing two of the people closest to him was perhaps Joshua’s greatest challenge of all.

There were moments when returning to the ring did not feel important, or even possible. But eventually, boxing became part of the healing process.

And so, under the bright lights of the Jeddah Superdome and with Latz and Sina embodied on the canvas, Joshua walked back into battle carrying far more than the pressure of victory on his shoulders.

Prenga was never supposed to be the final destination. The Albanian was always viewed as the bridge to something much bigger.

From the moment the fight was announced, it was understood that the real prize was Fury later this year.

This was the tune-up. The opportunity for Joshua to shake off the ring rust, rebuild momentum and remind the heavyweight division exactly who he is.

That is not to say there was no danger. There always is in the heavyweight division and Joshua was reminded of that the hard way.

Prenga entered the contest with 20 knockouts from 20 victories and just a single defeat. The power was genuine. In heavyweight boxing, one punch can change everything, and for a moment it looked as though it might.

The Albanian dominated a chaotic opening round, dropping Joshua twice and threatening to rip up the script.

Joshua was knocked down twice in the first round

But Joshua recovered in the second round, knocking Kristian Prenga out

It's anticipated that Joshua will finally fight Tyson Fury after both heavyweights won their fights this weekend

But there are levels in elite boxing. Prenga had never shared a ring with anyone approaching Joshua's pedigree or experience, and once the former two-time world champion returned to his corner and received a stern dressing down from his coaching team, he emerged with renewed purpose.

Still showing signs of the defensive vulnerabilities that have haunted him throughout his career, Joshua nevertheless displayed the resilience that has defined his comeback. He turned the tide in emphatic fashion, unleashing a devastating combination to stop Prenga 2:43 into the second round.

When Joshua's hand was raised, the emotion he had worked so hard to suppress could finally be contained no longer.

He had warned beforehand that he had kept so much inside. He did not want to centre himself in a story that belonged to grieving families. He wanted to honour his friends privately.

Instead, he pledged lifelong financial support to both families and vowed to continue pursuing the dreams they all shared together.

Yet as victory was confirmed in Jeddah, it was impossible not to think of everything he had endured to get there.

This was never just another win.

But there was one person missing: Tyson Fury.

Only 24 hours earlier, Fury had fought Mariusz Wach in Thailand, going seven rounds before the veteran Pole retired on his stool in a non-televised contest.

All week Fury had insisted he would not be travelling to Saudi Arabia for Joshua's fight and, despite widespread expectation that he would make a late appearance, the former world champion stayed away.

His absence did little to dampen the belief that British boxing's biggest fight is edging closer, but it denied fans the image they have waited years to see.

After so many failed negotiations, collapsed deals and false starts, supporters had hoped to see Joshua and Fury stand face-to-face in the ring for the first time with both men coming off victories.

But experience has taught Joshua not to assume anything in heavyweight boxing.

His long-awaited showdown with Deontay Wilder appeared all but set before Wilder suffered a shock defeat by Joseph Parker in December 2023 on the very same night Joshua won, sending months of planning into the bin.

The heavyweight division has a habit of snatching away the fights everyone wants to see.

Joshua wore a jacket featuring a medal bar with 'Sina' and 'Latz' pennants

Joshua honoured his friends, Latz and Sina, who were killed in a car crash in December

That is why there will remain a degree of caution until the AJ vs Fury fight is officially confirmed.

Joshua and Eddie Hearn have already revealed that the contract stipulates any showdown with Fury must take place in the United Kingdom because, in their eyes, the biggest fight in British boxing history belongs on British soil.

As things stand, however, Turki Alalshikh and Netflix are understood to favour Madison Square Garden in New York.

That means the contracts will need to be renegotiated.

The expectation is that discussions between all parties will take place over the coming days as they attempt to iron out the remaining details.

For now, Joshua's focus was not on what comes next, but on what he had already overcome.

The tears in Jeddah were not for Tyson Fury.

They were for Latz and Sina.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty kisses pregnant wife Holly's baby bump as he misses out on gold and finishes in third place in the 100m breaststroke final at the Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty kissed pregnant wife Holly's baby bump as he missed out on his 33rd major gold medal as he finished in third place in the 100m breaststroke final at the Commonwealth Games on Saturday.

The 18-year-old from Jersey Filip Nowacki finished ahead of his idol in second, but gold went to Australian Sam Williamson.

Williamson finished in 59.17 seconds, while Nowacki was milliseconds behind at 59.34 and Ramsay-Peaty behind him at 59.65.

Despite her husband missing out on the gold, Holly was ever the proud wife as she packed on the PDA with Adam after the medal ceremony.

The swimmer sweetly kissed his wife's growing baby bump before breaking down in tears over his 'hurtful' loss.

He said: 'I'm never afraid to show emotion. It's important because it helps create stronger people, stronger men, stronger fathers and stronger husbands.

'This cycle especially, I've worked harder than ever. To get a result like that hurts because I know I'm better than that.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty kissed pregnant wife Holly's baby bump as he finished in third place in 100m breaststroke final at Commonwealth Games on Saturday

The couple packed on the PDA after the swimmer missed out on his 33rd major gold medal

Adam was the favourite to win the 100m breaststroke final at the Commonwealth Games but only managed to secure third place

'It's still very raw. I honestly feel like I deserve more. There's a lot of thinking to do, but it's too early to draw any conclusions.

'Maybe it was just an off swim. Maybe it's because I've been away from championship racing for two years. I honestly don't know.

'What's the point of all the 5.30am starts? What's the point of all the metres every single day? What's the point of being exhausted all the time, or missing family events because you have to train?

'It has to mean something. For me, that means striving for excellence, and today wasn't excellence. That's where the emotion comes from.

'The choices I've made over the last few months have been difficult. At the same time, I'm proud that I got here and that I didn't quit after Paris [Olympics]. I know I deserve more, and I know I can work for it.

'It's been two years since I've raced heats, semis and finals, so maybe it's just an adjustment. It's too early to know what I'm capable of at this stage, but I'm a fighter.

'We've got another opportunity at the Europeans in two weeks, and I do enjoy a scrap. I lost that scrap today, but that's sport. Most of the time I've won those battles – this time I didn't.'

However, reports of his strained relationship with his parents have clearly taken their toll on Adam, as he added that he can't continue.

He continued: 'Over the last couple of months I've had to make some hard decisions so I could focus on doing my job.

'I've had to ignore a lot of the rubbish people write online. Enough is enough. This goes beyond sport. It's about being decent people. We all have to do better.

'My wife will always be proud of me. As a father, it doesn't matter whether you come home with a gold medal, as long as you come home. That's what really matters.'

Ahead of the Games, Holly, who announced last month she is expecting a baby girl with Adam, couldn't contain her smile as she took her seat to watch her husband, 31, compete in the final.

Holly, who is the daughter of TV chef Gordon Ramsay, 26, showed off her blossoming baby bump in a simple black T-shirt and matching jumper.

His pregnant Holly Ramsay couldn't contain her smile as she arrived to watch husband Adam compete in the final

Following the race, Adam admitted he was disappointed in his result: 'I've worked harder than ever. To get a result like that hurts because I know I'm better than that. It's still very raw'

Holly looked so proud of her husband after the race

Holly showed off her blossoming baby bump in a simple black T-shirt and matching jumper as she showed her support to Adam

The couple hugged after the tense final

The couple packed on the PDA after the race

Adam sweetly kissed Holly's baby bump

The couple looked more loved-up than ever after tying the knot in December

Adam was seen getting ready for the final

During the heats on Friday, Adam won despite a 10-minute delay caused by a detached lane rope.

He posted the fastest qualifying time and advanced comfortably to the semifinals and then progressed through the semifinals to book his place in the final.

The three-time Olympic champion is taking part in his fourth Commonwealth Games having clinched his first medals as a 19-year-old in Glasgow in 2014.

Adam has described these Games as a 'full circle moment' as he looks to reignite his career.

A silver medal at the Paris Olympics in 2024 helped him refocus after a difficult 2023 in which he withdrew from a series of events in order to focus on mental health concerns.

His win in the 100m in 2014 began eight years of almost total dominance in the event. That streak came to an end in dramatic fashion in Birmingham four years ago when he trailed home in a shock fourth place in the event.

Adam told TNT Sports: 'Job done, really. We've got a busy two weeks coming up, so we're reserving energy where we can.

'Last time I was here, I was very young. We barely had any world records to my name, or known world records to my name, so it's been a very long journey.'

Ramsay-Peaty debuted his new name on his swimming cap at the Commonwealth Games as he hopes his new moniker will bring him luck.

The three-time Olympic swimming champion is using his full name for the first time to compete at a major championship after marrying TV chef Gordon Ramsay's daughter Holly last December.

Sadly his parents did not attend the wedding and are assumed to not be attending the Commonwealth Games amid a falling out. Adam remains estranged from them.

Join the discussion Should family come before sporting fame, even if it risks your career?

The daughter of TV chef Gordon Ramsay, 26, looked excited as she took her seat in the crowd to watch her partner, 31

Styling her dark tresses loose, the star wore a radiant palette of makeup and accessorised with a simple cross necklace

The pregnant influencer was spotted staying hydrated in the crowd ahead of Adam competing in the final after he won his heat on Saturday

Holly cheered on Adam from the crowd

Holly was all smiles as she chatted with friends in the stands

The 18-year-old from Jersey Filip Nowacki finished ahead of his idol in second, but gold went to Australian Sam Williamson

Adam debuted his new name Ramsay-Peaty on his swimming cap at the Commonwealth Games as he hopes his new moniker will bring him luck

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail revealed that Adam's pregnant sister Bethany – the only member of his family to still be in contact with the couple – has now sensationally fallen out with Holly.

Not only are they no longer communicating, but this time it is Adam who is stuck in the middle, trying (and so far failing) to mend fences. Read the full story here.

The roots of the family conflict go back to September 2024, when Adam and Holly snubbed wider members of the Peaty family by not inviting them to their engagement party.

Caroline, who spent years ferrying her son to early-morning training sessions, was also not invited to Holly's glamorous hen do at Soho Farmhouse in the Cotswolds, even though the bride's mother, Tana, and friends including Victoria, were at the extravagant bash.

Adam changing his name to Ramsay-Peaty and registering under the double-barrel surname for the Games in Glasgow is the latest blow for his estranged loved ones – especially as Ramsay is placed first before Peaty.

A source said previously: 'Adam may be rich but we have something that he hasn't and that is brains, loyalty, integrity and family.

'Money makes for a cold bedfellow. It can't hold you tight when things go wrong or when you have a bad day.'

They added: 'When you live to be famous you aren't living, you are playing a role. Fame is but fleeting but family is forever.'

Adam's heat was temporarily halted as he was on the blocks when a lane divider broke off, requiring an official to strip to the waist and enter the pool to reconnect it.

The athlete duly wasted no time in recording the fastest time of the morning, 59.46 seconds, with only two rivals, Australia's Sam Williamson and Filip Nowacki of Jersey, also finishing in under a minute.

Adam has described these Games as a 'full circle moment' as he looks to reignite his career.

The influencer announced last month she is expecting a baby girl with Adam

Sports.title: LeBron James handed major boost after 76ers move as two-time NBA champion reunites with star in Philadelphia
Sports.content:
LeBron James handed major boost after 76ers move as two-time NBA champion reunites with star in Philadelphia

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

LeBron James has received a major boost in his quest to bring a championship to Philadelphia, with two-time NBA champion Kentavious Caldwell-Pope preparing to join him with the 76ers.

Caldwell-Pope agreed to a contract buyout with the Memphis Grizzlies and plans to sign a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the 76ers after clearing waivers, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

The move reunites James with his former Los Angeles Lakers teammate, with whom he previously won the 2020 NBA championship inside the Orlando bubble.

The veteran star brings elite capabilities to a transformed Philadelphia roster, providing elite perimeter defense alongside proven championship experience.

Caldwell-Pope earned his second championship ring in 2023 as a starter for the Nuggets, proving his status as one of the league's most reliable shooting guards.

His arrival bolsters a loaded 76ers squad that has undergone a dramatic offseason overhaul to build an immediate title contender around Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

LeBron James has received a major boost in his quest to bring a championship to Philadelphia

Two-time NBA champion Kentavious Caldwell-Pope is preparing to join James with the 76ers

The acquisition comes just days after James stunned the basketball world by taking a historic pay cut, signing a two-year, $8 million veteran deal to join Philadelphia.

By accepting a salary below market value, James allowed the 76ers' front office flexibility to construct a championship-caliber supporting cast around their new core.

Caldwell-Pope's addition addresses a critical need on the wing, providing head coach Nick Nurse with an experienced lockdown defender capable of spacing the floor for Embiid and James.

With James, Embiid, Maxey, Jaylen Brown and now Caldwell-Pope in the fold, Philadelphia has firmly positioned itself as a favorite in the Eastern Conference.

As training camp approaches, the 76ers' aggressive summer spending spree signals a clear, all-in mandate to deliver the franchise's first NBA title since 1983.

Shortly after James' move to Philadelphia was confirmed, President Donald Trump launched an astonishing attack on the NBA legend.

On Friday, Trump was asked to weigh in on who holds the title of the greatest basketball player of all time.

'Michael Jordan's a guy that's a friend of mine, I've played golf with him,' Trump said.

The news comes days after James stunned the basketball world by taking a historic pay cut

The move reunites James with his former Los Angeles Lakers teammate, with whom he previously won the 2020 NBA championship

'He's a really good guy and I think LeBron is - maybe he's a racist, but maybe he doesn't like Trump, I don't know - but I only like people that like me, so I would say Michael Jordan all the way.'

The comments mark the latest chapter in a long-standing feud between the four-time NBA champion and Trump, which dates back to James labeling him a 'bum' in 2017.

James, 41, has frequently used his platform to criticize Trump, previously endorsing Democratic candidates and launching voting-rights initiatives across the country.

Their bad blood spilled into the public eye during Trump's first presidency after he withdrew a White House invitation extended to Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry over his hesitation to visit.

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy 'hit with £1.6million tax bill' as huge major earnings laid bare
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy 'hit with £1.6million tax bill' as huge major earnings laid bare

Rory McIlroy's major success this year has come at a heavy cost as the golf superstar's tax deductions from 2026 come to light

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy will pay the most of any golfer this year when it comes to his majors tax bill (Image: Warren Little/Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy made history in 2026 as he became just the fourth golfer to successfully retain the Masters title. However, his success at the biggest tournaments the sport has to offer has also led to some serious tax deductions.

‌



McIlroy, 37, concluded his major season on Sunday with a T40 finish in The Open at Royal Birkdale. The Northern Irishman struggled to come back following a particularly disappointing two-over-par first round, ultimately finishing nine strokes behind eventual winner Ryan Fox.

‌



That was still sufficient to bag around £52,000 in prize money, though nothing compared with his £3.4m winnings from adding a second Green Jacket. His second straight win at Augusta unsurprisingly accounted for the vast majority of his major money in 2026, which was also supplemented by his £478,000 winnings for a T7 finish at the PGA Championship.

‌



When you add in in his £97,000 reward for tying 32nd at the US Open in May, McIlroy's total major prize haul for 2026 amounts to almost £4m on the dot. However, calculations courtesy of golfclubs4cash estimate that also means he's paying the most tax of any golfer this year when it comes to the major tournaments.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

His total tax bill from those four competitions amounts to approximately £1,634,840, accounting for fluctuations in the dollar to sterling conversion rate. As such, he's expected to have handed back a little more than a third of his major winnings this year.

‌



Golf news: Rory McIlroy sends invite to Bryson DeChambeau as star withdraws from 3M Open READ MORE :

That leaves around £2.35m of McIlroy's earnings that he can take straight to the bank. However, that's in addition to the other £2.4m or so he's won on other PGA Tour events this year (or around £1.5m once you apply for the same tax rate on those earnings).

That amounts to an estimated total take-home sum of £3.85m from all PGA Tour events so far in 2026. Not bad for a season's work in which McIlroy de-escalated his activity to focus more solely on the major competitions.

View 2 Images McIlroy endured a disappointing Open Championship, tying for 40th as he registered his worst major finish of 2026 (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

‌



It's close at the top of the majors tax bill totem pole, however, as Wyndham Clark almost paid an identical sum. The American finished in second place on the list, having forked over an estimated £1,630,278 in deductions, just £4,000 less than McIlroy.

Clark, 32, won the US Open for the second time in his career to bag the £3.4m top prize. His T21 finish at the Masters also came with a £184,000 reward, though he missed the cut at both last weekend's Open and the PGA Championship.

Sky broadcasts more than 1,400 live matches across the Premier League, EFL and more with at least 215 live from the top flight alongside Formula 1, darts and golf.

Article continues below

It should come as a surprise to nobody that world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler also worked his way onto the tax podium. This year marked the first since 2023 that the Texan failed to win a major, though he placed top four at three (and T14 at the PGA Championship), leaving him with £3.4m in prize money and a tax bill of a little more than £1.4m.

Scheffler and Sam Burns (fourth) are the only names among the top six on the list who made the cut without winning a major. And while the tax costs may be a burden, McIlroy will know he's doing something right if he features among the leaders once more in 2027.

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Transfer target's club frustrated as price set for 'next Dembele'

Manchester United are looking to make further progress in the transfer market

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is still looking to strengthen his midfield (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are in the midst of a crucial transfer window as they look to capitalise on the momentum built under Michael Carrick. Returning to the Champions League means reinforcing the squad is a necessity, with the midfield still a priority position.

‌



United have already strengthened their spine with the arrivals of Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa. French middlemen Manu Kone of Roma and Real Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni are both on the radar.

‌



However, the pursuit of Alex Scott has been called off, with United refusing to meet Bournemouth's £70m valuation. Meanwhile, Marcus Rashford's next steps remain uncertain following Barcelona's decision not to trigger their permanent purchase option. As it stands, he could be reintegrated into the squad later in pre-season.

‌



Following a youthful side's handsome victory over Rosenborg on Friday, here's a round-up of the latest United news…

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Roma's frustration

Roma want to sell Kone to United sooner rather than later to avoid a heavy UEFA fine.

‌



Old Trafford is the France star's most likely destination this summer but frustration is reportedly growing in Rome over the slow pace of the transfer. Roma need to sell a player before the end of the month to comply with financial regulations and avoid a penalty of up to £12million.

Marcus Rashford sent Michael Carrick message as Man Utd icons agree on transfer priority READ MORE :

According to Corriere dello Sport , United still hadn't made a concrete offer and are 'moving slowly' over the signing. United were said to be preparing an offer of £42m, with Roma wanting closer to £50m.

However, with time against them, the Serie A club may have to lower their valuation, especially as United have shown they are not afraid to walk away from a transfer if the price is not right.

‌



View 3 Images Manu Kone's potential move to United isn't progressing quickly enough for Roma (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

Competition for 'next Demebele'

United are in a head-to-head fight with Everton for Bologna forward Jonathan Rowe.

The 23-year-old, whose style of play was once likened to current Ballon d'Or holder Ousmane Dembele, has been turning heads in Serie A since arriving from Marseille last year, having started his career at Norwich City.

‌



View 3 Images Jonathan Rowe is a man in demand (Image: Getty Images)

According to Corriere di Bologna, they want around £35m for the two-footed attacker, who is capable of operating on both flanks, with David Moyes' Toffees also holding a strong interest.

Rowe, who holds British-Jamaican citizenship, has played for England at various levels. He played a pivotal role during the 2025 European Under-21 Championship, coming off the bench to score the winner against Germany in the final.

Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Real Madrid's stance on selling Vinicius Jr as shock Tottenham deal emerges

Arsenal continue to build their squad for the upcoming 2026/27 Premier League season

View 4 Images Vinicius Jr could move to Arsenal this summer (Image: Lars Baron/Getty Images)

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their squad further before the new Premier League season begins. Mikel Arteta has made three signings so far with Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier joining earlier this summer.

‌



Christos Tzolis became the most recent acquisition, arriving from Club Brugge in a deal worth £34million. The Gunners aren't showing signs of slowing down as they now explore a deal to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid.

‌



The Yan Diomande saga is also heating up, with Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain and Real all interested. Arteta could make a shock move to bring Cristian Romeo from Tottenham to address some defensive issues.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has taken a look at the three major headlines coming out of north London.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal get two green lights to proceed with Julian Alvarez transfer in record-breaking deal READ MORE :

Vinicius Jr move explored

Arsenal are exploring a stunning move to sign Vinicius Jr. The Athletic reports that the Gunners have registered an interest in the Brazil international with the deal in its early stages.

‌



View 4 Images The winger could head to the Premier League (Image: Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Real do not plan to lose the winger on a free transfer next summer with just 12 months remaining on his deal. They are also not happy to pay Vini's loyalty bonus if he sees out the rest of his contract.

It is understood that no contact has been made between the clubs as of yet but the Arsenal hierarchy are happy to pursue the potential transfer.

‌

This news comes just days after Arsenal made enquiries to sign the 19-year-old after his impressive debut season in Germany. Diomande's performance for the Ivory Coast at the World Cup also bolstered his valuation but it looks like Real are the ones pushing forward.

‌



It's understood that their first bid was an initial £76.9m plus £8.5m in add-ons. Now, the Spanish giants are set to put in an improved offer and are confident of landing the winger.

Shock Spurs move

View 4 Images Cristian Romero could move from one end of north London to the other (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Arsenal have joined Chelsea in considering a shock move for Tottenham's Cristian Romero. Reports in Italy claim that both London rivals are interested in the defender, who is available for £42m.

Sports.title: Tearful Anthony Joshua can’t get words out as he pays tribute to late friends
Sports.content:
Tearful Anthony Joshua can’t get words out as he pays tribute to late friends

An emotional Joshua paid tribute to late friends Latif “Latz” Ayodele and Sina Ghami after a dramatic win on his return to the ring on Saturday night

View Image An emotional Anthony Joshua after defeating Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua fought back the tears after paying tribute to close friends Latif “Latz” Ayodele and Sina Ghami just moments after knocking out Kristian Prenga.

The former two-time heavyweight world champion was back in the ring on Saturday night - just months after he was involved in a tragic crash in Nigeria which resulted in the deaths of Ayodele and Ghami. Joshua's late friends were also apart of his closely-knit training team.

Joshua, 36, escaped death when the car he and three others were travelling in crashed into a truck on a Nigerian motorway back in December. But the brave Brit made an inspirational recovery and was soon back in action as he looked to make his all-British showdown with Tyson Fury official. The 'Gypsy King' got the job done on Friday night after forcing Mariusz Wach to quit on his stool behind closed doors in Thailand.

But 'AJ' nearly saw his fight with Fury slip away from him after he was dropped in the opening seconds by Prenga. The Watford native survived, but was dropped again before eventually making it to the second round. The 36-year-old would go on to knock the Albanian out towards the end of the second stanza following a brutal left hand.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
