World.title: 60% of Iraqis have access to safely managed drinking water
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Around 60% of Iraq’s population has access to safely managed drinking water services, according to data from UN-Water and the Our World in Data platform. The figures highlight both the progress Iraq has made in expanding access to clean water and the significant challenges that remain.

The data comes as more than 2 billion people worldwide still lack access to safe drinking water at home, underscoring the global scale of the water security challenge.

According to the report, Iraq’s 60% access rate places it below many developed countries but ahead of several developing nations.

Among the countries with higher access rates are:

Japan: 99%

Italy: 97%

Ireland: 96%

Iran: 94%

Meanwhile, Iraq outperforms several developing countries, including:

Guatemala: 49%

Ghana: 43%

Indonesia: 30%

Guinea-Bissau: 24%

The report notes that safely managed drinking water involves more than simply having access to a water source.

Under the United Nations’ definition, drinking water must come from an improved source, be available on the premises, accessible whenever needed, and remain free from contamination. These standards form part of Sustainable Development Goal 6, which aims to ensure universal access to clean water and sanitation.

The report highlights that most countries in Europe, North America, and Australia have achieved access rates close to or at 100%, reflecting decades of investment in water infrastructure.

By contrast, many low-income countries—particularly in Africa—continue to record access rates below 20% due to inadequate infrastructure, limited funding, rapid population growth, and the growing effects of climate change.

For Iraq, expanding access to safely managed drinking water will require continued investment in water treatment plants, distribution networks, sanitation systems, and ongoing maintenance of existing infrastructure.

The report emphasizes that improving access to clean drinking water delivers benefits beyond basic services. Reliable water infrastructure helps improve public health, reduces the spread of waterborne diseases, supports education, and contributes to long-term economic development. As a result, expanding access to safely managed drinking water remains a key priority for achieving sustainable development and improving quality of life.

World.title: Kuwait to reopen Abdali border crossing within 48 hours after drone attack
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) – Kuwait will reopen the Abdali border crossing with Iraq within the next 48 hours, Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Yousef Saud Al-Sabah announced on Saturday, stressing that a recent drone attack on the facility will not disrupt passenger movement or bilateral trade.

The announcement came during Al-Sabah’s visit to Iraq’s southern Basra province, where he met Governor Asaad Al-Eidani to discuss border security, bilateral relations, and regional developments.

Speaking after arriving at the Safwan border crossing, Al-Sabah said the Abdali crossing would resume operations within two days, allowing the movement of travelers and commercial goods between Iraq and Kuwait.

“The Abdali border crossing will reopen to passenger and trade traffic within 48 hours,” he said, thanking Basra Governor Asaad Al-Eidani and describing relations between the two countries as rooted in brotherhood.

He emphasized that Kuwait and Iraq would not allow attempts to create division between the neighboring states.

“Whatever happens, we will remain neighbors and brothers,” Al-Sabah said. “We will not allow anyone seeking to spread discord between Iraq and Kuwait, and we will work to stop any attempts to fuel tensions from the very beginning.”

The Kuwaiti interior minister confirmed that authorities are still assessing the damage caused by the drone attack, which targeted the Abdali border crossing on Thursday.

However, he stressed that the repairs would not delay reopening the crossing. “The damage is being evaluated and will be repaired as quickly as possible,” he said. “This does not prevent the crossing from resuming operations. Traffic must continue.”

According to Al-Sabah, the crossing will be reopened in time to facilitate travel for Iraqi visitors and Kuwaiti pilgrims heading to Iraq during the Arbaeen pilgrimage season.

Basra Governor Asaad Al-Eidani welcomed the Kuwaiti delegation, describing the visit as a message of solidarity between the two countries. “Iraq, after the fall of the previous regime, should be a country of peace and friendship for all neighboring nations,” Al-Eidani said.

He acknowledged that both Iraq and Kuwait have been affected by wider regional instability despite not being direct participants in the ongoing conflict. “Sometimes mistakes happen because of irresponsible actions by individuals,” he added. “However, those incidents should not affect the strong relationship between our two countries.”

Al-Eidani also said the visit demonstrated the commitment of both governments to preserving regional stability and strengthening bilateral cooperation. Kuwait’s Ministry of Defense confirmed on Thursday that the Abdali border crossing had been targeted in a drone attack.

Officials said the incident caused only material damage, with no casualties reported. Specialized teams were immediately deployed to secure the site and remove drone debris.

An Iraqi security source also confirmed that explosions were heard on the Kuwaiti side of the border, while Iraq’s Safwan crossing in Basra remained unaffected and security conditions there were stable.

Following the attack, Kuwaiti authorities temporarily closed the Abdali crossing as a precaution. The latest developments come only weeks after tensions between the two countries following the fatal shooting of Iraqi fisherman Najm Abdullah by the Kuwaiti Coast Guard in early July.

Surviving fishermen later told local media that they were detained in Kuwait for six days and alleged they were subjected to mistreatment during interrogation before being released through Iraqi diplomatic efforts.

The incident prompted Iraq’s Basra Provincial Council to call for Abdullah to be officially recognized as a martyr and urged stronger measures to protect Iraqi fishermen operating in regional waters.

Despite those recent incidents, Saturday’s meeting between Iraqi and Kuwaiti officials underscored both governments’ commitment to maintaining strong bilateral relations and ensuring that security challenges do not disrupt cooperation between the two neighboring countries.

World.title: Strait of Hormuz crisis reshapes regional trade as Iraq faces growing economic pressure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The ongoing disruption in the Strait of Hormuz is doing more than slowing maritime traffic. According to Iraqi economic expert Manar Al-Obaidy, it is fundamentally redrawing trade routes across the Middle East, shifting commercial activity away from the Gulf and toward the Eastern Mediterranean.

In an analysis of first-half 2026 trade data, Al-Obaidy argues that the crisis has accelerated changes in global supply chains, creating new winners while exposing structural weaknesses in Gulf economies—particularly Iraq, whose economy remains heavily dependent on oil exports passing through the strategic waterway.

According to Al-Obaidy’s analysis, trade between China and several Gulf countries has fallen sharply during the first six months of 2026. Trade with Iran declined by 60%, while Iraq recorded a 55% drop. Saudi Arabia also experienced a significant decline of 48%, reflecting the growing reluctance of shipping companies and importers to rely on routes exposed to security risks in the Gulf.

At the same time, countries positioned along alternative Mediterranean trade corridors have seen remarkable gains. China’s trade with Syria surged by 281%, while trade with Jordan increased by 30%, Egypt by 25%, and Turkey by 10%.

The figures suggest that companies are increasingly redirecting cargo through safer maritime and overland routes rather than relying on the Strait of Hormuz.

Al-Obaidy believes the changes extend beyond a short-term shipping crisis. He argues that the current trends raise broader questions about whether global trade is entering a long-term transition toward new East-West logistics corridors.

While security concerns remain the immediate driver, businesses may continue using alternative routes even after tensions ease because they provide greater predictability and lower geopolitical risk. That shift could permanently alter regional trade patterns, even if it comes with higher transportation costs.

For Iraq, the consequences extend far beyond reduced shipping volumes. The country depends on oil exports for more than 90% of government revenue, with most crude shipments traditionally passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Any prolonged disruption directly affects public finances, budget planning, and the government’s ability to fund salaries and infrastructure projects.

However, Al-Obaidy warns that a second, potentially more serious challenge is emerging. As Asian buyers diversify their energy supplies, China and India could increasingly source crude from Africa and South America instead of relying as heavily on Gulf producers. If that trend continues, Iraq risks losing market share in some of its most important export destinations.

The shift also threatens Iraq’s broader ambition of becoming a regional logistics hub. As cargo increasingly flows through Mediterranean ports and neighboring countries, Iraq risks being bypassed in emerging trade networks.

That could reduce opportunities to expand non-oil exports, attract logistics investment, and strengthen its position as a transit corridor linking Asia and Europe. Without strategic adjustments, the country could find itself marginalized in both energy markets and regional trade.

Despite the risks, the changing trade landscape also presents Iraq with opportunities if policymakers act quickly. Accelerating the Development Road Project could position Iraq as a major land bridge connecting the Gulf with Turkey and Europe, offering an alternative to vulnerable maritime routes.

Expanding rail infrastructure, modernizing border crossings, and improving customs efficiency would strengthen Iraq’s competitiveness as regional supply chains evolve.

At the same time, investing in the ports of Umm Qasr and Al-Faw, together with logistics zones and industrial parks, would allow Iraq to capture greater value from transit trade rather than relying almost exclusively on oil exports.

Diversifying export markets and encouraging domestic manufacturing would also reduce the country’s exposure to external shocks, while expanding renewable energy and natural gas production could lower dependence on imported fuel and strengthen long-term energy security.

Al-Obaidy’s analysis suggests that the Strait of Hormuz crisis is more than a temporary geopolitical dispute. Instead, it may represent the beginning of a broader realignment in global trade, one that favors flexibility, diversified transport corridors, and resilient supply chains.

For Iraq, the message is clear. The country cannot control regional conflicts, but it can decide how it responds to them. Whether Iraq emerges stronger or becomes increasingly vulnerable will depend on how quickly it adapts its infrastructure, diversifies its economy, and positions itself within the new geography of international trade.

World.title: Iraq seeks Iranian assurances for oil tankers as Hormuz crisis threatens state revenues
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has asked Iran to guarantee the safe passage of Iraqi oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, as ongoing maritime disruptions threaten the country’s oil exports and place growing pressure on government finances. The request was reportedly made by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi during his visit to Tehran on July 23, according to sources cited by the U.S.-funded outlet Alhurra.

The visit marked Al-Zaidi’s first trip to Iran since taking office in May and came just days after his official visit to Washington, highlighting Baghdad’s efforts to balance relations with both regional and international partners amid escalating tensions in the Gulf.

According to the report, Al-Zaidi asked Iranian officials to ensure the safe passage of tankers transporting Iraqi crude through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most strategically important shipping lanes. However, the sources said Tehran did not provide a clear answer, leaving the request without either formal approval or rejection.

Furthermore, the report suggested that Iran may be reluctant to respond positively because of Baghdad’s recent strengthening of ties with the United States. That includes the signing of several major agreements with American companies during Al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington, a development that could complicate Iraq’s efforts to secure Iranian cooperation on regional security issues.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran came only days after his July 13–18 trip to the United States, where he met President Donald Trump and announced a new strategic partnership between Baghdad and Washington. The U.S. visit was the prime minister’s first major international tour since assuming office and focused on expanding economic and security cooperation.

During the Tehran visit, Al-Zaidi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, and both sides signed several agreements and memorandums of understanding. At the same time, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi delivered what many observers viewed as a carefully worded political message, stating that Iran “does not need messages or intermediaries because circumstances are changing rapidly.”

Meanwhile, the Iraqi government rejected reports published by The New York Times claiming that Al-Zaidi had carried a U.S. proposal for a ceasefire to Tehran. Officials insisted that the visit was instead aimed at strengthening bilateral relations and protecting Iraq’s national interests amid growing regional instability.

The request to Iran reflects the growing importance of the Strait of Hormuz to Iraq’s economic stability. More than 90% of Iraq’s government revenue comes from oil exports, and the majority of those shipments pass through the narrow waterway before reaching international markets.

Before the latest maritime crisis, Iraq exported roughly 90 million barrels of crude oil each month through the Strait of Hormuz. However, shipping activity has declined sharply as security risks intensified. According to vessel tracking data cited in the report, only one oil tanker crossed the strait on July 23, compared with three the previous day, marking one of the lowest daily figures in months.

The report also noted that Iran has continued targeting commercial vessels with missiles, drones, and unmanned boats despite a memorandum of understanding signed with the United States in June. As a result, Washington has increased military pressure in an effort to safeguard international shipping routes.

The slowdown in exports is already creating wider economic concerns for Iraq. Reduced oil revenues could affect the government’s ability to finance public-sector salaries, maintain budget spending, and support essential public services, particularly if disruptions continue over an extended period.

In addition, the uncertainty has contributed to fluctuations in the Iraqi dinar against the U.S. dollar, while Iraq’s electricity sector remains under significant pressure during the summer months. Continued dependence on imported Iranian natural gas has also increased concerns over possible power shortages, especially as electricity demand remains high.

According to the report, many Iraqis have once again begun relying on family and tribal support networks to cope with worsening economic conditions. While those informal systems have helped communities navigate previous crises, analysts warn they may not be sustainable if the current situation persists.

Consequently, prolonged pressure on household incomes, combined with rising economic uncertainty, could increase public frustration and revive the kind of demonstrations Iraq witnessed during previous waves of economic and political unrest. For now, Baghdad continues to pursue diplomatic efforts aimed at protecting its energy exports while seeking to shield the country from the wider consequences of regional conflict.

World.title: JD.com partners with Iraq’s GINI to expand e-commerce offerings
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China’s JD.com has partnered with Iraqi digital commerce platform GINI to increase access to its goods in Iraq, marking the latest step toward developing the country’s rapidly expanding e-commerce industry.

The deal would integrate JD.com’s product catalog into GINI’s digital marketplace and the SuperQi app, providing Iraqi customers with greater access to items from one of China’s top online retailers.

The agreement aims to establish a direct supply chain between JD.com and the Iraqi market, thereby enhancing product availability and facilitating cross-border online buying.

GINI, an Iraqi digital commerce and market automation platform, combines merchants, delivery providers, and payment services in a unified ecosystem, allowing companies to manage sales, payments, and logistics.

JD.com, founded in 1998, is China’s largest retailer by revenue and one of the country’s leading e-commerce companies, with a vast logistics network that enables rapid order fulfillment across China and international markets.

The agreement comes as Iraq’s e-commerce sector grows, along with rising internet penetration, digital payment adoption, and government efforts to modernize the economy and encourage more private sector investment in technology and digital services.

Baghdad has increasingly pushed to recruit multinational technology businesses and digital commerce platforms as part of larger attempts to diversify the economy away from oil, generate private-sector employment, and enhance access to products and services via online markets.

World.title: Houthis say hit Saudi Arabia as Trump weighs harder Iran strikes
World.content:
Sanaa – Tehran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile attack on Saudi Arabia on Saturday as US President Donald Trump mulled fresh strikes on Iran in the deepening Middle East war.

The US military broke its daily announcement of fresh strikes on the Islamic republic on Saturday, following 13 nights in a row hitting military targets there.

Trump said he had not yet decided whether to launch major strikes on Iran, hours before the conflict widened across the region with Yemen’s Houthi rebels claiming a missile attack on the southern Saudi city of Jizan.

The Houthis had accused US ally Riyadh of a “dangerous escalation” after it struck military targets belonging to the group on Friday, following the rebels announcing a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hitting its ships in the Red Sea.

The flare-up marks a new front in a war that has engulfed the region following US-Israeli strikes on Tehran in February, and comes on top of Iran’s parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh’s only other maritime route.

Riyadh did not immediately comment on the Houthis’ Ansarollah media post on Telegram on Saturday that a “Yemeni missile strike” had sparked fires in Jizan.

But Riyadh’s civil defence agency issued brief warnings to residents in the city, as well as Yanbu, early on Saturday.

The warning came after the Saudi-led coalition said Friday it had hit Houthi sites and destroyed targets threatening commercial vessels in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping.

A Yemeni security source told AFP a naval base in the port city of Hodeida and a military camp on Kamaran island were among the Saudi targets.

The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea.

– ‘Tipping point’ –

The escalation came after Trump said he would hold off on a major operation as Tehran was now getting “serious” in talks with Washington.

“No I haven’t,” Trump told journalists in the Oval Office when asked if he had made a decision on hitting Iran hard, for now dialing back reports that he was increasingly frustrated with the war and mulling a large-scale military operation.

“Look, we’re talking to them right now. I think they’re getting more and more serious as the days go by, for maybe the obvious reason.”

Trump said Iran had a choice between making a deal or facing a “much higher level” of strikes, after nearly two weeks of US attacks that have left a ceasefire in tatters.

The war that Trump once predicted would last four or five weeks is now nearing its fifth month, and is weighing on the Republican’s approval ratings ahead of crucial US midterm elections in November.

Trump added that he did not know what the “tipping point” would be for a decision, but reiterated that his red line would be if Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon.

The United States says it is carrying out the strikes to stop Iran closing the crucial Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has responded with strikes on US bases that have killed four service members.

The Iranian military said Friday it had carried out attacks targeting US military assets in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, meanwhile, said they had targeted an Amazon data center in Bahrain, according to state media, though neither the US tech giant nor Bahrain has commented on the claim.

There was also no confirmation from the United States of any targeting of its facilities or personnel.

In Bahrain, sirens sounded again early Saturday, the interior ministry said, urging residents to take shelter.

– ‘I trust them’ –

Trump also insisted Russia and China were not arming Iran, despite reports both were feeding Tehran intelligence to target US forces.

“President Xi (Jinping) said he will not partake, and President (Vladimir) Putin said the same thing… I trust them,” Trump told reporters.

“I don’t think they’d want to have me disappointed.”

On the diplomatic front, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in Kyrgyzstan.

Wang called for a resumption of negotiations and the implementation of a memorandum of understanding aimed at easing tensions in the Middle East and the Gulf region, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.

That referred to the preliminary deal aimed at ending the war which has collapsed as the foes fight to break a deadlock over the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia as conflict deepens
World.content:
Sanaa – Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia on Saturday, hours after vowing to retaliate against the kingdom for attacks as the Middle East war expanded.

Riyadh struck Houthi military targets in Hodeida on Friday, with rebel media reporting two wounded after the Yemeni group announced a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hit its ships.

The flare-up marks a new front of the war that has engulfed the region following US-Israeli strikes on Tehran in February, and comes on top of Iran’s parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh’s only other maritime route.

The rebels had accused Saudi Arabia of a “dangerous escalation” and said its actions “will not go unanswered”.

The Houthis’ Ansarollah media said on Telegram early Saturday that a “Yemeni missile strike” had sparked fires in the southern Saudi city of Jizan on the Red Sea.

Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the claim.

But Riyadh’s civil defence agency had issued brief warnings to residents in Jizan and Yanbu early Saturday for “potential danger”, only to lift the warnings minutes later.

Similar warnings have been issued in the past when missiles or drones were fired at the kingdom.

The warning came after the Saudi-led coalition said Friday it had hit Houthi sites and destroyed targets threatening commercial vessels in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping.

A Yemeni security source told AFP a naval base in the port city of Hodeida and a military camp on Kamaran island were among the Saudi targets.

The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea.

– Blockade –

The Yemeni security source, who requested anonymity, said the Saudi strikes targeted a telecommunications building near Hodeida’s port and a naval base at Ras al-Kathib in Hodeida.

The Houthis’ al-Masirah television channel said two people were wounded — a worker in Hodeida and a woman on Kamaran island.

It said a telecoms building had been hit in Hodeida.

On Monday, the rebels had warned in a radio message to ships that they would target vessels “belonging to (the) Saudi enemy” that do not comply with their blockade.

Saudi state media cited a transport authority official on Friday as saying “the vessel (NCC MASA), belonging to a Saudi company, was targeted while sailing in the Red Sea today… resulting in minor damage to the vessel’s hull”.

The ship resumed its course, the SPA added.

Red Sea access has become vital for Saudi Arabia to keep shipping oil as traffic in Hormuz is disrupted.

In April and May, all of Saudi seaborne crude exports departed from its Red Sea port of Yanbu, according to Kpler data. It represented 92 percent of all seaborne crude exports in June and 78 percent so far in July.

The Houthis have been at war with Yemen’s government since 2014, in a conflict that has killed hundreds of thousands of people.

The recent exchange of fire threatens a 2022 truce that has held despite expiring.

World.title: Mixed day for global equities as oil prices retreat
World.content:
New York – The main international oil contract Brent North Sea fell back under $100 Friday after surging past the key milestone the previous day on escalating Middle East strikes, helping US and European stock markets stabilize.

Brent dropped about four percent to under $97 a barrel, having soared seven percent Thursday. The key US contract, West Texas Intermediate, declined more than three percent after having gained more than six percent on Thursday.

The sizeable jumps had come after Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck oil tankers in the Red Sea, potentially opening a new front in the Middle East war.

Despite the United States launching fresh strikes Friday on Iran, there was relief on markets that some ships were still able to pass through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a crucial passage into the Red Sea.

“Ships with Saudi crude are still crossing…so for now, it is not a full blockade, reducing a bit the risk of an even tighter oil market,” Giovanni Staunovo, a commodities analyst at Swiss bank UBS, told AFP.

A Houthi spokesman said Friday that the rebels were not blocking traffic through the strategic strait.

On Wall Street, both the Dow and S&P 500 rose, while the Nasdaq retreated again, with semiconductor shares enduring another round of selling.

Angelo Kourkafas of Edward Jones described markets as buffeted by uncertainty over unpredictable geopolitical events and questions about how the Federal Reserve will weigh the latest jump in oil prices.

At the same time, “the bar is set high and there is also some skepticism about the sustainability” of this week’s lofty corporate earnings, Kourkafas said.

David Morrison at Trade Nation said expectations that the US Federal Reserve could hike interest rates at its meeting next week have risen from 13 percent last week to 30 percent currently.

“Perhaps more seriously, the CME’s FedWatch Tool shows a 90 percent probability of at least one 25-basis point rate hike before year-end,” he said.

Besides the Fed, next week’s schedule includes another heavy calendar of quarterly results featuring tech giants such as Amazon and Apple, as well as major industrial players including Boeing and Ford.

With tech stocks not as predominant in Europe, that region’s main stock markets advanced on Friday.

Asian stock markets followed the sell-off Thursday on Wall Street as world markets were battered by a perfect storm of the resurgent Middle East war, the spike in oil prices and concerns about the artificial intelligence boom.

World.title: 'Every misadventure by Pakistan will draw response beyond their imagination': Rajnath Singh on Vijay Diwas
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Defence minister

on Sunday issued a stern warning to Pakistan, saying every "misadventure" would invite a response "beyond their imagination".

While addressing the nation on the 27th

at the Kargil War Memorial in Drass, Ladakh, he said, ""Our intention is clear.

There will be no talks with Pakistan. If there are any talks, they will be only on PoK, which is a part of India and illegally occupied by Pakistan.

"

"At present, Pakistan has made

a part of its government policy, and the distinction between the military and militants has completely disappeared there. The army not only protects terrorist organizations but also works closely with them. Therefore, during Operation Sindoor, we made it clear that India will no longer view terrorists and the governments that support them separately," he added.

Drawing a sharp contrast between India and Pakistan, Defence minister Rajnath Singh further said that India is focused on innovation, technology and development, while Pakistan continues to promote infiltration and terrorism.

"India is pursuing innovation, while Pakistan is seeking new ways of infiltration. While India is designing ships, Pakistan is engaged in designing terrorism," he said.

In his address while reiterating India's firm stand on Pakistan, Rajnath Singh said there would be no talks with Islamabad, except on Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), which he described as an integral part of India under illegal occupation.





"Our intention is clear. There will be no talks with Pakistan. If there are any talks, they will be only on PoK, which is a part of India and illegally occupied by Pakistan."

'Indebted to all those valiant soldiers'

In an X post on Sunday, Singh wrote, "On the occasion of Kargil Vijay Diwas, I pay my deepest respects to all the brave soldiers who laid down their lives in the defense of our motherland. The nation will forever remain grateful and indebted to all those valiant soldiers who demonstrated extraordinary valor on the inaccessible peaks of Kargil in 1999."

He added that the

Indian Army

's indomitable courage, sacrifice and unwavering resolve would continue to inspire future generations with patriotism, dedication to duty and "the spirit of offering everything for the motherland."

'Army fully prepared'

Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday asserted that the Indian Army is "fully prepared" to tackle any challenge, saying the "intent of infiltrators" has remained unchanged since the 1999 Kargil conflict.

Speaking to Army personnel at a Shaurya Bhoj in Dras on Kargil Vijay Diwas, after attending Shaurya Sandhya at the Kargil War Memorial, Singh paid tribute to the soldiers who laid down their lives during the 1999 war and said that while India celebrates their sacrifice, the country must remain vigilant against continuing threats such as proxy war and cross-border infiltration.

"We have to remember that even today challenges have not reduced; the intent of infiltrators hasn't changed, and even today it adopts tools like a proxy war or infiltration," Singh said, in an apparent reference to Pakistan.

"I am fully assured that our Army is fully prepared for any such challenges," he added.

Observed every year on July 26, Kargil Vijay Diwas commemorates India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War, honours the 527 soldiers who laid down their lives during Operation Vijay and pays tribute to the courage of thousands who fought in one of the world's toughest battlefields.

World.title: Pradhan offered to quit on first day of student protest? BJP leader's big claim
World.content:
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday after which the CJP withdrew its 36-day agitation.

NEW DELHI: Hours after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister amid the nationwide protest over the NEET paper leak, Madhya Pradesh minister Kailash Vijayvargiya claimed that Pradhan had offered to step down on the very first day of the protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.Vijayvargiya, speaking to news agency PTI in Indore on Saturday, said Pradhan had informed the BJP leadership that he was willing to resign if the party believed it was necessary."On the first day, as soon as the student agitation began, Pradhan had told the BJP president that if he felt it was necessary, he was ready to resign as education minister," Vijayvargiya said.According to the BJP leader, the party president asked Pradhan not to submit his resignation at the time, saying no decision had been taken and advising him not to discuss the matter further.He claimed that Pradhan stepped down immediately once the party later decided that he should resign.Vijayvargiya also defended the former education minister, saying he had carried out every responsibility entrusted to him with honesty and dedication.Referring to Pradhan's resignation, he alleged that the move had thwarted attempts by "foreign forces" to destabilise India by fuelling unrest similar to that witnessed in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka."Pradhan's resignation has foiled the designs of those foreign forces that wanted to destabilise India by spreading violence, as happened in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka. I congratulate him for what he has done," he said.Pradhan resigned on Saturday, following which the Cockroach Janta Party withdrew its 36-day agitation that had mobilised lakhs of people over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations and the NEET paper leak.After Pradhan resigned, senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi has been entrusted with the additional charge of the Union Ministry of Education, succeeding Dharmendra Pradhan, who resigned on Saturday, taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak controversy.The appointment comes at a crucial time for the ministry, which is implementing a series of examination reforms following the controversy. Along with the Education Ministry, Joshi will continue to handle his existing portfolios of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and New and Renewable Energy.Soon after assuming the additional responsibility, Joshi said he accepted the role with "a sense of duty and humility" and pledged to work towards further strengthening India's education system."I accept this responsibility with a sense of duty and humility. I am thankful to the Prime Minister. In the last four to five years, Dharmendra Pradhan implemented the National Education Policy and several important initiatives. Under the guidance of the Prime Minister, I will work to the best of my ability and fulfill my responsibilities with dedication," he said.

World.title: Nepal eases rules on Indian currency, allows Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes up to Rs 25,000
World.content: NEW DELHI: Nepal has eased restrictions on the movement of Indian currency, allowing Indian and Nepali citizens to carry Indian Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes issued after November 9, 2016. According to the Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), the permitted notes can be carried into or taken out of Nepal up to a limit of Rs 25,000 per person.According to news agency PTI, the revised rules permit citizens of both countries to bring the approved currency notes into Nepal, carry them within the country, or take them out, subject to existing regulations.In its latest notice, the NRB clarified that older Indian currency notes issued before the 2016 demonetisation period will continue to remain prohibited in Nepal.The NRB added that only redesigned Indian Rs 500 notes and Rs 200 notes introduced after November 9, 2016, will be permitted under the new arrangement.The central bank had initially published the provision in the Nepal Gazette on February 11. However, it issued another notice on Thursday to clarify the implementation process and address concerns over cross-border currency movement.NRB spokesperson Guru Prasad Paudel said Nepali citizens would not be allowed to bring Indian currency into Nepal from countries other than India.He also clarified that Indian currency taken out of Nepal by Nepali citizens could only be carried to India and not to any third country.The new provision would facilitate Indian tourists visiting Nepal and Nepalese nationals engaged in trade and business with India, said Paudel.The rule change comes after years of restrictions introduced following Indiaâs demonetisation announcement on November 8, 2016, when the old Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes were withdrawn from circulation.Following the move, Nepal had restricted the use and movement of those discontinued Indian notes due to concerns over their circulation and financial impact.The latest decision affects cross-border transactions between India and Nepal, which share an open border and extensive economic links. India remains Nepalâs largest trading partner and a key source of tourists, while thousands of Nepali citizens travel to India for work, education and business.The NRB also stated that Nepali citizens and foreign visitors can bring foreign currency worth up to $5,000, or its equivalent in other currencies, into Nepal without filing a customs declaration. Amounts above that threshold must be declared upon arrival.

World.title: 'Gratitude to brave soldiers': PM Modi pays tribute to Kargil heroes on 27th Vijay Diwas
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Sunday paid tribute to the soldiers of the

on the occasion of the 27th

and remembered their role in safeguarding the country's sovereignty.

"On Kargil Vijay Diwas, our nation expresses gratitude to the brave soldiers for their extraordinary courage and commitment towards securing India.

Their valour in the face of the most formidable conditions will forever remain a source of national pride.

Their unwavering patriotism and devotion to duty will continue to inspire generations," the Prime Minister said in a post on X.

India is observing the 27th anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas, commemorating its victory in the 1999 Kargil War. The day marks the successful culmination of Operation Vijay and honours the 527 soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice while driving Pakistani intruders out of strategic heights in the Kargil sector.

The Kargil conflict, fought between May and July 1999, remains the only conventional war between two nuclear-armed neighbours. The battles were fought across the rugged mountain terrain of Kargil, Dras, Batalik, Mushkoh and Kaksar in Ladakh at altitudes exceeding 5,000 metres.

Despite freezing temperatures, low oxygen levels and heavily fortified enemy positions, Indian troops recaptured the occupied peaks without crossing the Line of Control, earning global recognition for their professionalism and military restraint.





Over the years, Kargil Vijay Diwas has come to symbolise not only India's military victory but also a defining moment that reshaped the country's defence preparedness, strategic planning and national security framework.

Union home minister

Amit Shah

also paid tribute to the soldiers, describing Kargil Vijay Diwas as a symbol of the Indian Army's indomitable courage and extraordinary valour.

"'Kargil Vijay Diwas' stands as a symbol of the Indian Army's indomitable courage and extraordinary valour.

In 1999, despite facing adverse conditions and enemy positions situated at high altitudes amidst the treacherous, snow-capped peaks of the Himalayas, our brave soldiers forced the enemy to their knees through 'Operation Vijay'. On 'Kargil Vijay Diwas', I pay tribute to all those brave sons who made the ultimate sacrifice to uphold the nation's integrity," Shah said.

Defence minister

Rajnath Singh

, who attended the Kargil Vijay Diwas commemorations at the Kargil War Memorial in Dras on Saturday, said the intent of infiltrators had not changed since the 1999 conflict and asserted that the Indian Army remained fully prepared to counter any challenge.

"We have to remember that even today challenges have not reduced; the intent of infiltrators hasn't changed, and even today it adopts tools like a proxy war or infiltration," Singh said in an apparent reference to Pakistan.

"I am fully assured that our Army is fully prepared for any such challenges," he added.

The defence minister also highlighted the government's focus on modernising the armed forces, saying sustained efforts were being made to equip the military with the latest technology and the best training.

Referring to the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, he expressed confidence that the Indian armed forces would emerge among the finest in the world.

Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha

Rahul Gandhi

also remembered the fallen soldiers, saying the nation would forever remain indebted to their courage, valour and supreme sacrifice.

"A humble tribute to all the brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice while defending India's borders, on Kargil Victory Day. The nation will forever remain indebted to your courage, valor, and supreme sacrifice," Gandhi wrote on X.

World.title: CRPF to do post-analysis of RAF action in NEET protests, says DG; 47 RAF personnel injured
World.content:
CRPF director general Gyanendra Pratap Singh

NEW DELHI: CRPF director general Gyanendra Pratap Singh on Saturday said the force would conduct a professional post-analysis of the action taken by personnel of Rapid Action Force (RAF), a unit of CRPF, against anti-NEET paper leak protestors, including during the July 20 march to Parliament.âNow, since agitation has been called off, and once assembled people disperse, we would make a professional post-event assessment, like we do after every major assignment, and then let you know of the view of force headquarters,â Singh told TOI on Saturday. This is the first official statement from CRPF in the wake of allegations that pellet guns were used against protestors during the July 20 march to Parliament.Three people have claimed to have suffered pellet injuries in the police action.At least 47 RAF personnel too sustained injuries, allegedly from violent elements in the protests.Sources said the post-event assessment by CRPF will go into all possible aspects of RAF deployment during the protests. This would include action taken by RAF personnel against the protestors, riot-control gear used by them and whether the ground situation justified it. It will examine if the RAF response was graded and in line with the standard operating procedures and riot control manual.An officer said the CRPF will also examine the provocation and aggression that the RAF personnel likely faced at the hands of external, motivated elements who may have infiltrated the protests.CRPF sources said of the 47 RAF personnel injured during the course of their deployment for protests in the Capital, six have sustained head injuries and four, fractures. An officer claimed RAF personnel were hit by protesters with iron rods, likely retrieved from damaged railings. The accounts of the personnel regarding how the injuries were sustained, will be recorded as part of the post-event analysis.Delhi Police had clarified that they do have any pump action guns (PAG), but these are part of RAFâs standard anti-riot gear, along with shock batons. The CRPF review will probe allegations of firing of pellets by any personnel on duty, and if such action was authorised, justified and part of a graded response.NEW DELHIPAG, commonly known as pellet gun, is classified as a 'non-lethalâ anti-riot measure. As per the standard RAF drill, it is to be used only as a second last resort, with police firing being the last. Any RAF anti-riot action should start with engagement with the protestors or unruly mob, followed by warning on public address system to disperse. If all this fails, water cannon or tear gas may be used. Pellet gun is the next level of force applied, and may be fitted with a muzzle deflector so that the pellets hit only the lower body, leaving vital organs unharmed.

World.title: Nepal seeks India's approval for biometric national identity card as travel document
World.content:
Nepal seeks India's approval for biometric National Identity card as travel document (ANI image)

Nepal plans to replace citizenship certificates

India reviews the proposal

The Kathmandu Post

Nepal has formally requested India's approval to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as an official travel document for cross-border journeys, alongside passports and citizenship certificates.At present, Nepali citizens travelling to India, particularly by air, must carry either a valid passport or an original citizenship certificate. Indian citizens entering Nepal are required to present either a passport or an original voter identity card with a photograph.However, Nepal's National Identity card contains biometric information, including fingerprints, facial images and iris scans. The programme was launched as a pilot in Panchthar district and among government employees in 2009.So far, more than 4.5 million Nepali citizens have received the card, while nearly 20 million applications have been submitted.The request comes as Nepal gradually makes the biometric National Identity card mandatory for banking, land registration, passport issuance and access to public services, with plans to eventually replace citizenship certificates."In the long run, we will have a single identity card replacing the citizenship certificate.It is verified, authentic and technology-friendly," Tiwari said."That is why we have requested India to allow the use of the National Identity Card while travelling by both air and land routes," he added.According to senior immigration officials quoted by, an Indian Embassy delegation met officials from Nepal's Department of Immigration earlier this week to discuss the proposalThe delegation was reportedly "positive" about the initiative and informed Nepalese officials that the request had been forwarded to authorities in New Delhi for consideration."We have already forwarded the proposal to the Indian side through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs," said Ram Chandra Tiwari, Director General of the Department of Immigration.Officials from Nepal's Home Ministry also said that discussions have included creating formal mechanisms to record cross-border travel data and better manage movement between the two neighbouring countries.

World.title: Kargil lessons shaped Operation Sindoor: Former army chief General VP Malik
World.content:
CHANDIGARH: Twenty-seven years after leading the Army during the 1999

, former Army chief General VP Malik (retd) said the conflict's hard lessons - from equipment shortages and intelligence gaps to the need for self-reliance - transformed India's military capabilities, enabling the precision strikes on Pakistani airfields during last year's

without crossing the border.

"The biggest operational lessons were the need to strengthen intelligence, surveillance and achieve 'atmanirbharta (self-reliance)' in military hardware," Gen Malik told TOI in an interview ahead of the 27th anniversary of

. Those lessons, he said, shaped India's military preparedness over the next two decades.

Citing Operation Sindoor, he pointed to the armed forces' growing reliance on short- and long-range drones for surveillance and precision strikes, along with advanced rockets and missiles.

"We did not have to enter Pakistani territory when we struck airfields and radar stations, causing major havoc," he said, contrasting it with Kargil.

He said indigenous and imported platforms, including BrahMos, Akash and the S-400, were now tested in real-world conditions. Combined with an integrated tri-services command under Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), they have significantly strengthened India's defence capability.





Yet, Gen Malik stressed that technology alone could not win wars. "The man behind the gun is always more important. We must look after them," he said.

Recalling his visits to the frontlines in Jammu & Kashmir, Gen Malik said the soldiers themselves became a source of strength. "...every six days, I would visit... While morale in Delhi was sometimes anxious or uncertain, not a single soldier ever told me the task was difficult.

Every visit replenished my own morale."

Reflecting on the reforms that followed the war, Gen Malik said govt constituted Kargil Review Committee, whose key recommendations included creating the CDS position to improve tri-service integration and civil-military coordination. He added that commemorating Vijay Diwas was not only about paying homage to the martyrs but also ensuring the lessons of the conflict continued to guide armed forces.

Gen Malik said the valour displayed remained an inspiration for future generations. While the victory involved strategic planning at the highest level, he insisted the credit belonged to the young officers and soldiers who fought at unforgiving heights. "We must also remember the supporting arms and services. People often forget them but military functions like an orchestra during war. When every arm works in harmony, we achieve victory.

"

Invoking Bhagavad Gita, he said, "The true test of any plan lies in its execution. As written in the Gita: 'Action is superior to knowledge'."

World.title: Students protest: Gen Z forces DP Change
World.content:
Protesters at Jantar Mantar celebrate news of Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation

Why BJP chose to cut its losses

NEW DELHI: Dharmendra Pradhan, who earned his early spurs by leading a protest against a Class 12 question paper leak in Odisha in 1996 as an ABVP national secretary, was forced to resign Saturday as Union education minister, in the face of unrelenting protests fuelled by studentsâ anger over NEET-UG paper leak.Govt conceded to the key demand of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and the opposition as Pradhan sent his resignation to PM Modi, in an unprecedented ouster of a cabinet minister of his govt for over 12 years, marking a political setback to BJP and a rare boost for its rivals.Five-time Karnataka MP and Union minister Pralhad Joshi, who holds several other portfolios, has been given additional charge of education.Jubilant CJP members, led by its founder Abhijeet Dipke, called off their agitation after a third round of talks with Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh.âDemocracy wins,â CJP said on X.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das announced withdrawal of protests with immediate effect at a news conference, where both ministers wore a resigned look. Govt has also agreed to provide âhonourableâ compensation to families of NEET candidates who died by suicide and withdraw FIRs against protesting students in Delhi and other BJP-governed states, he added.The two sides will again meet after four weeks to work on broader reforms in the exam system, CJP said.In a two-page statement, Pradhan said he has quit so that âanti-national forces do not take advantage of the situationâ at Jantar Mantar and across the countryâ. It is not a matter of personal prestige, he said.His statement was addressed to âmy young friendsâ, a nod to Gen Z, who have been the face of CJP-led protests, and left the all-powerful BJP searching for answers to their unconventional onslaught. A govt functionary said largescale participation of youth gave the campaign, which BJP initially saw as sponsored by AAP and Left-aligned groups, an emotive undercurrent, leaving them little choice but to retreat as the protest grew.For a party which rarely makes any concession to rivals on their terms and exudes an air of bold strength rooted in popular endorsement in polls, BJPâs decision to bow to the student protest also reflects the pragmatism it has shown when confronted with street agitation â better to cut losses than let the pain fester into a more serious challenge.In Nov 2021, Modi had announced withdrawal of farm laws in the face of over a yearlong protest by farmers, which was largely confined to Punjab and parts of Haryana and western UP but had remained stubborn. The PM, too, had ascribed the decision to national interest, which observers thought was a reference to the sensitivity of Punjab as a border state.Pradhanâs mention of the stir at Jantar Mantar but no acknowledgement of Congressled oppositionâs protest, which has kept Parliamentâs monsoon session deadlocked, is seemingly aimed at denying any credit to BJPâs political rivals while conceding to CJP, which is not really an electoral threat.With Rahul Gandhi, too, stepping up his agitationâ his surprise demonstration outside Modiâs residence on July 21 was a highlight â so as not to allow CJP, seen closer to its âsecularâ rival AAP, hog the limelight, Congress is bound to lay claim to the credit. However, BJP has more often than not seen off its challenge without much political damage.There was sympathy in the ranks for Pradhan who, as petroleum minister, rolled out the vote-spinner Ujjwala scheme and stayed engaged with the cadre. He had a stream of visitors â home minister Amit Shah and finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman included.âWe had to swallow the bitter pill because there was a real risk of violence breaking out. Any loss of lives would have been blamed on us. Moreover, it was about students and their families,â said a senior minister.The sense of resignation was accompanied by surprise as to why the leadership did not take measures it subsequently took to tackle the discontent: strengthening of the law against paper leaks, eviction of key bureaucrats from education ministry, drastic action against NTA officials, and Pradhanâs resignation.In his statement, Pradhan, 57, who took charge of education ministry in July 2021, emphasised his decades-long commitment to students and education, and said he took responsibility of the fallout of the NEET-UG paper leak from the very first day.The re-exam result was declared on time, and many poor meritorious students made the cut, he said, while blaming those in responsible positions, alikely swipe at Rahul and other key opposition figures, for trying to mislead students.The BJP brass expressed its full backing for Pradhan, a deft politician who has been the choice of Modi and Shah in helming numerous state elections, as he stepped down. BJP president Nitin Nabin credited him for key reforms and lauded him for prioritising larger interests, in keeping with âthe highest standards of integrity and selfless service in public lifeâ.

World.title: Tamil Nadu government extends Seventh State Finance Commission’s tenure till December 31
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government has extended the tenure of the Seventh State Finance Commission by four months, until December 31, 2026. The Commission’s tenure was originally scheduled to expire on August 31, 2026.

The Seventh State Finance Commission, chaired by retired IAS officer K. Allaudin, was constituted in May 2025 to study the financial position of village panchayats, panchayat union councils, district panchayats, town panchayats, municipalities and municipal corporations, and make appropriate recommendations on the distribution of funds to be provided by the State government.

The Commission was originally required to submit its report by August 31, 2026, covering the five-year period commencing from April 1, 2027. Following the extension, the Commission may now submit its report by December 31, 2026.

World.title: Visakhapatnam completes SIR digitisation of 20.23 lakh electors; draft roll on July 31
World.content:
The Visakhapatnam district administration has completed the digitisation of enumeration forms of all 20,23,009 electors as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR)-2026, and the draft electoral roll will be published on July 31, District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore has said.

In a statement, the Collector said the distribution, collection and digitisation of enumeration forms had been completed for voters across 1,980 polling stations in the district. The database had been updated after incorporating details of voters who had submitted enumeration forms, as well as those categorised as absent, shifted, deceased or duplicate (ASDD). Officials also carried out a fresh field verification of voters who had initially been placed in the ASDD category after enumeration forms were not received by July 14, improving the quality of the electoral database.

Mr. Kishore said the number of “no mapping” cases had come down from 1,80,725 to 27,555, or 1.36% of the electorate, and logical discrepancies from 5,48,723 to 2,02,323, or about 10% of voters. The number of notices to be issued after publication of the draft roll had fallen from 7,29,448 to 2,29,878.

The Collector said the names of 2,40,209 voters in the ASDD category would not be included in the draft electoral roll. Electors have been advised to check their names and particulars after the draft roll is published. Claims for inclusion may be submitted through Form 6, and requests for corrections through Form 8, between July 31 and August 30. The final electoral roll will be published on October 3, 2026, after the disposal of claims and objections, he said. Voters may contact the Election Commission helpline at 1950 or 0891-2590100, or approach constituency and district-level help desks.

World.title: 17 teaching hospitals in Andhra Pradesh lack sewage treatment plants; ₹83 crore plan drawn up
World.content:
Biomedical waste management and sewage treatment should be carried out in all government hospitals as per the regulations, said Andhra Pradesh Minister for Health, Medical and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav.

In a review meeting with health officials on Saturday (July 25, 2026), the Minister expressed displeasure over the poor implementation of the regulations at government hospitals. He asked the officials to ensure that biomedical waste was collected and disposed of properly.

Officials told the Minister that 400 grams of biomedical waste is generated a day from a single hospital bed. The Government General Hospitals in the State produce 13 lakh kg of biomedical waste, according to a release issued by the Health Department.

The Minister said the waste generated at the hospitals should be segregated and disposed of in accordance with the guidelines. Every hospital should comply with these rules in letter and spirit. The entire process should be monitored through CCTV cameras, and barcode tracking should be introduced to ensure accountability, he said.

The Minister also expressed displeasure over the poor management of wastewater in hospitals. He said that among secondary hospitals, only the Nuzvid and Banaganapalle area hospitals have Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs). Of the 40 teaching and super-speciality hospitals, 17 do not have STPs, he said.

He asked the officials to ensure that all 17 teaching hospitals, 54 area hospitals and nine district hospitals have STPs within 10 months. Installing the plants is estimated to cost ₹83 crore.

The Minister said the unnecessary crowding at government hospitals should be reduced. In intensive care units and hospital wards, visitors will be allowed only during designated hours, he said.

World.title: No talks with Pakistan except on PoK: Rajnath Singh on Kargil Vijay Diwas
World.content:
On the account of the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas, Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday (July 26, 2026) asserted that India can respond to any misadventure by Pakistan in a manner “beyond their imagination”. He said there will be no talks with Pakistan other than on Pakistan-occupied-Kashmir (PoK), which is a “part of India illegally occupied” by it.

Addressing military personnel and veteran in Dras, Mr. Singh said ‘Operation Sindoor’ clearly demonstrated what the fate of those who attempt to threaten India with terrorism will be. Earlier, he laid a wreath at the Kargil War Memorial, paying homage to the war heroes who laid their lives during the 1999 ‘Operation Vijay’. He was joined by Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth and senior military officers in Dras.

Mr. Singh, speaking at the memorial, also slammed Pakistan for making terrorism a “part of its state policy”.

Mr. Singh described India’s victory in the Kargil war in 1999 as “a diamond studded in the crown of Bharat Mata”.

The Defence Minister recalled the Operation Sindoor conducted in May 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22, 2025.

Under Operation Sindoor, the Indian armed forces dealt a severe blow to the backers and supporters of terrorism, he said. “Operation Sindoor made it clear what the fate will be of those who attempt to threaten India with terrorism,” Mr. Singh said.

He asserted that India and its armed forces have the capacity to respond to any misadventure by Pakistan in a manner “beyond their imagination”. “Any evil step towards the sovereignty and integrity of India will meet with the same fate,” the Defence Minister said.

At a time when India is designing ships, Pakistan is busy engaging in terror design, he said. “While we are finding new ways of innovation, Pakistan is seeking new ways of infiltration,” he added.

Kargil Vijay Diwas commemorates the culmination of Operation Vijay, the name given to India's military operation to reclaim the heights of Kargil after Pakistan’s infiltration, which culminated on this day in 1999.

With PTI inputs

World.title: Visakhapatnam to host AP Chambers Business Expo from September 11
World.content:
District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore has said the development of all sectors should remain the focus of Visakhapatnam’s growth, and said small and medium enterprises should be encouraged to strengthen the region’s economy.

At a meeting organised by the Andhra Pradesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry Federation (AP Chambers) at a hotel on Old Jail Road on Saturday (July 25, 2026), he released the brochure for the AP Chambers Business Expo scheduled from September 11 to 13.

The Collector said the expo, being organised in Visakhapatnam for the first time with a focus on the development of micro, small and medium enterprises, was a commendable effort. He described the city as a hub of opportunities and employment and urged all stakeholders to contribute to its development.

Mr. Kishore said Andhra Pradesh was attracting 25% of the investments coming into the country, and that a significant share was flowing to the erstwhile Visakhapatnam district. He added that the government was giving special attention to the Visakhapatnam Economic Region and the Bay City concept. AP Chambers Visakhapatnam Zone chairman P. Sobhan Prakash and State secretary R. Subba Rao also spoke.

World.title: Plea in Madras HC seeks constitution of expert committee over evaluation of Assistant Professor aspirants’ exam papers
World.content:
A public interest litigation (PIL) petition has been filed in the Madras High Court for constituting an independent expert committee to examine the fairness, consistency, transparency and uniformity in evaluation of the answer scripts of 42,064 candidates of the competitive written examination for 2,708 Assistant Professor vacancies in 61 faculties in government arts and science colleges in Tamil Nadu

First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan would be hearing on Monday (July 27, 2026) the PIL petition filed by Karu Nagarajan of ‘We The Leaders’ movement helmed by former BJP leader K. Annamalai. The petitioner had complained of unfairness in evaluation of the descriptive answers given by the candidates on general topics.

He told the court direct recruitment to the post of Assistant Professor had not taken place in the State for quite a few years. Initially, a notification was issued in 2019 for filling up 2,331 vacancies but it was rescinded in 2024 when it was decided to fill up 4,000 vacancies. The 2024 notification too was withdrawn in 2025 when a fresh notification was issued for 2,708 vacancies.

As per a Government Order issued on October 6, 2025, candidates who had applied in 2019 and 2024 were given fee exemption and age relaxation for participating in the fresh recruitment process. The Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB) conducted a written examination which comprised of objective type questions for 150 marks in the relevant subject in paper-I and descriptive type questions on general topics in paper-II.

In paper-II, the candidates were given five questions on topics such as the Indian Economy, Constitution, Modern Indian History, History and Economy of Tamil Nadu, environment and ecology, science and technology and current affairs and were expected to write an essay type answer for any one of the five questions. This single descriptive type answer carried a total of 50 marks.

Mr. Nagarajan claimed results of the examinations declared on June 25, 2026 revealed that a candidate who had scored 107 out of 150 marks in computer science paper-I had ended up scoring just one mark in paper-II. Conversely, a candidate who had scored 54 out of 150 marks in physics paper-I had scored 49 out of 50 marks in the descriptive answer type paper-II on general topics.

“The said pattern has been noticed across several subjects and it materially affects the final merit ranking of candidates giving rise to widespread concerns regarding the transparency, consistency and uniformity of the descriptive evaluation process, thereby warranting independent judicial scrutiny by this honourable court,” the petitioner’s affidavit read.

The petitioner said, the relief sought by him was not related to adjudication of any individual service dispute but was aimed at ensuring procedural fairness in public recruitment.

World.title: Kargil Vijay Diwas: President Murmu, PM Modi lead nation to pay tributes to war heroes on 27th anniversary of ‘Operation Vijay’
World.content:
As the country commemorates the 27th anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas, President Droupadi Mumu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the nation in paying tributes to the soldiers who laid down their lives during ‘Operation Vijay’ in 1999.

On July 26, 1999, the Indian Army announced the successful culmination of the operation, declaring victory over Pakistan in the Kargil war after a nearly three-month-long battle on the icy heights of Kargil in Ladakh.

On Sunday (July 26, 2026), the Army will host a ‘Shradhanjali Samaroh’ – wreath laying ceremony – at the Kargil War Memorial in Ladakh’s Drass to pay homage to the bravehearts of the war. Union Minister Rajnath Singh is expected to address military personnel and veterans during the event to commemorate the anniversary.

Exemplary models of our Army’s glorious traditions: President Murmu on martyrs’ valour

President Droupadi Murmu paid tribute to the valiant warriors who laid down their lives for the protection of the motherland, and said the nation shall forever remain indebted to them.

“On the occasion of Kargil Vijay Diwas, I pay humble tribute to those valiant warriors who laid down their lives for the protection of our motherland,” Murmu said in a post on X in Hindi.

Their unparalleled valour, unwavering resolve, and unparalleled patriotism stand as exemplary models of our Army’s glorious traditions, she said.

“The nation shall forever remain indebted to them. The saga of valour of those heroic warriors will continue to inspire future generations to tread the path of national service and steadfast duty,” the President said.

Brave soldiers will remain source of national pride: PM Modi

PM Narendra Modi said the valour of India's brave soldiers in the face of most formidable conditions will forever remain a source of national pride.

He also said that the nation expresses gratitude to the brave soldiers for their extraordinary courage and commitment towards securing India. "Their valour in the face of the most formidable conditions will forever remain a source of national pride. Their unwavering patriotism and devotion to duty will continue to inspire generations," he said in a post on X.

Indian Army will continue to inspire future generations: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh

“On the occasion of Kargil Vijay Diwas, I pay my deepest respects to all the brave soldiers who laid down their lives in the defense of our motherland. The nation will forever remain grateful and indebted to all those valiant soldiers who demonstrated extraordinary valor on the inaccessible peaks of Kargil in 1999,” said Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in a post on X. Mr. Singh is in Kargil today, where he will addressing soldiers on the occasion of Vijay Diwas.

“The indomitable courage, sacrifice, and unwavering resolve of the Indian Army will continue to inspire future generations with patriotism, dedication to duty, and the spirit of offering everything for the motherland,” he added.

Congress pays tribute to brave soldiers' ‘supreme sacrifice’

Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi paid his tribute to the war heroes by acknowledging their “supreme sacrifice while defending India’s borders” in the 1999 war.

“The nation will forever remain indebted to your courage, valor, and supreme sacrifice,” he wrote in a post on X.

Meanwhile, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharg took to X to “pay homage with reverence to our immortal heroes.”

“Their indomitable courage, unparalleled valor, and unwavering dedication to the nation will forever remain a source of inspiration for us all,” he said in a post in Hindi.

'कारगिल विजय दिवस' पर हमारे वीर सैनिकों, उनके परिवारों और समस्त देशवासियों को बधाई।



कारगिल युद्ध में मातृभूमि की रक्षा करते हुए सर्वोच्च बलिदान देने वाले हमारे अमर वीरों को हम श्रद्धापूर्वक नमन करते हैं।



उनका अदम्य साहस, अद्वितीय पराक्रम और राष्ट्र के प्रति अटूट समर्पण हम सभी… pic.twitter.com/8qznZu578p — Mallikarjun Kharge (@kharge) July 26, 2026

This day is an immortal symbol of the valour, sacrifice and patriotism of our brave soldiers: U.P. CM

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and several senior BJP leaders paid tributes to the indomitable courage and unparalleled valour of soldiers on Kargil Vijay Diwas.

In a post on X, Mr. Adityanath said, “Heartiest greetings to everyone on Kargil Vijay Diwas. This day is an immortal symbol of the valour, sacrifice and patriotism of our brave soldiers.” Paying homage to soldiers, he added, “Salute to all the immortal heroes of the Indian Army who laid down their lives in defence of the motherland. Jai Hind.”

Union Minister of State for Finance and BJP’s Uttar Pradesh president Pankaj Chaudhary said, “On Kargil Vijay Diwas, I pay my heartfelt respects to the immortal heroes who made the supreme sacrifice in defence of the motherland.” Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya said Kargil Vijay Diwas was an occasion to salute the “indomitable courage, unparalleled valour, unwavering resolve and unflinching patriotism” of the Indian armed forces.

Soldiers stood firm to protect the nation’s sovereignty: Andhra CM

Andhra Pradesh Governor S. Abdul Nazeer, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and YSRCP president YS Jagan Mohan Reddy on Sunday paid tribute to the brave soldiers who laid down their lives during the Kargil War, marking Kargil Vijay Diwas.

The Governor said the Indian Army soldiers fought valiantly under extremely harsh conditions to defend the motherland.

“Their indomitable spirit and unwavering resolve continue to inspire the youth with courage, patriotism and a spirit of selfless service,” Mr. Nazeer said in a post on ‘X’.

Similarly, the Chief Minister said Kargil Vijay Diwas is an occasion to pay solemn tribute to the brave soldiers whose extraordinary courage secured India’s victory.

“In the face of formidable terrain and relentless adversity, they stood firm to protect the nation’s sovereignty. Their supreme sacrifice and unmatched heroism continue to inspire generations and remain a timeless symbol of patriotism and national pride,” Mr. Naidu said in a post on ‘X’.

World.title: Assam flood situation improves as water levels recede, 6.5 lakh still affected
World.content:
The flood situation in Assam improved on Sunday (July 26, 2026) as water levels were receding in most of the affected areas, with those places not receiving overnight rainfall, even as over 6.5 lakh people remained hit in six districts and 66 people lost their lives in this year’s deluge, officials said.

An official of the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) said that water levels were receding in most of the flood-hit areas of Upper Assam, especially Charaideo, Sivasagar and Jorhat districts.

“We hope the situation would improve further during the day. This would help us provide relief in a better way,” he added.

According to the authority’s daily flood report issued at midnight, more than 6,54,800 people have been affected in Charaideo, Dibrugarh, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon and Sivasagar districts.

Sivasagar was the worst-hit district with nearly 2.9 lakh people affected, followed by Charaideo (1.9 lakh) and Jorhat (1.3 lakh). The flood situation has improved marginally since Friday (July 24, 2026), when more than 7.05 lakh people were affected across nine districts.

The ASDMA’s midnight bulletin said that four more people lost their lives in the deluge in the last 24 hours, taking the toll in this year’s floods to 66. Three deaths were reported in Sivasagar and one in Charaideo.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (July 25, 2026) offered full support to the Assam government in dealing with the deluge, which has shown signs of improvement as rain has stopped in most parts of the state.

Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal reviewed the relief measures at camps in flood-affected areas and directed officials concerned to ensure uninterrupted access to healthcare, food, drinking water and other essential services.

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the situation has slightly improved and the administration has been able to reach out to almost all the affected areas.

Addressing a press conference after a late-evening Cabinet Meeting, he said that a central team has arrived in the state to assess the damage caused by the flood in Upper Assam.

ASDMA said the administration has been operating 274 relief camps and distribution centres in six districts, taking care of 18,902 displaced people at present.

Multiple agencies such as the Army, NDRF, SDRF, Fire & Emergency Services, police and civil agencies have rescued many people from different parts of Upper Assam, it added.

The authority has distributed 1,668.68 quintals of rice, 286.99 quintals of dal, 83.75 quintals of salt and 7,995.01 litres of mustard oil among the flood victims of the state in the last 24 hours.

At present, 810 villages are under water and 34,970.8 hectares of crop areas have been damaged across Assam, the ASDMA said.

Embankments, roads, bridges and other infrastructure have been damaged by floodwaters in different districts of the state. At present, the Dikhow River at Sivasagar and the Dhansiri at Numaligarh are flowing above the danger level.

World.title: ‘Carefully assess security risks’: MEA’s advisory to vessels operating in Black Sea region
World.content:
With the security situation in and around the Black Sea remaining highly volatile amid the ongoing conflict, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Sunday issued an advisory for Indian nationals employed, or planning to take up employment, on commercial vessels operating in or transiting the region.

The MEA warned that commercial ships passing through Black Sea waters continue to face significant security threats, including missile and drone attacks. It noted that attacks on merchant vessels have increased since April 2026, resulting in the deaths of five Indian nationals.



Advising Indians to carefully evaluate the risks before accepting such assignments, the ministry urged those choosing to work on vessels operating in the conflict zone to exercise utmost caution and follow a series of safety measures.

World.title: This 1971 war hero is trapped by Chandigarh’s red tape
World.content:
Group Captain C.S. Sandhu (retd), a Vir Chakra and Vayu Sena Medal awardee who survived Pakistani gunfire during the 1971 war while piloting helicopters in one of the defining operations of the Bangladesh Liberation War, is now fighting a very different battle. The 88-year-old war hero, suffering from serious health problems, has spent nearly a year struggling with the Chandigarh Administration for permission to install an elevator in his residential building.

Decorated with the Vir Chakra, India’s third-highest wartime gallantry award, Group Captain Sandhu flew 34 missions in a single day during the 1971 war and emerged unscathed despite his Mi-4 helicopter being riddled with more than three dozen bullet holes. Today, after suffering a serious back injury in a fall, he is unable to climb to his fourth-floor flat in Jal Vayu Vihar Society, Sector 44. Despite repeated representations and medical recommendations, he continues to await permission to install a lift.

Doctors have advised Sandhu to avoid climbing stairs and taking painkillers. To reach his home, he must negotiate 56 steps, relying on an orthopaedic belt and a walking stick. He rarely leaves his apartment except when necessary.

Sandhu first applied for permission to install a lift on medical grounds in September 2025, when senior citizens and medical cases in the society were eligible under the existing policy. About five weeks later, the Chandigarh Administration informed him that a new lift policy had come into force and that the housing society would have to submit a fresh online application.

“An attempt through the Smart City portal at the end of October 2025 failed because the master data had not been uploaded. Despite repeated visits to department heads, the online system remained non-functional for over four to five months,” Sandhu said.



The society eventually submitted an offline application in March 2026, citing his medical condition. Sandhu also met the Deputy Commissioner, who assured him the matter would be fast-tracked. Nearly four months later, however, the application remains pending. Officials have since informed him that the proposed lift falls outside the zoning plan and requires special approval.

Sandhu questions why the application was not rejected at the outset if zoning rules were an obstacle. He also points to what he describes as an inconsistency in the regulations. While Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) flats are reportedly permitted to install lifts more freely, including on government land, non-CHB societies face stricter norms. He says the new policy does not clearly specify zoning restrictions for private societies, yet those provisions are being applied in his case.



Calling the prolonged delay “deliberate harassment”, Sandhu said he tried on three occasions in February to meet the UT Administrator during the designated public hearing day but was prevented from doing so by officials. He also sought intervention from the office of the Punjab Governor and UT Administrator, but says he received little encouragement.

“The ADC to the Governor asked me why I was bothering him. I banged the phone down,” he said.

Sandhu’s gallantry record remains one of the most distinguished in the Indian Air Force. During the 1971 operations against Pakistan, then Squadron Leader commanding 110 Helicopter Unit, he led the historic heliborne operation across the Meghna River in East Pakistan on the night of December 7-8.
